segments.text: How are you?
This is your mother speaking.
Do you recognize my voice?
It's 4 o'clock in the afternoon and it's April the 3rd, Wednesday, and it's pouring down rain.
I guess you'll call these April showers.
David has something to tell you.
He's next.
Hi Mike.
Yesterday I broke my arm and I ran into a kid and broke it.
I had to go to the hospital and stayed all night.
Today I got out of the hospital.
I'm expecting to get a duck around now.
And I'm going to name it Sam and be Sam the fourth.
But even the rabbit cage, it tore down my fort.
I'm going to burn it when it gets dry.
It's not windy.
David didn't tell you which arm he broke, Mike.
He broke his left arm again, the same one he broke a year and a half ago.
But this time the brakes were a little farther up, closer to the elbow this time.
And it was what they call a deformed brake.
The one bone was laying on top of the other.
This time it was a little more painful I believe.
They put him to sleep.
They wouldn't put the cats on, but the brake happened about 12.45 yesterday as the bell
rang and they were forming a line to go into school and he and another boy
collided and they would fell down and that's how the broken arm came about. It
was an accident, thank goodness. He wasn't fighting and they called me, they came
notified me at work to come as soon as I could get there and I left immediately
and went over and picked him up, and we were at the hospital by 1 o'clock.
But they wouldn't put the cast on until 5 o'clock last night
because he had eaten lunch, and they didn't want him to get sick.
They just put a temporary cast on
and then left his arm tied up, elevated all night,
and so it wouldn't swell.
And at about 10 o'clock this morning, they put the permanent cast on.
So, as you might have guessed, the drum lessons are postponed indefinitely.
And, uh, knowing him though, he'll probably try to play it before it's over with, before it's too long.
But, uh, there's never a dull moment around here, it seems like, anymore.
We've been playing baseball at school, Mike, and won't be able to play baseball now.
Since I got my broken arm and having a fitness thing at school,
pull-ups and push-ups and stuff won't be in that,
so I'll be doing okay doing pull-ups.
That's kind of hard.
Well, I had nothing else to say.
Here's mine.
Mike, I think Dave was a little microphone shy.
You know, he can do plenty of talking,
but when you get in front of a microphone,
he doesn't know what to say.
So we may take a day or so to record this, but we'll get it done as soon as possible and get it off to you.
We received your letter that you wrote on Saturday in two days, and that was very fast traveling for your mail.
looks like you're going to start getting it
a little quicker now
unless they decide to put you someplace
where you can't get that
helicopter on that ship
I hope you
enjoyed your tour of Tokyo
and saw many things
and we
really think you did a
wise thing in buying those radios
and sound cabinets
they're really nice and
I know you're going to enjoy
them for many years. It would be nice if we could have you get the same things, but I
don't know where we would put them at. I really had a busy evening last night, I'll tell you.
I didn't get away from the hospital until around 7 o'clock, and I had to go to the general
home and then go to a Marine Auxiliary meeting. And I wouldn't have went to that meeting if it
hadn't been for the fact they were showing slides from Vietnam. One of the women had them,
her boy, Millie Aschfeld, or so it was, and she offered to show the slides that he'd taken over
there. And they were well worthwhile to see. We were expecting some slides and a tape from Bill
any day. Georgia May has them and
wasn't able to find a tape recorder to play the tape on and I don't know whether she
found a projector or not to see the slides but
we're patiently waiting for her to get them off there. She was supposed to
mail them Saturday and I would think
that they would get here by the weekend and
I know we're going to enjoy them and
We're looking forward to you sending supplies too when you can.
And I'll bet you took a lot of nice pictures there in Tokyo.
I was really surprised you got that box this soon.
I only had mailed it on a Monday before you got it on Saturday.
And I hadn't really wanted you to get it until the end of this week, close to the Easter.
Easter but I hope you enjoyed the box and I hope you didn't think that I was
trying to embarrass you about that Easter Bunny it was just done as a joke
and if you'll notice the thing was made in Japan and it's traveled its way back
to Japan by now you probably have heard the bill and know that Easter's moved and I probably wrote to you
I can't remember sometimes what I wrote to you boys.
And his letters sound like he's got it made over there.
I never realized or ever thought that it could be so easy, which I'm very glad of it.
I wouldn't want to do it any other way.
But he said he sleeps 10 to 12 hours a day or night.
And doesn't really do much of anything.
the printing of the china seed and uh actually duper awkward about all it sounds like he's doing
i haven't been able to find out from him why they're moving down there maybe they don't know
why either but at any rate he's away from the bank and uh 20 miles a place called boyan h-o-i-a-n
And I wouldn't be surprised the next letter we get that he'll be moved again
because I think they're getting ready to start something.
It doesn't sound like they're going to stand still for too long.
Mike, about that newspaper subscription, don't worry about getting any additional papers.
I think they made a mistake somewhere and I'm not going to worry about it.
I got a notice that the subscription was running out and it would run out the 18th of April.
The notice that I had got when I first took out the subscription was it was supposed to run out the 18th of March.
So don't worry about it.
I am not going to renew it and it's their mistake.
So go ahead and enjoy them as long as they come.
And in the meantime, I will try to cut out any clippings that I think that will interest you,
especially those veterans or those servicemen news that you asked for.
And I'll also cut out the Dear Son article in the paper each Tuesday night.
That will give you a pretty good summary of what's been happening in this town.
and it hasn't changed too much.
The same old situation that goes on.
The school board's got everybody up in arms
and they've cut a lot of things out at schools
because of referendum pass
and it's making a lot of people thoroughly disgusted,
but that's the way it goes and it's nothing new really.
I guess if I was on the school board,
I probably wouldn't do any better job than what they're doing.
Well, Mike, I guess it's about time that I talk to you a little bit.
I wasn't here when Mother and David had been talking to you,
but it's now 7-15, the 3rd of April,
and I went to Springfield today.
It rained all day over there, and it's been raining real hard here this evening.
I had to go out to the hospital and sign some papers for David,
and I come home, and I just got done helping him with his homework a little bit.
He's getting along pretty good with it.
On the way home from Springfield, I was listening to the ballgame.
The Cubs and the Giants were playing at Phoenix.
and of course as usually
let the Giants tie it up in the bottom of the 8th
and then the Cubs scored 4 runs in the top of the 9th
and then they let the Giants tie them up
and it was an 11th inning when I got home
so I don't know how the game come out
but it looks like maybe they're going to
give us those thrills like they usually give us
all year long
But I don't know, they might make it this year,
but they're going to have to get some pitching,
which is, as of now, they don't seem to have it.
As for Holstman, he hasn't done a thing all year since he's been back with them.
I suppose that since he didn't lose any last year,
his head swelled up a little bit,
and he decided that he don't have to work quite as hard as the rest of them.
but he hasn't done a bit of good so far this year.
I don't suppose that you've heard anything down there yet about spring training,
but I expect when the season gets started,
you'll be able to pick up the, I think they have a game of the day
on that Armed Forces Network, so probably you'll hear some ball games
whether you're down around Japan and down in the South Pacific
or wherever you might be going from Japan.
I don't think you've told us where you're figuring,
if you know where you're going when you leave Japan or not.
I do hope you get to go to Australia
and swing down through that part of the world
and get to see a lot of things that you've probably read about
and heard about, but I don't believe there's anything like seeing them for yourself.
I've seen Dr. Hoffman at the stamp club the other night,
and he was asking about you and Bill, how you're getting along.
I told him we'd heard from you Monday night before I went to the stamp meeting
that you've been in Japan since Thursday.
And how fast the letter got here, which I thought was exceptionally fast,
Looks like that mail service is pretty good direct out of Japan.
However, I suppose there at that airport there in Japan, planes probably leave there about
like they do out of O'Hare Field in Chicago.
But it's still a pretty fast time, two days to make it that far and to get in the box
up at the post office.
It went many a mile in that length of time.
I would tell you if I was raining, hard to see any of the lights.
We've been flashing pretty bad lights.
It's been blinking on and off.
So I suppose before the night show, we'll be knocked out of lights for a couple hours.
But it don't make much difference.
I think David's going to be ready to hit the sack a little early
because I don't think he did much sleeping at the hospital last night.
He said he was only awake once, but that makes a pretty long night in that hospital.
I guess you've been hearing from Bill pretty regularly, or at least whenever he gets right,
it sounds like he's kind of living it up a little bit down there where he is now.
That Boucher boy was buried here today.
It's pretty rainy and bad.
that Bill get walling around down there in that China Sea.
He loved it.
He just decided to stay there with those gooks.
That cabinet, that plan you sent home for that cabinet that time,
it looks like it's a pretty good layout.
However, I think when you get home or when you get your stuff gathered up,
I would have to take some more detailed measurements off of everything you got there
because those sizes that you give, I'm assuming that that's the size of the various parts that you intended to put in it.
But, you know, you've got to have a clearance around most of that stuff
or you can't get it out once you get it in there or vice versa.
but I assume that you've got a place on the ship to take care of this stuff.
If you haven't, well, I suppose you'll be sent home,
but when you get home, we'll get something figured out.
We'll get a nice cabinet built up that'll hold all your stuff for you,
and it'll last you for a long time.
it shouldn't be too much of a chore to make you a nice cabinet for all your stuff.
I suppose by the time you get this, it'll be old news,
but the news come out today at about 11 o'clock this morning on the radio
where it looks like they're going to start some peace talks with Hanoi
on this Vietnam situation.
So maybe with the election coming up and everything involved, this thing might get settled down before very long.
At least I hope so.
It seems like the war that's down there, if you can call that a war, might get squared away by the politicians.
You can't tell with all the political aspects involved just what is going on.
But the president, I feel that he's got something up his sleeve
when he decided that he wasn't going to run again.
It's kind of hard to believe a Texan backing out from the glory that the job gives.
I know that it's no doubt a job with an awful lot of pressure involved on it,
but by the same token, he wanted it and he got it,
and I think he's also helped get us into this situation,
maybe not personally, but through political commitments
and so forth that he or the ones before him
might have made agreements or treaties
or some other thing that got us involved,
but I'm satisfied we're involved only in a defensive war
and that ceases to be a war when you're only on the defense.
If you're going to ever win anything,
you've got to be on the offense sometimes.
Although they say one of the best defenses is a good offense,
or we don't know about that.
I don't feel that we've ever been turned loose to get on the offense
offense due to the fact that when you're in that type of country or that type of jungle and terrain
and you're continually on the defense and with no more people,
when you talk about 500,000 people, that is a lot of people.
However, that's a lot of brush down there, and 500,000 Americans hardly makes a dent in it
when you figure that probably only one out of every four is a fighting man,
that cuts it down to 125,000 the way I look at it.
That would probably do the fighting, and that's not very many people
when you're trying to move in that type of an operation.
looks to me like
the bombing
I believe if I was calling the shots
I believe I'd have hit them a little harder with the bombs
but then of course as you know I'm not calling the shots
and maybe it's
maybe it's best they don't drop
one of the big apples over there
but I really don't believe as far as
the average American is concerned
that the country means anything to us,
except that there's probably something there
that somebody needs or wants or has to protect,
and I imagine that this is no different than any other war.
That's usually what we're after,
is to fight to protect somebody's big interest in these things,
and no doubt there, there's something
that has to be looked after that belongs
that either our own people or some of our friends
that we've got to keep the communists from taking over.
Well, I had to leave for a while.
I had the guy come to pick up a stamp album,
and of course I had to help David finish his homework,
and I just got him bedded down, so it's 9.15 now,
so maybe I can get a few more words on here to you.
I don't know whether you was getting the paper, whether you was reading anything about it or not,
but the farmers had an awful time last fall getting the corn picked and the crops out.
I was over by Champaign the other day.
I noticed one field that they were just starting to pick the field of corn the other day,
and I've seen quite a few of these crops raised, and this is the first time I've ever seen them picking.
corn when it's just at the end of March.
But of course they have to get it out of the field
so they can go ahead and plow and get planted again.
Of course these farmers, you know, they gripe anyway,
but I think this year they've really got something to gripe about.
They didn't get much for the corn that they did get out,
and it cost them, I think,
a considerable amount of money to get their corn picked
because I seen sometimes when I was going either to Champaign or to Springfield,
I seen them out in the field pulling the corn picker with some of them old-time pickers.
They'd have two tractors pulling the thing to get it out of the mud and get it through the fields,
and they really had a rough go of it.
But, of course, I suppose this year now that they'll come up with some more than 175 bushel acre of corn,
so I guess they can make it.
However, I have noticed in the paper this year probably there's more farm sales,
more farmers getting out of the farming business this time of year than there has been before.
I just looked outside to see if it was still raining.
and of course the rain has stopped now.
I think it's stopped temporarily only.
The south drive is full of water,
and boy, that grass in the front yard has really turned green.
It's starting to look like spring anyway.
Of course, we'll all be glad for spring to really get here.
It's been not too rough a winter.
Weather-wise, we have had some pretty cold weather, some snow,
but we haven't had too much snow like we have in the past.
But it's been bad.
We've had actually bad weather since back in October.
I think we started getting rain, and it's been kind of miserable ever since.

1968-04-03.text: How are you? This is your mother speaking. Do you recognize my voice? It's 4 o'clock in the afternoon and it's April the 3rd, Wednesday, and it's pouring down rain. I guess you'll call these April showers. David has something to tell you. He's next. Hi Mike. Yesterday I broke my arm and I ran into a kid and broke it. I had to go to the hospital and stayed all night. Today I got out of the hospital. I'm expecting to get a duck around now. And I'm going to name it Sam and be Sam the fourth. But even the rabbit cage, it tore down my fort. I'm going to burn it when it gets dry. It's not windy. David didn't tell you which arm he broke, Mike. He broke his left arm again, the same one he broke a year and a half ago. But this time the brakes were a little farther up, closer to the elbow this time. And it was what they call a deformed brake. The one bone was laying on top of the other. This time it was a little more painful I believe. They put him to sleep. They wouldn't put the cats on, but the brake happened about 12.45 yesterday as the bell rang and they were forming a line to go into school and he and another boy collided and they would fell down and that's how the broken arm came about. It was an accident, thank goodness. He wasn't fighting and they called me, they came notified me at work to come as soon as I could get there and I left immediately and went over and picked him up, and we were at the hospital by 1 o'clock. But they wouldn't put the cast on until 5 o'clock last night because he had eaten lunch, and they didn't want him to get sick. They just put a temporary cast on and then left his arm tied up, elevated all night, and so it wouldn't swell. And at about 10 o'clock this morning, they put the permanent cast on. So, as you might have guessed, the drum lessons are postponed indefinitely. And, uh, knowing him though, he'll probably try to play it before it's over with, before it's too long. But, uh, there's never a dull moment around here, it seems like, anymore. We've been playing baseball at school, Mike, and won't be able to play baseball now. Since I got my broken arm and having a fitness thing at school, pull-ups and push-ups and stuff won't be in that, so I'll be doing okay doing pull-ups. That's kind of hard. Well, I had nothing else to say. Here's mine. Mike, I think Dave was a little microphone shy. You know, he can do plenty of talking, but when you get in front of a microphone, he doesn't know what to say. So we may take a day or so to record this, but we'll get it done as soon as possible and get it off to you. We received your letter that you wrote on Saturday in two days, and that was very fast traveling for your mail. looks like you're going to start getting it a little quicker now unless they decide to put you someplace where you can't get that helicopter on that ship I hope you enjoyed your tour of Tokyo and saw many things and we really think you did a wise thing in buying those radios and sound cabinets they're really nice and I know you're going to enjoy them for many years. It would be nice if we could have you get the same things, but I don't know where we would put them at. I really had a busy evening last night, I'll tell you. I didn't get away from the hospital until around 7 o'clock, and I had to go to the general home and then go to a Marine Auxiliary meeting. And I wouldn't have went to that meeting if it hadn't been for the fact they were showing slides from Vietnam. One of the women had them, her boy, Millie Aschfeld, or so it was, and she offered to show the slides that he'd taken over there. And they were well worthwhile to see. We were expecting some slides and a tape from Bill any day. Georgia May has them and wasn't able to find a tape recorder to play the tape on and I don't know whether she found a projector or not to see the slides but we're patiently waiting for her to get them off there. She was supposed to mail them Saturday and I would think that they would get here by the weekend and I know we're going to enjoy them and We're looking forward to you sending supplies too when you can. And I'll bet you took a lot of nice pictures there in Tokyo. I was really surprised you got that box this soon. I only had mailed it on a Monday before you got it on Saturday. And I hadn't really wanted you to get it until the end of this week, close to the Easter. Easter but I hope you enjoyed the box and I hope you didn't think that I was trying to embarrass you about that Easter Bunny it was just done as a joke and if you'll notice the thing was made in Japan and it's traveled its way back to Japan by now you probably have heard the bill and know that Easter's moved and I probably wrote to you I can't remember sometimes what I wrote to you boys. And his letters sound like he's got it made over there. I never realized or ever thought that it could be so easy, which I'm very glad of it. I wouldn't want to do it any other way. But he said he sleeps 10 to 12 hours a day or night. And doesn't really do much of anything. the printing of the china seed and uh actually duper awkward about all it sounds like he's doing i haven't been able to find out from him why they're moving down there maybe they don't know why either but at any rate he's away from the bank and uh 20 miles a place called boyan h-o-i-a-n And I wouldn't be surprised the next letter we get that he'll be moved again because I think they're getting ready to start something. It doesn't sound like they're going to stand still for too long. Mike, about that newspaper subscription, don't worry about getting any additional papers. I think they made a mistake somewhere and I'm not going to worry about it. I got a notice that the subscription was running out and it would run out the 18th of April. The notice that I had got when I first took out the subscription was it was supposed to run out the 18th of March. So don't worry about it. I am not going to renew it and it's their mistake. So go ahead and enjoy them as long as they come. And in the meantime, I will try to cut out any clippings that I think that will interest you, especially those veterans or those servicemen news that you asked for. And I'll also cut out the Dear Son article in the paper each Tuesday night. That will give you a pretty good summary of what's been happening in this town. and it hasn't changed too much. The same old situation that goes on. The school board's got everybody up in arms and they've cut a lot of things out at schools because of referendum pass and it's making a lot of people thoroughly disgusted, but that's the way it goes and it's nothing new really. I guess if I was on the school board, I probably wouldn't do any better job than what they're doing. Well, Mike, I guess it's about time that I talk to you a little bit. I wasn't here when Mother and David had been talking to you, but it's now 7-15, the 3rd of April, and I went to Springfield today. It rained all day over there, and it's been raining real hard here this evening. I had to go out to the hospital and sign some papers for David, and I come home, and I just got done helping him with his homework a little bit. He's getting along pretty good with it. On the way home from Springfield, I was listening to the ballgame. The Cubs and the Giants were playing at Phoenix. and of course as usually let the Giants tie it up in the bottom of the 8th and then the Cubs scored 4 runs in the top of the 9th and then they let the Giants tie them up and it was an 11th inning when I got home so I don't know how the game come out but it looks like maybe they're going to give us those thrills like they usually give us all year long But I don't know, they might make it this year, but they're going to have to get some pitching, which is, as of now, they don't seem to have it. As for Holstman, he hasn't done a thing all year since he's been back with them. I suppose that since he didn't lose any last year, his head swelled up a little bit, and he decided that he don't have to work quite as hard as the rest of them. but he hasn't done a bit of good so far this year. I don't suppose that you've heard anything down there yet about spring training, but I expect when the season gets started, you'll be able to pick up the, I think they have a game of the day on that Armed Forces Network, so probably you'll hear some ball games whether you're down around Japan and down in the South Pacific or wherever you might be going from Japan. I don't think you've told us where you're figuring, if you know where you're going when you leave Japan or not. I do hope you get to go to Australia and swing down through that part of the world and get to see a lot of things that you've probably read about and heard about, but I don't believe there's anything like seeing them for yourself. I've seen Dr. Hoffman at the stamp club the other night, and he was asking about you and Bill, how you're getting along. I told him we'd heard from you Monday night before I went to the stamp meeting that you've been in Japan since Thursday. And how fast the letter got here, which I thought was exceptionally fast, Looks like that mail service is pretty good direct out of Japan. However, I suppose there at that airport there in Japan, planes probably leave there about like they do out of O'Hare Field in Chicago. But it's still a pretty fast time, two days to make it that far and to get in the box up at the post office. It went many a mile in that length of time. I would tell you if I was raining, hard to see any of the lights. We've been flashing pretty bad lights. It's been blinking on and off. So I suppose before the night show, we'll be knocked out of lights for a couple hours. But it don't make much difference. I think David's going to be ready to hit the sack a little early because I don't think he did much sleeping at the hospital last night. He said he was only awake once, but that makes a pretty long night in that hospital. I guess you've been hearing from Bill pretty regularly, or at least whenever he gets right, it sounds like he's kind of living it up a little bit down there where he is now. That Boucher boy was buried here today. It's pretty rainy and bad. that Bill get walling around down there in that China Sea. He loved it. He just decided to stay there with those gooks. That cabinet, that plan you sent home for that cabinet that time, it looks like it's a pretty good layout. However, I think when you get home or when you get your stuff gathered up, I would have to take some more detailed measurements off of everything you got there because those sizes that you give, I'm assuming that that's the size of the various parts that you intended to put in it. But, you know, you've got to have a clearance around most of that stuff or you can't get it out once you get it in there or vice versa. but I assume that you've got a place on the ship to take care of this stuff. If you haven't, well, I suppose you'll be sent home, but when you get home, we'll get something figured out. We'll get a nice cabinet built up that'll hold all your stuff for you, and it'll last you for a long time. it shouldn't be too much of a chore to make you a nice cabinet for all your stuff. I suppose by the time you get this, it'll be old news, but the news come out today at about 11 o'clock this morning on the radio where it looks like they're going to start some peace talks with Hanoi on this Vietnam situation. So maybe with the election coming up and everything involved, this thing might get settled down before very long. At least I hope so. It seems like the war that's down there, if you can call that a war, might get squared away by the politicians. You can't tell with all the political aspects involved just what is going on. But the president, I feel that he's got something up his sleeve when he decided that he wasn't going to run again. It's kind of hard to believe a Texan backing out from the glory that the job gives. I know that it's no doubt a job with an awful lot of pressure involved on it, but by the same token, he wanted it and he got it, and I think he's also helped get us into this situation, maybe not personally, but through political commitments and so forth that he or the ones before him might have made agreements or treaties or some other thing that got us involved, but I'm satisfied we're involved only in a defensive war and that ceases to be a war when you're only on the defense. If you're going to ever win anything, you've got to be on the offense sometimes. Although they say one of the best defenses is a good offense, or we don't know about that. I don't feel that we've ever been turned loose to get on the offense offense due to the fact that when you're in that type of country or that type of jungle and terrain and you're continually on the defense and with no more people, when you talk about 500,000 people, that is a lot of people. However, that's a lot of brush down there, and 500,000 Americans hardly makes a dent in it when you figure that probably only one out of every four is a fighting man, that cuts it down to 125,000 the way I look at it. That would probably do the fighting, and that's not very many people when you're trying to move in that type of an operation. looks to me like the bombing I believe if I was calling the shots I believe I'd have hit them a little harder with the bombs but then of course as you know I'm not calling the shots and maybe it's maybe it's best they don't drop one of the big apples over there but I really don't believe as far as the average American is concerned that the country means anything to us, except that there's probably something there that somebody needs or wants or has to protect, and I imagine that this is no different than any other war. That's usually what we're after, is to fight to protect somebody's big interest in these things, and no doubt there, there's something that has to be looked after that belongs that either our own people or some of our friends that we've got to keep the communists from taking over. Well, I had to leave for a while. I had the guy come to pick up a stamp album, and of course I had to help David finish his homework, and I just got him bedded down, so it's 9.15 now, so maybe I can get a few more words on here to you. I don't know whether you was getting the paper, whether you was reading anything about it or not, but the farmers had an awful time last fall getting the corn picked and the crops out. I was over by Champaign the other day. I noticed one field that they were just starting to pick the field of corn the other day, and I've seen quite a few of these crops raised, and this is the first time I've ever seen them picking. corn when it's just at the end of March. But of course they have to get it out of the field so they can go ahead and plow and get planted again. Of course these farmers, you know, they gripe anyway, but I think this year they've really got something to gripe about. They didn't get much for the corn that they did get out, and it cost them, I think, a considerable amount of money to get their corn picked because I seen sometimes when I was going either to Champaign or to Springfield, I seen them out in the field pulling the corn picker with some of them old-time pickers. They'd have two tractors pulling the thing to get it out of the mud and get it through the fields, and they really had a rough go of it. But, of course, I suppose this year now that they'll come up with some more than 175 bushel acre of corn, so I guess they can make it. However, I have noticed in the paper this year probably there's more farm sales, more farmers getting out of the farming business this time of year than there has been before. I just looked outside to see if it was still raining. and of course the rain has stopped now. I think it's stopped temporarily only. The south drive is full of water, and boy, that grass in the front yard has really turned green. It's starting to look like spring anyway. Of course, we'll all be glad for spring to really get here. It's been not too rough a winter. Weather-wise, we have had some pretty cold weather, some snow, but we haven't had too much snow like we have in the past. But it's been bad. We've had actually bad weather since back in October. I think we started getting rain, and it's been kind of miserable ever since. But it'll clear up one of these days, and we'll be looking for some cool weather and some rain and everything else. Of course, you know how it is back in this part of the country about the weather. It don't ever suit, but I'm sure we'll make it through this one again. Police radio has been going pretty good tonight. Nothing spectacular, just about every subway in town has been flooded and cars stalled in it and so forth. Grandma called a while ago to see if we were getting any police calls, and I told her, yeah, what we've been hearing. She said, well, she wasn't getting anything but airplanes tonight. Of course, she finally said that she'd moved the set about three times and probably got it knocked out of whack, so I suppose that she's probably got it back in adjustment now. and catch up with what's going on, if anything. In your last letter, you mentioned about getting something from Japan. Well, I don't know what Mother or David might have told you, but I don't know of anything that I might need or want that they'd have down there that you could pick up. As far as I'm concerned, we don't have everything, but I think we've got about everything we need. this tape recorder I thought would be kind of handy. Of course, maybe I spurs and maybe I didn't, but anyway, we've got it. I know that most of the radios and binoculars and all that stuff that they make down there is real good, and I'm sure that those pieces that you bought will hold up and last quite a while. You know, when I was doing that job out at General Electric, you know, they got an awful lot of their parts that comes with their radios and TVs and those photographs and everything that come from Japan. They get probably a semi-load of stuff in there every week. I suppose it did come from up from New Orleans I don't know where it was shipped from but I suppose that was the port of entry for it from Japan that I suppose they was transistors and etc that they purchased from some manufacturer in Japan so it does seem like their stuff is awful good I suppose also that But price-wise, I imagine that that's got a lot to do with it as far as GE is concerned. You mentioned about being glad to get your feet on that ground again after being on that ship for so long. I was never on a ship quite that long, but I know just exactly what you mean. Because that steel is steel and ain't nothing like that dirt. I don't care whether it's Japan's dirt or whose dirt you're standing in, if it's wrong or pavement, it really makes you feel like you're a human being again. It even seems, at least it seemed to me, like the air even smelled better or tasted better, did something for you when you get off of those ships because that confined living on a ship gets pretty rough, and I know just exactly what it is. Doc Postboy was out here, oh, it's been some time ago, I don't know, it was probably maybe a month or so ago, he was telling us about his tape recorder that he had, he's got one of those mics that you don't have a switch on the mic to start or stop the recording, it'll only record when a sound is, So when the mic is picking up the sound, I never seen one, but I can imagine that that's pretty handy. Now, of course, this and we've got this thumb switch on the microphone that you put it on or off, whichever the case may be. But one that only picks up sound, that records only any sound that would come through it. That sounds like it'd be all right. I assume that they probably got those mics down in Japan, but I also imagine that the instrument, the recording device itself, has to be wired in some way that it'll only work on that. You might, well, of course, I suppose by the time you get this, you'd probably be gone from there, but most of these recording devices are so, what I've seen of them, it seems like every one of them, the mic's got a little different type of connection that goes into the case, so I don't suppose any of them is interchangeable without getting a special adapter or so forth for them. I don't know how much I've put on this tape, but I just happened to look. There's not too much of the tape left, and I think Mother wants to take this up and let Grandma and Grandpa talk to you a little bit on here. So for this time, I'll say goodbye to you. You take care of yourself and keep letting us know how you're getting along. If you need anything, let us know. so you might when you get this recording from us if you want to or you could make a tape from this on your recorder and send it to Bill because Bill I don't believe has got access to this cartridge type recorder that we've got but he can and he can play those regular tapes like you'll be able to make. So I'll say goodbye again, Mike, and take care of yourself. Well, Mike, it's Thursday morning now, and Daddy put quite a bit on this tape that's about to run out. It may run out before I get a chance to say goodbye, so I'll say it now. I'm ready for work, and David's ready for school, and I'm going to take him this morning. He's got a stack of books that I know he can't handle, so I'll take him today. I hope he makes it through the day. His hand is swell quite a bit through the night, and it's getting in trouble, but I think that'll pass in a day or two. I had to go to a meeting with him last night. I'll be glad when those things are through, because it's taken up an awful lot of time, but it may be worthwhile in the long run. So two of the men today gave us some ideas, and I think that we've got quite a bit accomplished right now. I haven't heard from my practical nurse test yet, but I'm keeping my fingers crossed, and I hope to hear just any day now. And believe you me, when I do hear, and if it's a good result, you'll be about the first or second one to know it. And you'll probably hear me all the way to wherever you're at because I'll be really excited about it. There isn't enough tape left on here, so I won't grapple to say anything. So maybe the next time they can put a few words on or else send one themselves, but they have a tape recorder that they can make their own tape now. The other side of this tape is empty, so you can send a message back to us and send it in return mail. We'll be anxious to hear from you, honey.
