learning how to fly. One speckled one, it's kind of stingy and in a blackish kind. He's the one that can fly.
So I put them up on the, well I threw them up so they could fly.
The speckles were landed up on the roof of the garage.
So the kids went up there.
They stayed up there for about an hour.
They'd walk around in the gutter and make all kinds of noise.
by then they never came down so I went up on the roof there and threw them down into the cave.
Didn't hurt them.
Fish for the fish pond now. We got some bug eyes and regular goldfish and some moss and stuff.
Tuesday when I took Sam out to the park before I took him out I had mommy get some film for him.
and then took some pictures of him and put him in the pond then and I had to hold him
because he was scared, he was frightened and everything.
The way I ran and banded him this time was I took some wire that has insulation around
it and twisted it around his leg you know just loosen it up not too loose so he couldn't
get it off but loosen it up and not tight so he could you know he could go a little
more and it wouldn't stop the circulation.
I had a blue one on one side of his leg and a blue one on the other side.
I took and painted his feet black and then put silver stripes down it.
He wore that off.
I applied some bill yesterday and it was real cool.
I had some pictures of his death.
The deaf looks something like a sand, the uh, third, the black and yellow deaf, the
mallard deaf.
I'm just kidding, the mallard is probably something like a Vietnam type deaf, foreign
deaf.
That is the morning the birds get louder and louder in the morning, you know, when they sing around 5.
Yesterday morning they woke me up at 8.30 and they were, you know, loud then.
But my biggest pity, he really liked Sam.
They always sit out in the yard with each other.
But now, kids don't know what to do without Sam around.
Talk to you, I guess.
I'll see you, Mike. I'm gonna have to go out while I'm happy to, but...
Still have nothing else to say, so...
As long as I'm not finishing the tape up, I guess. Bye.
Of course, we were all wrong on some of those lines, but that's what they were.
And we thought that they were pictures of, I don't know, that showed one jeep or one truck that had been burnt.
And it looked like it had hit a mine or something. It had been hit by something.
And we thought it was this truck that his buddy was killed in.
But as it turned out, the tape we got today, it was a different truck. It had been in a mine and it had burnt naturally.
So then there was one Korean in, which, he was killed. So Bill had taken protection from it.
We were wrong about those slides, but we were happy to get the tape.
And the slides that came yesterday, the 13th, were mailed.
They were postmarked with the U.S. Navy postmarked the 10th of June.
So that is really the fastest we've ever gotten anything from there.
And no doubt he made the tape just before he sent the slides out.
And in the tape, he didn't mention anything about being moved.
And I'm just beginning to wonder if maybe they were just threatening him
with the fact that he could be moved if he didn't learn to say yes or no, sir,
instead of coming back with an answer.
And so I hope he doesn't get moved because I think he's real happy where he's at.
He says so on the tape, at the end of this tape that we made.
And they really have a lot of fun and it's one big happy family there.
So as long as it can stay that way for a long time, it shouldn't be too rough.
I'm going to go back on to this conversation that I ended at the end of the tape.
and tell you my opinion, I don't know whether you're interested or not, but I feel like I want to get it off my chest.
But the thing of it is, whenever George May would call Mother about any thing that she'd have to call about,
well, the conversation would always get on to you more.
And so Mother had just talked to Coach May one day, and when she got through, well, I was up there shortly afterwards.
And Mother said, I just hate to talk to that girl on the phone anymore, because she just is so upset about those boys being over there.
And it just breaks my heart for her to be so upset and everything.
everything. And I said, well, I realize that she probably is, and I think we all are concerned
about them, but she can't be that way. She has to get a hold of herself and keep her
chin up to keep those boys from knowing it. And I said, that isn't going to help her any
to be that way. Well, of course, and Mother was crying when she was telling me all this,
you know, and all the tears in me. Well, Mike, actually, I could be in tears all the time
if I let myself. But I feel like that this is to be, and if I can't keep my spirits up,
then what's it going to be like for your kids to get better that is all depressing and everything.
And what I meant by making this a discussion is they are all aga about you boys being old in Vietnam and this and that and so forth.
And everything, every time there's anything in the paper, why there's a great deal of concern from the other end and everything.
everything but when it comes to a mere little thing like a tape being made and sent to you kids
they don't have the time and I think that uh there I know they're not any busier than we are and
how long would it take to say a few words on tape and I know that they're really jarring on the spot
to want to hear any tapes or CA to slide that we get from you kids. So I'm not going to
say anything to them. In fact, this last tape that you sent, I'm not even going to let them
know we got it. I don't feel like that whatever you sent or taped to us, that is to us. And

If you have anything to say on, well, mother quickly takes offense to things that you might say that's the truth about them. And I can't help it if she's that way. And so I just try to ignore it and don't breed any more problems than what there already are.

But I know from past experiences that the words that you're singing have many conversations and things go a lot better. But I wish they would get busy and show a little more of concern in the right way.

and she, I send boxes to you kids frequently, and she is going to send the boxes, every time I turn around, she was there for a while, she was talking about, well, she was going to send the boxes to Bill, and, or send some books or something, and, so, nothing was ever, she never did good,
And so the next day or two, I said, well, I set Bill a box today, or I set Mike a box today.
Oh, you did? I said, yes.
So it's just one of those things, like, just because I'm doing it, she can act like they can't do it either.
Well, I don't care what they do.
As long as I know what I'm doing, and I feel like I'm doing the right thing, that's all that matters to me.
And I think that you can read between the lines.

It just goes well. That was it. I want to tell you that the mall down here at the Talley is opening and the Ben Franklin has opened and the beauty show down there has a thrifty drug. All their supplies in now.
And every time I talk on this thing, my throat starts to choke up, and it isn't.
It's just that I'm talking, I think, more, and in the frame of mind that I'm talking, I am.
So please excuse the throat clearing.
But anyway, there's supposed to be 12 stores when they all get open,
and I don't think some of the spots are rented out yet, but it certainly is a nice place,
and you won't believe your eyes when you see it again.
Well, another thing, I don't know whether I spoke to you or not about our vacation plans,
but I told your dad that I would believe it when I saw it,
and I guess that it really is going to come true.
We are going to Canada.
and in one of the stamp newspapers he has read that they are having a fair in Montreal
and they're utilizing the buildings and the spots that the Expo Fair was at
and it's just the Canadian fair, there's no foreign exhibits or anything

But it should be interesting to see, and it would be a nice trip, plus a pool. Plus, if we went south to see the churches, we would have the worry of the problems that are going on in the south, and I definitely don't want to go into anything when we know it's already there.
even though I would really like to see Ruth and Jack and Joy, but it isn't worth the worry.
If we went east to Washington, D.C., or anything like that, we'd still run into those problems.
So maybe the Canadians are a little bit more livable to associate with at this time,
and it would be a cooler trip.
And, uh, but, uh, it came as a complete surprise to me when he mentioned it last week, this is where we should go.
And, uh, I myself, uh, would, uh, in a way like to go to Colorado.
Uh, there's flying to, uh, sea just a minute from here.
Well, David was just knocking on the door. I'm back in the back bedroom finishing up this tape, and he's knocking on the door to let me know he's going over to Jimmy's when he's playing.
and he seems to be real thrilled with it and I hope it holds together long enough to have some fun out of it.
But anyway, it came as a complete surprise to me that this was the trip that we were going to plan.
So as far as I'm concerned, I don't care where we go just so we can get away from here for a while.
And the German couple that live back here near Hope Road and there,
They went on this trip last summer to see the Expo Fair.
So they're going to, they brought some maps over the night, and they're going to call
the Chicago Motor Club and get us a routing for us so we can have a good trip up there.
there. And I didn't get the dimension when we were going. We are going, well, Daddy's
asking for his vacation to start August 5th. And I imagine that we might be there Saturday
morning early before the 5th. And that'll get us to a party on the 3rd for 10 days.
and then that will give him a few days home.
He had thought about going later on in the month, but I don't care to go that late,
that close to school starting, because I would like to be home a week or ten days before school starts
to get anything done that needs to be done before I start school and David also.

And not because George Ray's coming home, because I could care less about being here for her visit, but it's just that we would probably get back just as she's pulling in. So I don't imagine I'll see too much of her, but I'll be here anyway.
And, uh, well, uh, my grandma has things planned, like there's going to be some short trips made, and, um, one of them will be up to, uh, the Dixon Mound.
And, uh, they go through that day, like, uh, I'm going to stay home with Becky and babysit her.
That is if she will let me babysit her.
But that might be a little hard with a stranger, which I am a stranger to her.
Well, David just came in and he wants me to run him up to Bolle's or Franklin Mall.
He needs things for his airplane like gasoline and I don't know what all. He just sends off some stuff.
So, I don't usually look close to all of his phones.
The second trip, we get mail early in the morning and then again after 1.30.
They make another deposit if there's anything.
But since school's been out, I haven't been making that second trip up there.
It's just too much running along with the day we're going to summer school.
So, and I'm, of course, being busy here, but I just haven't tried to get uptown and do it.
But today, I'm kind of getting it off.
It's kind of good.
I used off last Friday, too.
But you have to have a day that you can just group off and do whatever you want to.
And so I want to get this tape run off.
and there's a sprinkle as much as I can and that takes off.
But it's thundering outside right now and the prediction is for heavy rain and thunderstorms and possibly hail.
So I guess that sounds like typical weather to you, but we do need the rain pretty bad.
and I regret it. It used to be watered. I've kind of been putting it off because of the
protection rain the last few days, which we haven't had any since. But I think it's
about to get the job done today. When Bull showed up, I came home with the groceries
and I was waiting for David to get out of the zoo. And I got my grocery shopping done.
And so I ran into a woman uptown and took her home and dropped her off and we talked a little bit.
And I got home here and unloaded the groceries and started playing that tape to see if it was a description of the slides, which it turned out to be.
And here come both. And he had been here since last Saturday.
and they would not have just happened to run into him.
I was in the park the other day with the duck out there.

Well, naturally, we'd been wondering about him, wondering about him long.
By running into him last Tuesday afternoon, I knew sort of what the idea was for not showing up.
So I hadn't been too worried about him since Tuesday.
But you never know when he's going to come in here.

And so he came in here about 11.30, and I had planned on coming right back home after I picked up David, because the stamp store didn't open until noon today. And I figured if I pick up David, I'd go up to the plaid stamp place and pick up the things that I wanted to get.
So I asked him if he was going to stick around. I said, well, he would if I was coming right back.
And I said, well, I had a plan on it. So he said he'd be back later on this afternoon.
So I want to get out of here and get the runaround done and the neighbor boat done before he shows up.
So I said, well, I'm up that boat. I'll stop at the post office again.
and also I want to pick up a bulb for the slide projector because one of these
signs when I'm showing these slides to someone that bulb is going to burn out and we're not going to be able to finish showing the pictures so I figured I'd pick up the spare. I checked over to
I'm hoping that Miles will have one.
This projector is pretty good at John, one thing it isn't.

and if it would take those Super 8 films of yours, but he says no it wouldn't.

Well, I do want to congratulate you on passing your SOFI test.

And I was real happy to know that you had.

And I'm also thrilled that you want to go ahead and get more courses to take advantage of while you're over there. And that would be a good way to spend your liberty, studying, because it does help take up a lot of time.

But I looked around and seen some of the women that have taken up the path so I feel like if they can do it, I can do it.
I'm sure going to try my best.
I bet your dad is really getting his legs run off right now with these three jobs.
and not going to let Lincoln start his vacation this Saturday.
And his son gets married Saturday,
and as soon as the victims' wedding goes with,
they're taking off on vacation.
I don't know exactly where they're going,
but he's going to be gone for a month.
So your dad's going to have to take care of his work.
They're at the main compound there, Lincoln,

And besides this new job starting, they're at the town of the farm, which they call the Annex. Plus, he's still going to Champaign and Springfield. So I'll tell you, he's going to be running his legs off. He's going to be ready for that vacation when all of this gets here.

So, I love my stuff. I really can't think too much more. Jake and Shorty have a tape recorder like this, which I wrote here, and it's really been funny how they've been taping on it, trying to teach Jake how to run it.

course, he's, uh, David could do, uh, what, uh, in five minutes, what it's taken Jake a week to do, and, uh, so they, I, uh, think that in due time, if, don't get, don't be waiting to stay up, uh, losing any sleep waiting for a tape, but I imagine it's in due time that you may end up getting a tape from them, and, uh, he's quite a character when he's in a tape, so boy, he really likes to, to, uh, jack on that tape recorder.
And I tell you, we've all got more than a floor of asthma than some of the things that we sit on just from practicing.
So, I'm just about ready to run down on a conversation.
But since I am searching for work, honey, I'm going to find myself.
I would like to get ready for sailing and take care of yourself and have a journey back to the States.
It won't be long now, but we'll be having your two-week-old,
and you will enjoy it and get back.
It'll be here.
And I'll be writing you a letter in a day or two.
Bye-bye.

It picks up about everything I want. WLS sounds like WDZ, not a squirrely sounding. And what, Mommy and me went up to the pride stamp store today and cashed some of her pride stamp books in. And she got a pillow for Daddy and slippers to clip the grass. And then some figurines to put up on the cabinet up there by the dining room. And then she got me an airplane, a gas airplane. Just like a fighter airplane. fighting three wheels. It shoots two rockets off of it. And the pilot rejects, you know, you push a lever or something where it's flying. It opens it up and lets the pilot out. And it's a pretty neat plane. I've been sleeping on the top bunk now because it's been hot. Daddy said it's cooler up there. Then I wouldn't sleep with any covers on. Then I'd kick my covers off to the side and they'd fall off. Last night it was cold. So I had to get down from there and go around looking for all my covers and put them back on. I took Sammy out to the park, I think it was Tuesday, Tuesday or Wednesday, that was Tuesday. and I took him he walked out to the water swim around real close to the shore and then when I get ready to leave he got out of the water and start coming up by the car and looked like he wanted to come home with me so I caught him and threw him in the water as far as I could then we got the car and took off. So, I've got three pigeons now. My little ones are starting to fly now, learning how to fly. One speckled one, it's kind of stingy and in a blackish kind. He's the one that can fly. So I put them up on the, well I threw them up so they could fly. The speckles were landed up on the roof of the garage. So the kids went up there. They stayed up there for about an hour. They'd walk around in the gutter and make all kinds of noise. by then they never came down so I went up on the roof there and threw them down into the cave. Didn't hurt them. Fish for the fish pond now. We got some bug eyes and regular goldfish and some moss and stuff. Tuesday when I took Sam out to the park before I took him out I had mommy get some film for him. and then took some pictures of him and put him in the pond then and I had to hold him because he was scared, he was frightened and everything. The way I ran and banded him this time was I took some wire that has insulation around it and twisted it around his leg you know just loosen it up not too loose so he couldn't get it off but loosen it up and not tight so he could you know he could go a little more and it wouldn't stop the circulation. I had a blue one on one side of his leg and a blue one on the other side. I took and painted his feet black and then put silver stripes down it. He wore that off. I applied some bill yesterday and it was real cool. I had some pictures of his death. The deaf looks something like a sand, the uh, third, the black and yellow deaf, the mallard deaf. I'm just kidding, the mallard is probably something like a Vietnam type deaf, foreign deaf. That is the morning the birds get louder and louder in the morning, you know, when they sing around 5. Yesterday morning they woke me up at 8.30 and they were, you know, loud then. But my biggest pity, he really liked Sam. They always sit out in the yard with each other. But now, kids don't know what to do without Sam around. Talk to you, I guess. I'll see you, Mike. I'm gonna have to go out while I'm happy to, but... Still have nothing else to say, so... As long as I'm not finishing the tape up, I guess. Bye. Of course, we were all wrong on some of those lines, but that's what they were. And we thought that they were pictures of, I don't know, that showed one jeep or one truck that had been burnt. And it looked like it had hit a mine or something. It had been hit by something. And we thought it was this truck that his buddy was killed in. But as it turned out, the tape we got today, it was a different truck. It had been in a mine and it had burnt naturally. So then there was one Korean in, which, he was killed. So Bill had taken protection from it. We were wrong about those slides, but we were happy to get the tape. And the slides that came yesterday, the 13th, were mailed. They were postmarked with the U.S. Navy postmarked the 10th of June. So that is really the fastest we've ever gotten anything from there. And no doubt he made the tape just before he sent the slides out. And in the tape, he didn't mention anything about being moved. And I'm just beginning to wonder if maybe they were just threatening him with the fact that he could be moved if he didn't learn to say yes or no, sir, instead of coming back with an answer. And so I hope he doesn't get moved because I think he's real happy where he's at. He says so on the tape, at the end of this tape that we made. And they really have a lot of fun and it's one big happy family there. So as long as it can stay that way for a long time, it shouldn't be too rough. I'm going to go back on to this conversation that I ended at the end of the tape. and tell you my opinion, I don't know whether you're interested or not, but I feel like I want to get it off my chest. But the thing of it is, whenever George May would call Mother about any thing that she'd have to call about, well, the conversation would always get on to you more. And so Mother had just talked to Coach May one day, and when she got through, well, I was up there shortly afterwards. And Mother said, I just hate to talk to that girl on the phone anymore, because she just is so upset about those boys being over there. And it just breaks my heart for her to be so upset and everything. everything. And I said, well, I realize that she probably is, and I think we all are concerned about them, but she can't be that way. She has to get a hold of herself and keep her chin up to keep those boys from knowing it. And I said, that isn't going to help her any to be that way. Well, of course, and Mother was crying when she was telling me all this, you know, and all the tears in me. Well, Mike, actually, I could be in tears all the time if I let myself. But I feel like that this is to be, and if I can't keep my spirits up, then what's it going to be like for your kids to get better that is all depressing and everything. And what I meant by making this a discussion is they are all aga about you boys being old in Vietnam and this and that and so forth. And everything, every time there's anything in the paper, why there's a great deal of concern from the other end and everything. everything but when it comes to a mere little thing like a tape being made and sent to you kids they don't have the time and I think that uh there I know they're not any busier than we are and how long would it take to say a few words on tape and I know that they're really jarring on the spot to want to hear any tapes or CA to slide that we get from you kids. So I'm not going to say anything to them. In fact, this last tape that you sent, I'm not even going to let them know we got it. I don't feel like that whatever you sent or taped to us, that is to us. And If you have anything to say on, well, mother quickly takes offense to things that you might say that's the truth about them. And I can't help it if she's that way. And so I just try to ignore it and don't breed any more problems than what there already are. But I know from past experiences that the words that you're singing have many conversations and things go a lot better. But I wish they would get busy and show a little more of concern in the right way. and she, I send boxes to you kids frequently, and she is going to send the boxes, every time I turn around, she was there for a while, she was talking about, well, she was going to send the boxes to Bill, and, or send some books or something, and, so, nothing was ever, she never did good, And so the next day or two, I said, well, I set Bill a box today, or I set Mike a box today. Oh, you did? I said, yes. So it's just one of those things, like, just because I'm doing it, she can act like they can't do it either. Well, I don't care what they do. As long as I know what I'm doing, and I feel like I'm doing the right thing, that's all that matters to me. And I think that you can read between the lines. It just goes well. That was it. I want to tell you that the mall down here at the Talley is opening and the Ben Franklin has opened and the beauty show down there has a thrifty drug. All their supplies in now. And every time I talk on this thing, my throat starts to choke up, and it isn't. It's just that I'm talking, I think, more, and in the frame of mind that I'm talking, I am. So please excuse the throat clearing. But anyway, there's supposed to be 12 stores when they all get open, and I don't think some of the spots are rented out yet, but it certainly is a nice place, and you won't believe your eyes when you see it again. Well, another thing, I don't know whether I spoke to you or not about our vacation plans, but I told your dad that I would believe it when I saw it, and I guess that it really is going to come true. We are going to Canada. and in one of the stamp newspapers he has read that they are having a fair in Montreal and they're utilizing the buildings and the spots that the Expo Fair was at and it's just the Canadian fair, there's no foreign exhibits or anything But it should be interesting to see, and it would be a nice trip, plus a pool. Plus, if we went south to see the churches, we would have the worry of the problems that are going on in the south, and I definitely don't want to go into anything when we know it's already there. even though I would really like to see Ruth and Jack and Joy, but it isn't worth the worry. If we went east to Washington, D.C., or anything like that, we'd still run into those problems. So maybe the Canadians are a little bit more livable to associate with at this time, and it would be a cooler trip. And, uh, but, uh, it came as a complete surprise to me when he mentioned it last week, this is where we should go. And, uh, I myself, uh, would, uh, in a way like to go to Colorado. Uh, there's flying to, uh, sea just a minute from here. Well, David was just knocking on the door. I'm back in the back bedroom finishing up this tape, and he's knocking on the door to let me know he's going over to Jimmy's when he's playing. and he seems to be real thrilled with it and I hope it holds together long enough to have some fun out of it. But anyway, it came as a complete surprise to me that this was the trip that we were going to plan. So as far as I'm concerned, I don't care where we go just so we can get away from here for a while. And the German couple that live back here near Hope Road and there, They went on this trip last summer to see the Expo Fair. So they're going to, they brought some maps over the night, and they're going to call the Chicago Motor Club and get us a routing for us so we can have a good trip up there. there. And I didn't get the dimension when we were going. We are going, well, Daddy's asking for his vacation to start August 5th. And I imagine that we might be there Saturday morning early before the 5th. And that'll get us to a party on the 3rd for 10 days. and then that will give him a few days home. He had thought about going later on in the month, but I don't care to go that late, that close to school starting, because I would like to be home a week or ten days before school starts to get anything done that needs to be done before I start school and David also. And not because George Ray's coming home, because I could care less about being here for her visit, but it's just that we would probably get back just as she's pulling in. So I don't imagine I'll see too much of her, but I'll be here anyway. And, uh, well, uh, my grandma has things planned, like there's going to be some short trips made, and, um, one of them will be up to, uh, the Dixon Mound. And, uh, they go through that day, like, uh, I'm going to stay home with Becky and babysit her. That is if she will let me babysit her. But that might be a little hard with a stranger, which I am a stranger to her. Well, David just came in and he wants me to run him up to Bolle's or Franklin Mall. He needs things for his airplane like gasoline and I don't know what all. He just sends off some stuff. So, I don't usually look close to all of his phones. The second trip, we get mail early in the morning and then again after 1.30. They make another deposit if there's anything. But since school's been out, I haven't been making that second trip up there. It's just too much running along with the day we're going to summer school. So, and I'm, of course, being busy here, but I just haven't tried to get uptown and do it. But today, I'm kind of getting it off. It's kind of good. I used off last Friday, too. But you have to have a day that you can just group off and do whatever you want to. And so I want to get this tape run off. and there's a sprinkle as much as I can and that takes off. But it's thundering outside right now and the prediction is for heavy rain and thunderstorms and possibly hail. So I guess that sounds like typical weather to you, but we do need the rain pretty bad. and I regret it. It used to be watered. I've kind of been putting it off because of the protection rain the last few days, which we haven't had any since. But I think it's about to get the job done today. When Bull showed up, I came home with the groceries and I was waiting for David to get out of the zoo. And I got my grocery shopping done. And so I ran into a woman uptown and took her home and dropped her off and we talked a little bit. And I got home here and unloaded the groceries and started playing that tape to see if it was a description of the slides, which it turned out to be. And here come both. And he had been here since last Saturday. and they would not have just happened to run into him. I was in the park the other day with the duck out there. He had made up his mind that he wouldn't come out until he had found a job. Well, naturally, we'd been wondering about him, wondering about him long. By running into him last Tuesday afternoon, I knew sort of what the idea was for not showing up. So I hadn't been too worried about him since Tuesday. But you never know when he's going to come in here. And so he came in here about 11.30, and I had planned on coming right back home after I picked up David, because the stamp store didn't open until noon today. And I figured if I pick up David, I'd go up to the plaid stamp place and pick up the things that I wanted to get. So I asked him if he was going to stick around. I said, well, he would if I was coming right back. And I said, well, I had a plan on it. So he said he'd be back later on this afternoon. So I want to get out of here and get the runaround done and the neighbor boat done before he shows up. So I said, well, I'm up that boat. I'll stop at the post office again. and also I want to pick up a bulb for the slide projector because one of these signs when I'm showing these slides to someone that bulb is going to burn out and we're not going to be able to finish showing the pictures so I figured I'd pick up the spare. I checked over to I'm hoping that Miles will have one. This projector is pretty good at John, one thing it isn't. Little did Uncle John realize when he gave it to us about 18 years ago that we'd be showing slides on that you boys would be taking over there. I questioned Daddy about that movie projector that we have. and if it would take those Super 8 films of yours, but he says no it wouldn't. So maybe, I don't think we'll ever do a new projector. No more movies than we take anymore, but we could always ramp one. And if you do what you say you're going to about anyone out there in California, that's all necessary. But I know you'll enjoy having a movie camera and you'll learn how to use it. You just want to make sure you don't pan, which is moving it around too fast. because you want to get the full action of what you're taking. So, it seemed like there was something else I wanted to talk about. Well, I do want to congratulate you on passing your SOFI test. I had no doubt for what you would pass it anyway. And I was real happy to know that you had. And I'm also thrilled that you want to go ahead and get more courses to take advantage of while you're over there. And that would be a good way to spend your liberty, studying, because it does help take up a lot of time. I will no doubt be doing plenty of it this fall myself. I'm just hoping that that course is more than what I could handle. But I looked around and seen some of the women that have taken up the path so I feel like if they can do it, I can do it. I'm sure going to try my best. I bet your dad is really getting his legs run off right now with these three jobs. and not going to let Lincoln start his vacation this Saturday. And his son gets married Saturday, and as soon as the victims' wedding goes with, they're taking off on vacation. I don't know exactly where they're going, but he's going to be gone for a month. So your dad's going to have to take care of his work. They're at the main compound there, Lincoln, And besides this new job starting, they're at the town of the farm, which they call the Annex. Plus, he's still going to Champaign and Springfield. So I'll tell you, he's going to be running his legs off. He's going to be ready for that vacation when all of this gets here. So, I love my stuff. I really can't think too much more. Jake and Shorty have a tape recorder like this, which I wrote here, and it's really been funny how they've been taping on it, trying to teach Jake how to run it. course, he's, uh, David could do, uh, what, uh, in five minutes, what it's taken Jake a week to do, and, uh, so they, I, uh, think that in due time, if, don't get, don't be waiting to stay up, uh, losing any sleep waiting for a tape, but I imagine it's in due time that you may end up getting a tape from them, and, uh, he's quite a character when he's in a tape, so boy, he really likes to, to, uh, jack on that tape recorder. And I tell you, we've all got more than a floor of asthma than some of the things that we sit on just from practicing. So, I'm just about ready to run down on a conversation. But since I am searching for work, honey, I'm going to find myself. I would like to get ready for sailing and take care of yourself and have a journey back to the States. It won't be long now, but we'll be having your two-week-old, and you will enjoy it and get back. It'll be here. And I'll be writing you a letter in a day or two. Bye-bye. Boom.

1968-06-20.label: WF Given to Mike
1968-06-20.text:
Thurs. 20 Jun

Greetings Duc,
        Well ol' buddy whats it like
in the real Navy?
        I haven't heard from you
recently so I decided to write.
We just finished up making river
supply runs. We now are on market
time patrol. You may know exactly
what I'm talking about. In case
you don't - I explain a little.
  We carry ammo, fuel, and spare
parts along with a spare crew
for 4 swift boats. Once each
day, each boat, comes alongside
for a spare crew and re-supply.
You've read enough about swifts
to know they check all junks
and watch the coast line.
     Well ol' buddy do you
remember in school when we were
told about type desks. I wrote
to the Ft Branch and to a
senator about wanting a one year
tour because I'm married.
  Guess what - I am leaving here
in Sept for 30 days leave and
then reporting to the USS
Tulare AKA 112. It has 6-3"50's
and quite a bit of FT gear -
I have a lot to learn before
I get there.

#2

  I've been searching for info
on 3" mounts but no luck so far.
I hope they have patience with
me. Maybe I can learn
some electronics while I'm
there.
     Well are you going for
second class this fall? I
think I'll take the test but
if I do pass I'm not extending
for second.               (in Navy)
     Well I'm over 3 now, celebrated
my 20th birthday, 1st anniversary
and decided the Navy's not
for me - how about you. I've
been getting nothing but
screwed over. We have had
laundry or fresh water showers
since we left Taiwan. I've
spent so much time on watch
on this thing - I almost
live in the pilot house or
after-steering.
     Well not much else is
happening. I don't have any
Purple Heart or Navy Cross
yet. We've got the
usual 3 ribbons & we're up
for unit citation.

#3.

  My new ship is out of Diego
so maybe I'll see you.
Just think Duc - pretty
soon we're half way.

  Well I best go.

            Take care & write,
                   Sincerely
                     Giv

P.S. Plan to be in Subic from
3 July to 25th then Guam
for 5 weeks just in case
you are
1968-06-20.attribution: Letter, W.F. Given FTG-3 — Ducy Family Archives

1968-06-20.label: Jouett Jargon
1968-06-20.text:
June 20, 1968 "Jouett Jargon"
                                        SAVE

HOBART
    MANILA (UPI)--THE AUSTRALIAN DESTROYER HMAS HOBART STEAMED INTO THE BIG U.S. NAVAL BASE OF SUBIC BAY IN THE PHILLIPINES TODAY FOR REPAIRS FOLLOWING A ROCKET ATTACK OFF THE VIETNAM COAST.
    HOBART WAS HIT SUNDAY BY AN "AIR-TO-AIR ROCKET POSSIBLY FIRED BY FRIENDLY AIRCRAFT," ACCORDING TO AN AUSTRALIAN SPOKESMAN IN SAIGON. THE ATTACK WHICH COST THE LIVES OF TWO AUSTRALIAN SAILORS, OCCURRED IN THE SOUTH CHINA SEA NEAR THE DEMILITARIZED ZONE DIVIDING THE TWO VIETNAMS.
    A U.S. NAVAL SPOKESMAN SAID THE AUSTRALIAN SHIP ARRIVED ABOUT 8 A.M. (2400 GMT) AND TIED UP AT ONE OF THE BASE'S MAIN DOCKS. THE BASE, ON THE WESTERN COAST OF LUZON, IS ABOUT 60 AIR MILES FROM MANILA BUT TAKES SIX HOURS TO REACH BY ROAD.
    THE SPOKESMAN SAID HE HAD NO ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.
    THE AUSTRALIAN SPOKESMAN IN SAIGON DECLINED TO GIVE THE EXTENT OF DAMAGE TO THE DESTROYER WHICH HAS BEEN IN VIETNAM WATERS SINCE MARCH. THAT THE SHIP SAILED FOR SUBIC BAY MAY HAVE INDICATED THE ROCKET RIPPED INTO SOME VITAL GEAR.
    DETAILS OF THE ATTACK WERE SKETCHY. IT OCCURRED ABOUT THE SAME TIME THAT AMERICAN PLANES WERE SHOOTING DOWN SEVEN COMMUNIST HELICOPTERS OPERATING OVER SOUTH VIETNAM FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE WAR.

[Handwritten annotation: "This gave us a scare!"]

---

[Top of page 2 — partial fragment from preceding article:]
...WHOLE RANGE OF WEAPONS SUCH AS MACHINE GUNS, BAZOOKAS, MORTARS AND ANTI-TANK GUNS.

VIOLENCE
    WASHINGTON (UPI)--CHAIRMAN MILTON EISENHOWER SAID TUESDAY THE PRESIDENT'S COMMISSION ON VIOLENCE WOULD INVESTIGATE THREE MAJOR AREAS OF LAWLESSNESS--POLITICAL ASSASSINATION, CRIMINAL ATTACKS ON INDIVIDUALS AND CIVIL DISORDERS SUCH AS RIOTS.
    IN A STATEMENT AFTER THE FIRST MEETING OF THE 10-MEMBER COMMISSION NAMED BY PRESIDENT JOHNSON AFTER THE SLAYING OF SEN. ROBERT F. KENNEDY, EISENHOWER SAID:
    "WE ARE TODAY A FREE AND PROGRESSIVE SOCIETY. WE SHALL REMAIN SO BY FINDING WAYS TO ACHIEVE OUR GOALS WITHOUT VIOLENCE. WE HOPE OUR COMMISSION CAN HELP TO ILLUMINATE THE PATH... WE EXPRESS OUR CONFIDENCE THAT LIBERTY, PROGRESS AND ORDER ARE NOT IRRECONCILABLE."
    EISENHOWER SAID THAT IN ADDITION TO THE THREE MAJOR AREAS OF INVESTIGATION THE COMMISSION ALSO WOULD STUDY THE SALE AND CONTROL OF GUNS, THE STRUCTURE OF LAW AND LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND THEORETICAL, CULTURAL, RELIGIOUS AND OTHER FACTORS RELATING TO AN UNDERSTANDING OF VIOLENCE.
    EISENHOWER SAID THE COMMISSION WOULD FIRST SEEK TO MEASURE THE EXTENT OF VIOLENCE AND UNDERSTAND ITS CAUSES AND "DEVELOP CONCRETE RECOMMENDATIONS TO CONTROL AND REDUCE THE DOMESTIC VIOLENCE WHICH SEEMS TO BE SCOURGING THIS NATION."
    "WE STARTED WORK WITH OPEN MINDS," EISENHOWER ADDED. "BUT WE DO NOT BEGIN OUR EFFORT AT DEAD CENTER."

1968-06-21.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-06-21.text:
21 June 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Sounds as if you poor squids had a little action up your way. Just make sure you get those MIG pilots back safe and fuck the others (ha ha.)

Here is that money order for the 30 bucks I owe you. I finely got to a post office to get it made out.

Now Sam is in Da Nang back at the Bn. area. I am on 30 days of mess duty, and Sam really skating. I have the mid duty, and all of my work is done by 8:30 PM. I can't really bitch because no one fucks with me, and the one thing I can't stand is to get fucked with.

Do you remember that Bob White me and Carter, Angle and Penny hung around with and drank together? Well I saw him in Hoi-An, his in the Seabees. He gave me a Allied catalog. I am going to order a Sony 907 tape recorder, it only cost $34.50. I also checked at the PX for one and it cost $31.00 but would take 3-4 months to get to me. So I said fuck that! What do you think about it? OK ya you know that walkie-talkie we bought (C-555) well they've got them for $11.00 now each. If you want to look at this catalog I'll send it. Just let me know.

Well I am going to go for now, I'll write again soon. Be good and don't "fall off the ship."

P.S. I almost forgot               Little Brother
Connie wanted your                  Bill
address, so I gave it to her.
Has she written yet? Just wondering.
                                    OVER

CINCPACFLT VISIT

On 21 June, JOUETT was paid a great honor and enjoyed a rare privilege when she
was visited by three of the most important U.S. Navy Commanders in the Pacific
Fleet. This episode of the JOUETT heritage began when eight gongs rang out sharply,
as the word was passed "Pacific Fleet, arriving". Then the word was passed,
"Seventh Fleet, arriving". This was followed by the announcement "Carrier Division
Five, Arriving".

The three admirals quickly were escorted to the bridge and CIC Areas, where they
were then briefed on current operations.

CINCPACFLT addressed the assembled officers and men of JOUETT, commending
them on the fine manner in which they were carrying out their duties.

[Photo: Three admirals being briefed on the bridge, examining equipment and charts with Jouett officers. Officers in khaki uniforms, admirals in khaki with scrambled eggs on caps]

[Photo: Admiral greeting officers on deck, saluting, with ship's superstructure visible in background]

1968-06-21.label: Vigilance — Page 29
1968-06-21.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-06-21.text:
CRUISER GETS UNIT AWARD

The Navy's Meritorious Unit Commendation was presented to the crew of the USS Canberra (CA 70) by
RAdm. S.H. Kinney. Canberra, then designated CAG 2, was cited for "meritorious achievement in
connection with military operations against enemy aggressor forces in Vietnam."

The citation read in part: "Throughout her tours on the gunline, Canberra supported the forces
ashore with effective and devastating gunfire. Her fire support of many operations.. resulted in
the infliction of severe damage upon the enemy."


SEAFARERS INITIATE 27 MEMBERS

During a recent deployment, a unique organization was founded on the USS Saint Paul (CA 73), "The
Seafarers' Club".

There is only one requirement for membership in this exclusive club, and that is to have a minimum
of 15 years of sea duty. Twenty-seven crewmembers of this 1,100-man cruiser, ranging from Captain
to Second Class Petty Officer, represent more than 425 years of sea service.

A ceremony took place on the forecastle of the veteran cruiser during a brief lull in naval gunfire
operations off the coast of Vietnam. The Senior Seafarer, Chief Bosun Frank Alves, presented
Seafarer certificates to the members at the first meeting of the club. Of his 27-year Naval career,
Chief Warrant Officer Alves has 21 years, nine months and 20 days of sea duty.

The Saint Paul is commanded by a Seafarer, Capt. Ralph A. Hilson, with more than 17 years of sea
duty to his credit.

Rear Admiral S.H. Moore, embarked on Saint Paul as Commander Cruiser-Destroyer Group, U.S. Seventh
Fleet, was admitted to the club as an honorary member. He has 17 years of at-sea time.


'STARS' VISIT DLG IN TONKIN GULF

Eight gongs rang out sharply aboard the guided missile frigate USS Jouett (DLG 29)—as the word was
passed, "Pacific Fleet arriving", "Seventh Fleet arriving", "Carrier Division Five arriving".

Shortly thereafter a big SH-3 helicopter landed on the helo deck aft. Admiral John J. Hyland, Vice
Admiral William F. Bringle, and Rear Admiral Ralph W. Cousins, were greeted by Captain Arthur
Emerson, Jr., Commander Destroyer Squadron One, and Captain Robert S. Hayes, Commanding Officer of
the Jouett.

The three admirals, on a surprise visit to the Jouett, while conducting operations in the Tonkin
Gulf, quickly toured the bridge and CIC area, and then were briefed on current operations. They also
met and congratulated the embarked helicopter crew who had recently been flown into hostile territory
to rescue two Navy aviators.

Later Adm. Hyland spoke to the assembled officers and men of the Jouett, commending them on the fine
manner in which they were carrying out their job in the Seventh Fleet.

He predicted that in years to come they would be happy and proud to know that they had served their
nation when it needed them. He noted in particular the success achieved by the team of surface ships
and helicopters, under Capt. Emerson's command, in rescuing downed aviators.

As the admirals bid farewell, before lifting off in their helicopter, the gongs rang out, followed
in order by; "Pacific Fleet, departing", "Seventh Fleet, departing', "Carrier Division Five,
departing".

The Senior Chief Petty Officer, Tinbrook Collins, Jr., who escorted the admirals, stated, "In all
my 29 years in the Navy, I have never been so near to so many stars at one time. I had stars in my
eyes all afternoon."

[Photo: STARS-(left to right) Capt. A.T. Emerson, Jr., COMDESRON ONE, Adm. J.J. Hyland,
CINCPACFLT, VAdm. W.F. Bringle, COMSEVENTHFLT, RAdm. R.W. Cousins, COMCARDIV FIVE, Capt. R.S.
Hayes, Commanding Officer of the Jouett, and LCdr. J.M. Loveless, Jouett's Operations Officer,
attend a briefing in the ship's CIC. (Photo by FTM2 R.J. Bain)]

1968-06-22.attribution: Audio cassette recording, Tape 6, Side 1 — Mike Ducy. Transcribed by OpenAI Whisper. Ducy Family Archives

segments.text: Hello, Mother, Dad, and David. This is Saturday the 22nd of June and our ship is still up here on station in the Gulf of Tonkin.
We've got about six more days left up here in the combat zone and then we head back to Subic Bay for a short stop and make way back to the States.
Our time of arrival is still on the 18th of July, and there has been a slight change in
our plans from the last time since I talked to you.
Our plans were to escort the Enterprise back and not to cross the equator, but as I mentioned,
that would probably change, as most things here in the Navy do, and our plans have changed.
We are to cross the equator on about the 10th of July.
And, of course, you already know the big initiation ceremonies and everything will take place.
So it should be quite an experience for most of the guys on the ship
because there are about 75, I'll put that between 50 and 75 people on the ship
who have crossed the equator before.
And the rest of us, which totaled about 350 and never have had the opportunity to do that.
The way they do this, if you cross the equator, you are known as a shellback.
If you have not crossed the equator, you're known as a pollywog.
So that's what I am.
I'm a pollywog.
And, of course, the shellbacks now are starting to plan what they're going to do
and hold little meetings and everything just to get some arrangement on how they're going to hold the ceremonies.
Of course, they're outnumbered pretty well, so some of the Paliwags there on the ship have been putting out little signs like King Neptune is dead, Paliwag power, Paliwag rule, and stuff like that.
But Navy tradition being what it is, I don't think that just because the shellbacks are outnumbered,
they're going to call off the ceremonies because this is a real traditional happening,
and no doubt it's going to be carried through all the way.
So I'll be sure to have plenty of film in my camera that day and hope to get some pretty good pictures of it.
I received your tape of June 14th this afternoon when the mail came in.
I was real glad to hear that things are still going along pretty fine back home,
and David sounded like he was in pretty good spirits.
I hope he does enjoy himself at summer school and summer camp as well.
I didn't mean to say enjoy himself at summer school,
but I'm sure he'll get a little bit out of it,
and I know he'll have a good time out there at Boy Scout camp.
Thursday night we refueled from an oiler,
and as usual they sent across third-class mail and packages,
and I got your care package there the same night.
I was glad to get it.
It didn't take too long to get here, considering the circumstances.
I received a letter from you on the 16th, which you wrote on June the 10th,
and I was kind of waiting to hold off the answer,
feeling that you would be sending me a tape in a few days and so I held off
too loud to you know rather answer this letter our mail on here has been kind of
slow it's I don't know why it's been this way this time up here perhaps they
haven't got the good facilities to handle it like they had before I don't
really know everything if they go through to get mail on here to us but
Somewhere along the line it's getting slowed up going back to the States and also coming
out here to us.
I mentioned we had about six more days left up here in the Gulf and we've got about 27
days left till we arrive back in the States.
We've got a status board down here in the gun plotting room and we keep the days counted
on that and every day we erase the number and count it down one more.
So everybody's pretty well up to date on how many days we've got left over here.
And they're starting to make slight preparations for getting back in the States,
like cleaning out certain parts of the ship and just making rather small arrangements,
one at a time, so we'll be all ready to pull back into San Diego.
Thursday morning, they brought the Catholic chaplain aboard,
and he said mass and heard confessions.
It's, I believe, the second time that he's came aboard since we've been out here on the line.
And he was from the Enterprise.
He said that he was pretty well impressed by the Jewess and everything that's been going on up here on the ship.
And the other day we had three admirals come aboard at one time, and they were very impressed by the way we've been handling ourselves up here.
and we're really impressed by the ship.
So this put a few points on the captain's side, I suppose.
And I suppose they'll have all kinds of write-ups and everything about us
back in the San Diego papers and everything when we get back.
So it'll be a few souvenirs to cut out of pasting the scrapbook a few years from now.
On Wednesday night, about 12 o'clock midnight or thereafter,
actually about 12 30 midnight which made it early thursday morning we had a star alert a
f4 was down about 10 miles inland and we launched the helicopter and they went in and picked up both
of the pilots but i'm like this ship they were injured i believe a little bit and the helicopter
did pick up some small arms fire from some ground troops but uh nobody in the helo got hurt this
time and they got back safe in the sun and it's the only action that we've actually had up here
since i last wrote to you things uh aren't actually quiet up here i was just back on the
fantail before i came on watch right now where i'm at now and i could see some uh bombing and
uh tracer shells over there on the beach of course we're not really too close i imagine we're about
12 miles or 10 miles off the coast.
So we're well out of range of anything over there.
But you can see it pretty well during the night.
And they're keeping up a steady pace of bombing over there.
I don't really think it's doing much good because the war is still going on.
And as long as it's still going on, you know that somebody's not doing something right.
But it all remains to be seen.
there's so many aspects that have to take place before anybody can really claim that they're
winning any victory at all. The news weeks that you sent in the package were real good reading.
I brought them down here in the gun plowing room and most of the guys look at them and read them.
Kind of good to see what's happening back there and see what the politicians are up to,
who's taking good care of us servicemen over here
and read about all those draft dodgers and everybody else.
The news over here is fairly accurate.
We listen to the AFVN, which is the Armed Forces Vietnam Network,
and they've got pretty good news reports on there.
We also receive a little newspaper here on the ship that they print up in the Radio Central,
which they receive off of the teletype network.
And so we get news possibly one or two days after it comes out,
and we get the stars and stripes.
But by the time we get the stars and stripes, it's all old news,
and we've already read about it or heard about it on the radio over here.
So we know pretty well what's going on in the world.
And baseball season, I've been keeping pretty well up to date on that,
keeping an eye on the baseball scores.
I see there that the Cubs aren't doing too bad.
They're right around the 500 mark.
It seems like the National League, as usual, is pretty tight there.
And it's just about open for anyone.
Of course, the Cardinals are doing just like they did last year.
They're on top, and they just might stay there all the rest of the way through the season.
I'm looking forward to when I do get back in San Diego to possibly go up to Los Angeles
and take in a few baseball games up there.
It's the time of the year when the baseball season is pretty well in full swing,
and I'm sure they ought to find a pretty good game up there at this time of the year.
I noticed I didn't have my tape recorder turned up too high,
so you ought to hear a little increase in volume here.
I noticed on your side, too, of the tape there where you were talking at Mother,
it was a real week, and I could barely hear it.
I couldn't make out hardly anything that you said.
I hope you didn't say anything real important.
but this is something that you kind of have to watch when you're making a tape recording.
Make sure you've got the volume turned up all the way.
I hope this background noise isn't too loud.
I'm sitting here at the radar console and it puts off a lot of noise because it's got fans
in it and all kinds of little gadgets running and everything and it makes a little bit of noise.
So I think that my voice is probably drowning it out well enough
that you can probably still hear it in the background.
Well, I don't know what Bill's been up to. I haven't heard from him in quite a while.
Of course, what you've told me in the tape and your letters is mostly news to me because I haven't received any letters from him or anything in a while.
He mentioned in his last letter that he was going to send a tape and some slides to me.
But it takes an awful long time for his mail to get to me and mine to get to him.
But I expect to be hearing from him in a few more days.
Well, sorry I had to break off there. We had a target that came up there and it got in about six and a half miles from us.
It wasn't confirmed as a friendly target. I don't know what it was. It was some kind of a surface craft, a small boat of some type.
So I'll get back to finishing up the rest of this tape now.
now. I've got back five rolls of movie film that I've taken over here, three rolls I took up in
Hong Kong and the other two I shot in Da Nang and around the ship here. I've got two more out yet
and I should be getting them back in about a week or so. I ran out of movie film here on the ship
so I've only got the roll left that I have in my camera and I hope to make that last until we stop
back in Subic Bay on our way back to the States because I want to get some
pictures of some of the stops we'll be making back to the States and our arrival
back in San Diego there in July. You mentioned in your tape that the month
was almost half over when you wrote, excuse me, when you made the tape and as
I make this tape right now, it's being the 22nd of June this month.
It's practically over.
It's not half over.
It's practically over.
And by the time you receive this tape, it'll be almost over.
These last two months have really gone fast.
I don't know where they went to.
And the time just has really been flying by.
I don't know how it can, but it's been going by pretty quick for me.

I mentioned in one of my last letters or on the last tape that I sent that due to the leave situation upon arrival back in San Diego that the duty sections would probably be down to three duty sections.
And, of course, when you get down to a small number of duty sections like that,
the liberty isn't at its best.
But since they have found out just who is going on leave and who is not,
they find that not as many people are going on leave as they expected.
So it has word out that we will be in fourth section duty.
We'll have the same duty and liberty status that we had before we left the state.
So this sounds pretty good.
I should be able to get in some good three-day weekends there.
And I hope this holds true and they don't change their mind like they do so often here.
I suppose a lot of the guys are going to hold off for Christmas time but take their leave.
Of course, I'd imagine that by the time Christmas season is over with,
just about everybody on the ship that wanted to take leave will have taken it
and then we'll be back on the ship by then.
Of course, everyone's just worrying about getting back to the States now,
and we're not looking forward, or nobody knows just exactly how long we will be back in the States,
how long we'll stay tied up to the pier.
Most of us would be contented to stay tied up there to the pier for another nine or ten months at least.
know what the shift schedule is and I don't even believe that the captain knows. We'll probably
find out a short time after we do get back in the States after we've been back for a month or so.
They'll probably start releasing a little bit of information on what our next operating schedules
and such might be. I haven't yet received a tape from Grandma and Grandpa yet nor have I received
one from Georgia May I expect if they have sent one it will probably be here
in the next couple of days as I said before mail has been real slow over here
and we haven't received any mail of past two days so I suppose if they have sent
anything it should be on its way and if not I will go ahead and make a couple
more tapes and send them on out to them but I sure would like to hear from them
Of course, they've probably been tied down and haven't had a chance to do anything.
I can understand this.
But I still look forward to hearing from everybody back home,
and I really enjoy sending these tapes home.
And I know that you all are pleased to hear Bill and my voices as well
when we do send these tapes home.
I applied for two more correspondence courses.
I believe I mentioned this once before.
I haven't got them yet I imagine they will arrive while we are in Subic Bay
which will be there in just about another eight or nine days and they'll
probably arrive then I don't have something to work on when I get back in
the state I hope to get these done in a pretty quick time and get the test over
for them so I can go on and get some more finished. It's something to occupy some of
my spare time and I find it rather interesting and enjoyable. So it's a pretty good deal.
It's not costing me any more money. It only costs $5 to enroll in it and you can have
all the courses you want. You get to keep a textbook and if for nothing else the textbooks
the textbooks that they give you are good to have, whether you get any benefits from
the course or not, just the idea that you get to keep the textbooks makes it that much
worthwhile.
I kind of laughed there in your letter when you mentioned about Bill and his little run-in
with the captain there in Da Nang while he went in there one day.
I suppose that that outfit where they're at up there in Hoi An, they are pretty lax and
lenient in some of their ways.
doing things and Bill probably thinks a lot of that over there fun games the
probably pretty carefree but he still has to be reminded every so often he is
in a service and the Marines are as well I suppose they feel it's very necessary
to use little ways to remind the troops over there
that they are in a serious situation,
and they do expect them to put forth their effort
and act like they're supposed to.
I don't suspect that he really was transferred to Da Nang
or wherever he was going to go
because of his not having a haircut
or not speaking to the officer properly.
I do imagine that after a couple more months, possibly he will be transferred somewhere else.
It just seems like it's par for the course.
I've talked to guys here on the ship who have brothers and relatives over there,
and they say that they've only been in one place for about six months,
and they transfer him to some other outfit.
From what he's told me, they don't seem to be doing too much up there.
Of course, I never was able to get too much out of him, just what they do.
He didn't relay too much information to me when he came aboard the ship that day,
just exactly what they do.
Seems like they have the Koreans there doing all the hard work for him,
and they just kind of sit back and enjoy themselves.
I enjoyed David's conversation on the tape,
and he mentioned about taking his duck out to the park.
I can just kind of picture that duck trying to get out of the water and follow him up to the car.
I remember when he took his first family out there to the park,
he was rather reluctant to take it out there, but he did give in,
and I suppose he felt just about the same way about this one.
I hope that the radio suits him pretty fine.
Actually, I'm glad to hear that he said it's working pretty fine,
and he's doing what he expected it to.
I like his little idea of his savings program that he mentioned.
He's going to put 50 cents a week in the bank, so he doesn't have to worry about it too much.
It wasn't too much money off of my back to pay for it, and as far as I'm concerned, he doesn't have to worry about it.
I wasted money in more ways than one, and I don't consider that a waste of money.
So it's nothing to me.
When I get back in the States and put on my civilian clothes,
I'm afraid I'm going to find that they don't fit me as well as I was wearing them when I left.
Of course, I've gained about 20 pounds since I came over here,
and I think the big reason why it's not that I've been eating more food than usual
because I ate three meals a day before I came over here,
but I think the idea of doing a little bit more beer drinking over here
than what I did when I was back in the States
is a pretty good reason for why I've put on the extra weight.
I don't really feel bad, nor do I think that I look bad,
but I do notice the extra weight,
and I believe I'll take most of it off by the time I do get back to the States
or after I do get back there.
I'll probably pick up some new clothes while I'm back there in San Diego
just to wear around town there and wear on liberty and wear on weekends.
So I hope I can keep the waistline down where it should be.
And while I'm on the same subject, Mother, you mentioned that the doctor recommended
that Dad go on a diet, and you figured you'd go right along with him.
And I suppose if you'd twist David's arm a little bit,
I suppose he'll go right along with you and he'll be real glad to go on a diet too.
I know David would be pretty active this summer at Boy Scout camp
and going out to the pool every day and things like this.
So he shouldn't have too much of a weight problem in that line.
Well, on the 1st of July, the armed forces get a big benefit,
one of the many benefits you get while you're here in the service.
New pay raise goes into effect.
and my pay will jump up $15 a month from $235 a month to $251 a month.
And this will be the beginning of the new fiscal year, of course,
and we have a big payday scheduled for next Friday.
I believe it will be a 16-day payday, and they'll clear all the money off the books
and calculate it and see if they made any errors on your pay records or anything
and reimburse you for it.
So I suppose I'll probably be sending some more money home then.
It actually all depends if we stop in Subic Bay or not.
I would like to buy a turntable for my high-fly equipment.
That's the only item I haven't bought.
And if I can get one there in Subic Bay, if we have a chance, I'll probably buy one there.
If I do, I don't believe I'll be sending too much money home.
But the fact remains to be seen.
But of course with the new pay rates for the armed forces, I suppose President Johnson
is working on a new tax increase bill.
It seems like they're always pulling something like that to give somebody one thing and take
away from somebody else to help pay for it.
There's more than one way around it and those politicians and government officials, they've
got pretty good ways of getting things to work their way. Of course I've heard on the
news and read in our little newspapers there that most of these political people who are
running for office have started to jump in there and pick up the votes that Bobby Kennedy
was most likely to get in these primaries in all these states.
And it just seems like no one has forgot actually what's happened yet.
And these other candidates for nomination are jumping right in there
and trying to pick up the votes.
You think it isn't really right for them to do it,
but of course they've got to get out and get their votes.
It seems like a pretty ruthless way to be a candidate for office, but this is what they have to do.
Well, tomorrow's Sunday again, and they're going to slack off on us like they always do on Sunday.
They'll give us a holiday routine, and they'll get some of the big benefits of Sunday on here.
you spend a little bit more time in our rack if we're not on watch and they'll
probably still a movie in the afternoon and have ice cream to go along with it
and popcorn yeah that's right we have popcorn here on the chip too they brought
a popcorn machine before we left the state and they sell popcorn here every
night for 10 cents a bag that's right they sell it they don't they don't give
it to you. The idea for selling a popcorn is to make some profit to help pay for the
cruise book, which I mentioned that they're going to have ready for us when we get back
in the States. So it's a little profit maker for them, and nobody really complains about
having to pay for the popcorn because it's a little fringe benefit over here. I did notice
the popcorn machine when it came on board the ship that one day. He said, you mean you
guys have popcorn? I said, yeah. I said, just like downtown, you go to a movie every night and buy
popcorn and Coke. I said, we really got it made. He said, yeah, I guess you do. So, yeah, I kind of had to laugh about that.
I'm glad to hear that the dress material arrived safe and sound. I was kind of undecided on what
selection of material to pick. I'm not really too much up on what pattern design would look
best on who and things like that. So I just decided to get it. And I thought maybe if
you wasn't satisfied with yours, you could trade it with grandma. If she wasn't satisfied
with hers, she could trade it with you or whatever the situation might be. I was with
a couple of other guys when we went in the store there in Hong Kong to buy it and they had a yard
goods area there in this department store and they had silk this pure silk and uh this girl
that waited on me she uh she's trying to get me to buy some of this silk and I believe it cost about
uh let's see I think it was 15 Hong Kong dollars a yard which made it uh
about $2.50 a yard in American money.
And not being a great connoisseur of dress material,
I do know that that is rather expensive.
I would like to have got it for you,
but I knew this would be just as well, this cotton material,
and I only hope it wasn't imported from the United States.
It would be kind of an ironic thing.
But most of these foreigners over here, they like to get you to spend more money than what you intend to do.
And you just kind of have to watch out for them.
It's rather funny after you get used to it.
You go in some of these shops and these stores and these people, they want you to buy this and they want you to buy that.
And I actually get a lot of fun out of turning them down and saying no to them.
Because you can't do this back in the United States.
Of course, a lot of these merchants, they wouldn't put such a big scene on with you to get you to buy things from them and such.
But in the United States, you couldn't be so stern and strict with these people when they try to really put it on you.
They get you to buy some of their merchandise.
But over here, you can get away with it and you can tell them no.
And you can tell them a few other things, too.
and there's nothing much they can do about it.
I don't imagine it makes for too good foreign relations,
but that's too bad.
I've got the attitude that everybody over here
likes to take advantage of the sailors
and the military personnel,
and they're out to take all the money from them if they can.
Everybody over here seems to have a hand in the sailors' pocket
trying to get a little bit of money out of there,
and the guys just got to watch out for them.
and learn to say no to these people.
Well, things up here have been pretty quiet this past week.
Just about the everyday routine has been taking place here on the ship.
Our radar and our electronic gear here is still up.
We haven't had any casualties with it.
The gun mounts are still in operating order.
So things are going along pretty smooth.
Well, I just about reached the end of this side of the tape,
and I believe I'm at a loss for words to fill out the other side.
So I'll sign off here and tell everyone at home hello and goodbye in the same breath,
and I'll be waiting to hear again from everyone
and be looking forward to another tape from you.
So so long for now.
