...WITH A SENSE OF DUTY...

[Photo: Group photo — Radarman First Class Allen R. Melton with Admiral Hyland, LTJG Clyde Lassen, MR Lassen's Co-Pilot, and two rescued aviators from USS America, all standing together]

...With a sense of Duty...emblematic of the dedicated and professional services
rendered by USS JOUETT in the Tonkin Gulf is the performance of Radarman First
Class Allen R. Melton, pictured above with Admiral Hyland, Commander-In-Chief,
U.S. Pacific Fleet, Medal of Honor Nominee LTJG Clyde Lassen, MR Lassen's
Co-Pilot, and two rescued aviators from the USS AMERICA. On the night of 19 June,
an aircraft from the USS AMERICA was brought down deep in enemy territory. The
scene of the crash was pinpointed by RD1 Melton in less than one minute, and a
rescue helicopter, piloted by LTJG Lassen was vectored to the scene. Despite heavy
enemy concentrations of troops and ground fire in the area, a successful rescue was
effected. For his incredible bravery under fire, LTJG Lassen was nominated for the
nation's highest award for his role in this COMDESRON ONE-JOUETT SAR.

1968-07-11.label: Tape 8, Side 1 — Mike Ducy
1968-07-11.attribution: Audio cassette recording, Tape 8, Side 1 — Mike Ducy. Transcribed by OpenAI Whisper. Ducy Family Archives

segments.text: Hello Mother, Dad and David. Well, here I am again. This is Thursday the 11th of July.
And at this present time our ship is underway for Pearl Harbor. Our last stop over here was Guam on the 5th of July.
So it's been a pretty long stretch of sea here between these two ports.
We're expected to arrive in Pearl Harbor Saturday the 13th about 8 o'clock in the morning.
We should be there for about 10 hours to take care of some major evolutions like having a customs check, picking up some stores, of course fuel on water.
And we'll also receive mail while we're in there.
While we are in Pearl Harbor, Liberty calls should go about 12 o'clock for those of us who are in the Liberty section.
and give us a chance to go and buy a few last souvenirs there
and also make one last stop at the EM Club
before we get underway and arrive back in San Diego about four days later.
As I mentioned before, we were in Guam on the 5th,
and I received your 26th of June letter then,
and I was real glad to hear from you.
I imagine I'll be getting another letter from you in Pearl Harbor.
I certainly hope so. I would like to say that I hope this tape does reach you before I arrive back in the state.
Our plans are to arrive in San Diego at 10 o'clock the morning of Thursday, July the 18th, which is just one week from now.
It will all be over with. And I plan to call you that evening about 6 o'clock your time.
And if I do not have a watch, if I'm not on the duty section or whatever,
I will try to call you about 6 o'clock your time.
And I hope you have received this tape by then.
Well, I'll give you a little rundown of our activities that we have taken place here since I last wrote to you.
On the 30th of June, we were relieved up on SAR Station by the USS Horn, which is DLG-30.
a ship identical to ours, except just a little bit newer.
And we left the area about 9 o'clock that night and proceeded to Subic Bay.
We arrived there in Subic on the 2nd of July,
and we had to offload about 250 rounds of 5-inch ammunition,
which we didn't use up while we were there in the combat zone,
which is a pretty good thing.
and we offloaded some small arms ammunition, 50 caliber machine gun ammunition and other
various types of projectiles. Of course during the whole process of offloading the ammunition
it rained on us and I'm not kidding I don't believe I've ever been so soaked in all my life
from rain but later on the rain cleared up and we had liberty call about 12 o'clock and I got
away from the ship about 1 o'clock and went over and bought a few last items.
I bought some movie films so I could take some movie pictures here on the ship.
And we got away from there that night about 7 o'clock and proceeded on to Guam.
On the 4th of July here on the ship, which was on a Thursday just one week ago,
we held a 21-gun salute.
The ship was underway, of course, out here in the Pacific Ocean somewhere.
And we held a 21-gun salute, and they read the Declaration of Independence during the noon hour.
And later on in the afternoon, we had what we call a fan tail and flight deck frolic.
up on the uh helicopter flight deck they set up chairs and a charcoal grill and everything and
they cooked uh hamburgers and we had some of the entertainers here on the ship get out their
musical instruments and provide some music and it was a rather informal affair and uh it was a
pretty good thing to kind of let us know it was the fourth and a holiday also.
And then later on that night when it got dark, we did have our own impromptu
fireworks, which consisted of shooting illuminating flares out of a gun, which
these flares they use are distress signals that if a boat goes down or a plane should happen to
go down they shoot these flares up and they something but a red or a green tracer shell
that flies through the air and you can spot it it's a fairly colorful it's nothing like the
sky rockets and everything else that they have at the fourth of july ceremonies back home but
But at least there was a little bit of fireworks there that we had.
And that wound up the Fourth of July ceremonies here aboard the ship.
The next day was the fifth, and we arrived in Guam.
We were there for a real short time, about six hours, actually.
And we loaded, excuse me, we took on some fuel and water, and we picked up mail there.
And they gave liberty to the guys who were not in the duty section.
I happen to be in the duty section, and it's a fairly good thing because they only got about two and a half hours of liberty while they were there anyway.
And in Guam, it's rather hard to get around because the base is so large and transportation is very hard to come by.
So it didn't satisfy me at all because I had duty and had to stay aboard the ship.
Well, as I said before in one of my last letters or tapes, I don't remember which,
we had planned to cross the equator on the 10th of this month, and that we did.
Let me tell you, I've never seen anything like this before.
This ceremony that they had and some of the things that they put us through,
I can hardly describe it, but the best way that I can describe it is the 75-foot movie film
that I shot which I'm gonna be very anxious to get back and take a look at
is showing some of the guys going through the ceremony and everything we
crossed the equator about nine o'clock that morning and they held a ceremony
till about one o'clock that afternoon because they had about 400 people they
had to send through there and like I said before I just can't describe what
it was like it was uh a lot of fun after it was over with to get to watch some of the other guys
go through there and at the same moment as we were crossing excuse me as we were crossing the
equator we crossed the 180th meridian which is the international state line and uh i'll explain
something about this this might be a little bit confusing but we have had two wednesdays this week
the first Wednesday of course we had the shellback ceremonies for crossing the equator
and the second Wednesday was just another Wednesday this week because when you cross
the international date line going back to the states you have to repeat
one day in the week which means if you cross it on a Wednesday you have to
to repeat that Wednesday again in order to conform to the time zones and the other time
areas back in the state when you arrive back there.
Of course, when we came over here, when we crossed the date line, we skipped one day.
We came over and crossed it on a Monday and the next day was automatically a Wednesday.
So this sounds rather confusing, but this is the way they did it.
So this has been an eight day week for us rather than seven days.
So our Wednesday yesterday was nothing like the first Wednesday of this week.
It was just a regular day out here at sea like it has been all day today.
The sea is fairly calm out here.
It's rather choppy, a little bit rough.
It doesn't seem to be bothering anybody too much.
It does get fairly rough between this stretch here, between these two ports of Guam and
Pearl Harbor, and we might be seeing a little rougher seas between Pearl Harbor and San
Diego like we did when we came over here.
Well, as you know, there are no certainties here in the Navy, and I found a very good
example of this the other day.
actually was last week, the 3rd of July,
myself and another F.T. were assigned to work down in the storeroom
to take inventory because the supply department had their hands full
and they needed some extra people to help them out.
So for five days, I got to play storekeeper
between the hours of 8 p.m. in the evening
and six o'clock the next morning so this is a 10-hour stretch of working at night
and we did get to sleep for the rest of the day i admit that i got more sleep this way than i ever
have before but it was not the most interesting of work or anything like that it was a little
break from the normal routine but it still wasn't something that i particularly cared for
but it's just a perfect example as i said before that you don't know what's going to happen from
one day to the next and they're always coming around with some new job for you to do or some
new idea that they come up with and uh i was pretty dissatisfied with it when i was first
notified that I had been volunteered for it but I got over it as everyone does
and I got used to it and everything it's one storeroom that we had to work down in
I'm telling you it must be about 125 degrees down there it was really really hot
and I think I lost about five pounds of weight down there that night while I was working down
there believe it or not but uh they've got the most of the job over with now they let us go
um about five days ago we uh finished up down there for the last night
and we're back on a normal daily routine right now of an eight hour a day job
so things are starting to shape up pretty good and of course everybody's looking forward to
getting back to the state.
They're making final preparations here on the ship
by cleaning up certain areas, painting out and everything.
Of course, Gunnery Division is also doing their share of the work.
We have most of our topside area painted out,
and tomorrow afternoon we plan to paint out the rest of the O3 level,
which is the upper deck that we have to take care of,
which is exposed to the weather.
and we plan to paint out the rest of the deck up there so it'll be all nice and clean and sharp
preparing for our arrival back in san diego and here on the ship they're making all kinds of plans
for homecoming activities when the ship pulls back in they plan to buy some uh colored balloons
in pearl harbor and fill them with helium and release them as the ship is pulling through the
Harbor back in San Diego to advertise to everybody that the Jewett has returned from a very successful
mission over here in the western Pacific.
And, of course, the captain sent home his newsletter, which I suppose you've got by
now, informing everybody of some of the proceedings that were going to take place as the ship
arrived back in the state.
and I'm sure it'll be a very happy occasion and very colorful as well
because there are to be two other ships returned at the same time with us.
So I suppose there'll be quite a crowd of people down there on the pier waiting for us when we pull back in.
As you've probably noticed by now, I've enclosed a money order in the envelope with this tape
and you can go ahead and put it in the bank with the rest of my money.
I also had a $30 money order from Bill that he sent me to pay off this long-standing debt that he's had.
I sent this MPC back to him to have him buy a money order and send it to me.
And my last letter that I received from him, he sent the money order back.
And I'm not sending it along because I might want to use the extra money in Pearl Harbor
to buy some final items before we leave there and head back for the States.
So I'm holding on to it, and if necessary, I can send it on after our next payday,
which will be the day before we arrive back in the States.
I read in your letter that you mentioned Bill was back in Da Nang
for 30 days' tour of meth duty.
He also mentioned this in his letter that he sent to me.
He gave no indication of why he had been sent there,
but I can think of a few good reasons myself, and I'm sure that you can too.
But I suppose we'll be hearing from him soon,
and he'll probably say that his tour of Massoudi is over with
and he's being sent somewhere else.
But I'd like to see him stay there in the area of Da Nang
because that is a fairly safe area there.
It's one of the largest cities in South Vietnam.
Actually, it's the second largest city there, and it's fairly safe.
If he's right in the military premises there of the city,
it shouldn't be a very bad duty.
But I'm sure that whatever they are making him do there,
I'm sure that he's getting along with it all right,
and he's learning to accept it.
That's about all you can do.
Of course, myself, I really don't care what they do to me from day to day
because it just gets one more day shorter while I'm in here,
and it's just one more day that I won't have to do over in my short career while I'm in here.
Do you remember this buddy of mine that I went to aid school with,
and I had mentioned before that I saw him over here in Guam when we came over here
and stopped in Guam the first time.
You know, I went aboard the ship that he was on.
Well, he had got married last summer,
and he's been aboard this LST over here for just about a year.
He came on active duty the same time I did.
And they have a policy here in the Navy that if a man is married,
he only has to spend one year of overseas duty and this is what this is
qualified as overseas duty because he's in an overseas port so when I last
talked to him there in Guam which was about five months ago he was really
hoping to get a transfer to get out of there pretty bad because he would like
to get some stateside duty so he could bring his wife up to the west coast so i received a letter
from him here the other day and uh he said that he had got a transfer to a ship which was home
ported in san diego and that he was due to get 30 days leave in september and then report to the
ship in october there in san diego and so he mentioned there possibly be a chance we might
be able to see each other back there and I'm pretty glad for him that he did get the transfer
of duty because over there in Guam it's actually not the best of duty and the ship that they have
there are these LSTs. I'm sure the dad knows what I'm talking about about an LST because
they're the lower quality of ship that the Navy has and the one that he was on was
I believe the oldest LST that the Navy still has.
It was built before the war,
and believe you me,
it's not the most attractive ship that I've ever seen.
So he's probably pretty glad to be getting off of it,
and I hope that we have a chance to see each other
when he gets back in San Diego
and he gets assigned to his new ship.
Well, David, I hope you enjoyed your stay at Boy Scout Camp.
this summer and that you had a lot of fun and you learned a lot about scouts
and found out just exactly what they have to offer there for you. I know that
me and Bill we had a lot of fun the times that we went out there and I'm
sure you liked it real well and you're probably looking forward to going again
next summer. I suppose that within another week or so summer school will
probably be over for you and I hope you did a real good job in it this summer and learned a few
things that you didn't pick up last year in school and uh prepared yourself a little bit better for
the school would start this fall you know summer vacation is almost halfway over with I actually
hate to mention it but I'm sure you're quite aware of it and before too long it'll be time to go back
to school again and get in that everyday routine of getting up every morning and going to school
so I hope you did pick up a little bit of extra knowledge there in summer school this year,
and that you'll be able to do a little bit better in school this fall,
because, you know, the school doesn't get any easier as it goes along.
It gets a little bit harder, and you have to remember the things from the previous years,
and it's quite necessary to know all this so you can get yourself all the way through grade school
and then go on into high school because it's very important.
I don't know whether you realize this or not,
but it's very important to study hard and try to remember all you can
about what they teach you in school because you will use it at one time or another.
In the last paper I received from Georgia May,
which has actually been the only one I've received from her,
I mentioned this a while back in one of my letters.
she mentioned that they would be anxious to see the ship when it arrives back in San Diego
and that they would most likely be there well I don't know whether she realized that this would
be on a weekday or not and of course I mentioned on the return tape that I sent her that
if they couldn't make it it was not going to be no heartbreak to me but of course I would be glad
to see them there, so I don't know what they're going to do about it or not, whether they're
going to be there or whatever the case might be.
I explained to them that there might be a chance that I had duty that first night in
San Diego, and it would be practically useless for them to come there because I would not
be able to leave the ship.
Of course, they could come on and visit for a while, and then, of course, they'd have
to go on back.
but I don't know what they're going to do about it.
I expect I will receive an answer from them in Pearl Harbor
when we get there and receive mail.
I will send a letter out to her this evening
and explain just a little bit more about our schedule for getting in there.
And I really don't expect to see her there.
It's not going to be any hard luck story as far as I'm concerned
because they don't come.
but being in the middle of the week there like it is on a Thursday,
I really don't think that they'll be able to make it down.
So I'm planning on calling them the first night in there after I call you
and see if they're going to be home that weekend,
and I will probably go up and see them the first weekend in there
because I believe the next weekend while I'm in there I'll have duty over the weekend,
either on Saturday or Sunday.
so it's not going to be all liberty and fun and games when we get back in here
because we've got the usual duty sections and everything that we have to stay in.
Of course, everyone was fairly upset this morning when they came out on the plan of the day
that our liberty upon returning to the state would commence at 1530 every day,
which is 3.30, which they felt that they were really giving us something great
because they're giving us early liberty.
Well, you know how early that is?
That is an hour earlier than what we usually have liberty back in the States.
Liberty usually commences at 16.30, which is 4.30 in the afternoon.
And they really felt they was really giving us something great.
It doesn't make much sense to me or to any of the other guys here on the ship
because most of the other fellas have been on other ships that I've talked to,
and they said upon their return from six months at sea,
they usually were on ships which gave liberty at 12 o'clock every day at noon.
And this doesn't make much sense to anyone.
I don't know why they're doing it like this,
because I figure that after ships have been gone from the States for six months
and having some of the rotten liberty that we had over here,
it just doesn't make sense why they can't give you some good liberty when you do return to your
home port but that question is not for me to answer nor is it for anyone else to it's the
people that make the rules that know all the answers and that's one of the many reasons why
a lot of guys don't particularly care for this outfit and that's one reason why i'm not really
crazy about it either the only thing i can say is when uh i get ready to take leave and i've got

I just let some of the time pass and see just exactly what happens

Well, I see my tape is getting fairly short.
I don't think it's quite ready to run out yet, but I'm about ready to run out of conversation.
And I'll be signing off right at this point.
Don't forget I'll call you on the evening of Thursday, July the 18th, about 6 o'clock your time.
And I hope you do get this tape before then.
If not, you can always listen to it after I call you on the phone.
Sorry there hasn't been too much news to report this time on the tape, but we haven't seen any action.
we've been out here all alone by ourselves and there hasn't really been too much going on with
the exception of the equator crossing and uh i'll be real anxious to get that film back and uh i
might go ahead and send it on home to you and you might have a chance to get a movie projector to
take a look at it and if not i might have purchased a projector by the time and uh i might send it on
home with you too so you can see some of these movies that i'm taking over here but in any case
i'll be seeing you later on the next time i talk to you will be the night that we
arrive back in the states so so long for now
Thank you.
Thank you.

1968-07-11.text: Hello Mother, Dad and David. Well, here I am again. This is Thursday the 11th of July. And at this present time our ship is underway for Pearl Harbor. Our last stop over here was Guam on the 5th of July. So it's been a pretty long stretch of sea here between these two ports. We're expected to arrive in Pearl Harbor Saturday the 13th about 8 o'clock in the morning. We should be there for about 10 hours to take care of some major evolutions like having a customs check, picking up some stores, of course fuel on water. And we'll also receive mail while we're in there. While we are in Pearl Harbor, Liberty calls should go about 12 o'clock for those of us who are in the Liberty section. and give us a chance to go and buy a few last souvenirs there and also make one last stop at the EM Club before we get underway and arrive back in San Diego about four days later. As I mentioned before, we were in Guam on the 5th, and I received your 26th of June letter then, and I was real glad to hear from you. I imagine I'll be getting another letter from you in Pearl Harbor. I certainly hope so. I would like to say that I hope this tape does reach you before I arrive back in the state. Our plans are to arrive in San Diego at 10 o'clock the morning of Thursday, July the 18th, which is just one week from now. It will all be over with. And I plan to call you that evening about 6 o'clock your time. And if I do not have a watch, if I'm not on the duty section or whatever, I will try to call you about 6 o'clock your time. And I hope you have received this tape by then. Well, I'll give you a little rundown of our activities that we have taken place here since I last wrote to you. On the 30th of June, we were relieved up on SAR Station by the USS Horn, which is DLG-30. a ship identical to ours, except just a little bit newer. And we left the area about 9 o'clock that night and proceeded to Subic Bay. We arrived there in Subic on the 2nd of July, and we had to offload about 250 rounds of 5-inch ammunition, which we didn't use up while we were there in the combat zone, which is a pretty good thing. and we offloaded some small arms ammunition, 50 caliber machine gun ammunition and other various types of projectiles. Of course during the whole process of offloading the ammunition it rained on us and I'm not kidding I don't believe I've ever been so soaked in all my life from rain but later on the rain cleared up and we had liberty call about 12 o'clock and I got away from the ship about 1 o'clock and went over and bought a few last items. I bought some movie films so I could take some movie pictures here on the ship. And we got away from there that night about 7 o'clock and proceeded on to Guam. On the 4th of July here on the ship, which was on a Thursday just one week ago, we held a 21-gun salute. The ship was underway, of course, out here in the Pacific Ocean somewhere. And we held a 21-gun salute, and they read the Declaration of Independence during the noon hour. And later on in the afternoon, we had what we call a fan tail and flight deck frolic. up on the uh helicopter flight deck they set up chairs and a charcoal grill and everything and they cooked uh hamburgers and we had some of the entertainers here on the ship get out their musical instruments and provide some music and it was a rather informal affair and uh it was a pretty good thing to kind of let us know it was the fourth and a holiday also. And then later on that night when it got dark, we did have our own impromptu fireworks, which consisted of shooting illuminating flares out of a gun, which these flares they use are distress signals that if a boat goes down or a plane should happen to go down they shoot these flares up and they something but a red or a green tracer shell that flies through the air and you can spot it it's a fairly colorful it's nothing like the sky rockets and everything else that they have at the fourth of july ceremonies back home but But at least there was a little bit of fireworks there that we had. And that wound up the Fourth of July ceremonies here aboard the ship. The next day was the fifth, and we arrived in Guam. We were there for a real short time, about six hours, actually. And we loaded, excuse me, we took on some fuel and water, and we picked up mail there. And they gave liberty to the guys who were not in the duty section. I happen to be in the duty section, and it's a fairly good thing because they only got about two and a half hours of liberty while they were there anyway. And in Guam, it's rather hard to get around because the base is so large and transportation is very hard to come by. So it didn't satisfy me at all because I had duty and had to stay aboard the ship. Well, as I said before in one of my last letters or tapes, I don't remember which, we had planned to cross the equator on the 10th of this month, and that we did. Let me tell you, I've never seen anything like this before. This ceremony that they had and some of the things that they put us through, I can hardly describe it, but the best way that I can describe it is the 75-foot movie film that I shot which I'm gonna be very anxious to get back and take a look at is showing some of the guys going through the ceremony and everything we crossed the equator about nine o'clock that morning and they held a ceremony till about one o'clock that afternoon because they had about 400 people they had to send through there and like I said before I just can't describe what it was like it was uh a lot of fun after it was over with to get to watch some of the other guys go through there and at the same moment as we were crossing excuse me as we were crossing the equator we crossed the 180th meridian which is the international state line and uh i'll explain something about this this might be a little bit confusing but we have had two wednesdays this week the first Wednesday of course we had the shellback ceremonies for crossing the equator and the second Wednesday was just another Wednesday this week because when you cross the international date line going back to the states you have to repeat one day in the week which means if you cross it on a Wednesday you have to to repeat that Wednesday again in order to conform to the time zones and the other time areas back in the state when you arrive back there. Of course, when we came over here, when we crossed the date line, we skipped one day. We came over and crossed it on a Monday and the next day was automatically a Wednesday. So this sounds rather confusing, but this is the way they did it. So this has been an eight day week for us rather than seven days. So our Wednesday yesterday was nothing like the first Wednesday of this week. It was just a regular day out here at sea like it has been all day today. The sea is fairly calm out here. It's rather choppy, a little bit rough. It doesn't seem to be bothering anybody too much. It does get fairly rough between this stretch here, between these two ports of Guam and Pearl Harbor, and we might be seeing a little rougher seas between Pearl Harbor and San Diego like we did when we came over here. Well, as you know, there are no certainties here in the Navy, and I found a very good example of this the other day. actually was last week, the 3rd of July, myself and another F.T. were assigned to work down in the storeroom to take inventory because the supply department had their hands full and they needed some extra people to help them out. So for five days, I got to play storekeeper between the hours of 8 p.m. in the evening and six o'clock the next morning so this is a 10-hour stretch of working at night and we did get to sleep for the rest of the day i admit that i got more sleep this way than i ever have before but it was not the most interesting of work or anything like that it was a little break from the normal routine but it still wasn't something that i particularly cared for but it's just a perfect example as i said before that you don't know what's going to happen from one day to the next and they're always coming around with some new job for you to do or some new idea that they come up with and uh i was pretty dissatisfied with it when i was first notified that I had been volunteered for it but I got over it as everyone does and I got used to it and everything it's one storeroom that we had to work down in I'm telling you it must be about 125 degrees down there it was really really hot and I think I lost about five pounds of weight down there that night while I was working down there believe it or not but uh they've got the most of the job over with now they let us go um about five days ago we uh finished up down there for the last night and we're back on a normal daily routine right now of an eight hour a day job so things are starting to shape up pretty good and of course everybody's looking forward to getting back to the state. They're making final preparations here on the ship by cleaning up certain areas, painting out and everything. Of course, Gunnery Division is also doing their share of the work. We have most of our topside area painted out, and tomorrow afternoon we plan to paint out the rest of the O3 level, which is the upper deck that we have to take care of, which is exposed to the weather. and we plan to paint out the rest of the deck up there so it'll be all nice and clean and sharp preparing for our arrival back in san diego and here on the ship they're making all kinds of plans for homecoming activities when the ship pulls back in they plan to buy some uh colored balloons in pearl harbor and fill them with helium and release them as the ship is pulling through the Harbor back in San Diego to advertise to everybody that the Jewett has returned from a very successful mission over here in the western Pacific. And, of course, the captain sent home his newsletter, which I suppose you've got by now, informing everybody of some of the proceedings that were going to take place as the ship arrived back in the state. and I'm sure it'll be a very happy occasion and very colorful as well because there are to be two other ships returned at the same time with us. So I suppose there'll be quite a crowd of people down there on the pier waiting for us when we pull back in. As you've probably noticed by now, I've enclosed a money order in the envelope with this tape and you can go ahead and put it in the bank with the rest of my money. I also had a $30 money order from Bill that he sent me to pay off this long-standing debt that he's had. I sent this MPC back to him to have him buy a money order and send it to me. And my last letter that I received from him, he sent the money order back. And I'm not sending it along because I might want to use the extra money in Pearl Harbor to buy some final items before we leave there and head back for the States. So I'm holding on to it, and if necessary, I can send it on after our next payday, which will be the day before we arrive back in the States. I read in your letter that you mentioned Bill was back in Da Nang for 30 days' tour of meth duty. He also mentioned this in his letter that he sent to me. He gave no indication of why he had been sent there, but I can think of a few good reasons myself, and I'm sure that you can too. But I suppose we'll be hearing from him soon, and he'll probably say that his tour of Massoudi is over with and he's being sent somewhere else. But I'd like to see him stay there in the area of Da Nang because that is a fairly safe area there. It's one of the largest cities in South Vietnam. Actually, it's the second largest city there, and it's fairly safe. If he's right in the military premises there of the city, it shouldn't be a very bad duty. But I'm sure that whatever they are making him do there, I'm sure that he's getting along with it all right, and he's learning to accept it. That's about all you can do. Of course, myself, I really don't care what they do to me from day to day because it just gets one more day shorter while I'm in here, and it's just one more day that I won't have to do over in my short career while I'm in here. Do you remember this buddy of mine that I went to aid school with, and I had mentioned before that I saw him over here in Guam when we came over here and stopped in Guam the first time. You know, I went aboard the ship that he was on. Well, he had got married last summer, and he's been aboard this LST over here for just about a year. He came on active duty the same time I did. And they have a policy here in the Navy that if a man is married, he only has to spend one year of overseas duty and this is what this is qualified as overseas duty because he's in an overseas port so when I last talked to him there in Guam which was about five months ago he was really hoping to get a transfer to get out of there pretty bad because he would like to get some stateside duty so he could bring his wife up to the west coast so i received a letter from him here the other day and uh he said that he had got a transfer to a ship which was home ported in san diego and that he was due to get 30 days leave in september and then report to the ship in october there in san diego and so he mentioned there possibly be a chance we might be able to see each other back there and I'm pretty glad for him that he did get the transfer of duty because over there in Guam it's actually not the best of duty and the ship that they have there are these LSTs. I'm sure the dad knows what I'm talking about about an LST because they're the lower quality of ship that the Navy has and the one that he was on was I believe the oldest LST that the Navy still has. It was built before the war, and believe you me, it's not the most attractive ship that I've ever seen. So he's probably pretty glad to be getting off of it, and I hope that we have a chance to see each other when he gets back in San Diego and he gets assigned to his new ship. Well, David, I hope you enjoyed your stay at Boy Scout Camp. this summer and that you had a lot of fun and you learned a lot about scouts and found out just exactly what they have to offer there for you. I know that me and Bill we had a lot of fun the times that we went out there and I'm sure you liked it real well and you're probably looking forward to going again next summer. I suppose that within another week or so summer school will probably be over for you and I hope you did a real good job in it this summer and learned a few things that you didn't pick up last year in school and uh prepared yourself a little bit better for the school would start this fall you know summer vacation is almost halfway over with I actually hate to mention it but I'm sure you're quite aware of it and before too long it'll be time to go back to school again and get in that everyday routine of getting up every morning and going to school so I hope you did pick up a little bit of extra knowledge there in summer school this year, and that you'll be able to do a little bit better in school this fall, because, you know, the school doesn't get any easier as it goes along. It gets a little bit harder, and you have to remember the things from the previous years, and it's quite necessary to know all this so you can get yourself all the way through grade school and then go on into high school because it's very important. I don't know whether you realize this or not, but it's very important to study hard and try to remember all you can about what they teach you in school because you will use it at one time or another. In the last paper I received from Georgia May, which has actually been the only one I've received from her, I mentioned this a while back in one of my letters. she mentioned that they would be anxious to see the ship when it arrives back in San Diego and that they would most likely be there well I don't know whether she realized that this would be on a weekday or not and of course I mentioned on the return tape that I sent her that if they couldn't make it it was not going to be no heartbreak to me but of course I would be glad to see them there, so I don't know what they're going to do about it or not, whether they're going to be there or whatever the case might be. I explained to them that there might be a chance that I had duty that first night in San Diego, and it would be practically useless for them to come there because I would not be able to leave the ship. Of course, they could come on and visit for a while, and then, of course, they'd have to go on back. but I don't know what they're going to do about it. I expect I will receive an answer from them in Pearl Harbor when we get there and receive mail. I will send a letter out to her this evening and explain just a little bit more about our schedule for getting in there. And I really don't expect to see her there. It's not going to be any hard luck story as far as I'm concerned because they don't come. but being in the middle of the week there like it is on a Thursday, I really don't think that they'll be able to make it down. So I'm planning on calling them the first night in there after I call you and see if they're going to be home that weekend, and I will probably go up and see them the first weekend in there because I believe the next weekend while I'm in there I'll have duty over the weekend, either on Saturday or Sunday. so it's not going to be all liberty and fun and games when we get back in here because we've got the usual duty sections and everything that we have to stay in. Of course, everyone was fairly upset this morning when they came out on the plan of the day that our liberty upon returning to the state would commence at 1530 every day, which is 3.30, which they felt that they were really giving us something great because they're giving us early liberty. Well, you know how early that is? That is an hour earlier than what we usually have liberty back in the States. Liberty usually commences at 16.30, which is 4.30 in the afternoon. And they really felt they was really giving us something great. It doesn't make much sense to me or to any of the other guys here on the ship because most of the other fellas have been on other ships that I've talked to, and they said upon their return from six months at sea, they usually were on ships which gave liberty at 12 o'clock every day at noon. And this doesn't make much sense to anyone. I don't know why they're doing it like this, because I figure that after ships have been gone from the States for six months and having some of the rotten liberty that we had over here, it just doesn't make sense why they can't give you some good liberty when you do return to your home port but that question is not for me to answer nor is it for anyone else to it's the people that make the rules that know all the answers and that's one of the many reasons why a lot of guys don't particularly care for this outfit and that's one reason why i'm not really crazy about it either the only thing i can say is when uh i get ready to take leave and i've got the days earned that i want to take i certainly hope that they don't give me any static about that because some of these guys that are taking leave upon arriving back in the states have had to rather fight for it or didn't get as many days as they wanted to and that's one reason why i'm holding off on my leave i figure i'll ask for leave when not too many other people are wanting it and i shouldn't have too much trouble in getting it i mentioned just a few sentences earlier about our liberty over here in west pack being so bad actually there's some statistics i suppose you might have read this in the captain's letter before but uh out of the six months that we were over here we spent approximately one month in port. Now we actually saw two good liberty ports over here. That was Yokosuka, Japan, and Hong Kong. Now in Japan, we were there for 10 days, and I think this is a little bit better liberty than what we had in Hong Kong. In Hong Kong, we were only there for about four days, and the rest of our time was in port over here. We spent in Subic Bay. We spent quite a bit of time in there, I'd say the longest time we ever spent in there was about four days in one stretch. We spent a lot of one and two day stops in there after we had returned from combat duty up there in the Gulf and then after we had returned from Liberty Port. Of course we had about five days in Pearl Harbor which I'd say was also some of the better over here and it hasn't really been a cruise which has been for excuse me which has been for Liberty like a lot of ships come over here for it all I meant I did get to see some of the foreign soil over here and I did I am satisfied that I did see as much of it as I wanted to I don't particularly care to want to come back again. I thought that I would like to when I first came over here. I thought I'd like to make another one of these cruises, but I've seen all the foreigners and all the foreign soil that I want to see for a while. I think I've saw my share of it, and I don't particularly care about coming back over here again. As far as I know, from what I've heard, the Jewett is not scheduled to come back over here at least for another year and that means that'll be about the time when I get out but I tell you one thing right now this ship does get underway to leave the States again in January I won't be a bit surprised at all because that's the way they run things here in the Navy and it won't surprise me one bit at all if we do get underway again in January or February and come back over here. This could happen very easily. A lot of people don't look at it that way. Of course, they're not thinking in those terms. They're not thinking ahead like that. But I see no reason at all from my viewpoint why the ship wouldn't be able to come back over again that soon. Most ships, they come back to the States and stay in the States for six months, and they come back over again for six months, and then back home again for six months and back over again, and this could be the same schedule that we might follow. It's something that all remains to be seen, and, of course, only time will tell. And that's about the best way to find out. I just let some of the time pass and see just exactly what happens because there's no such thing as a sure thing here in the Navy, and we're always going to have to sit back and just take it easy for a while while we are back in the States and see what they come up with next. Of course, there's always the remote possibility that I might get transferred off of this ship for when it's coming back over here again. If the need arises for an FT on some other ship or whatever the case might be, this happens occasionally with people who have a fairly short time left in the Navy. Of course, I'll only have about a year left. As of the day the ship ties up in San Diego upon returning, I'll actually have just less than 13 months, and it would be a real nice case to let a guy like myself sit back in the States for about four or five months and then put him on a ship that's bound over here and let him finish out his last six or seven months in the service over here and then send him back to the States for another month and a half, and then he gets out. This could happen very easily. It's been done before and is being done right now. There have been a few guys transferred off of our ship. While they've been over here, they have got down to the point where they have a very short time left in, and they transfer them to ships that are already over here or some guys are getting back into states and getting transferred to other ships which are getting underway within a couple of months or so. So they can make another cruise over here. Navy's always thinking of you. They like to have you see as much of this ocean out here as possible and they're not going to disappoint you in any way if that's what you want to do. Well, I see my tape is getting fairly short. I don't think it's quite ready to run out yet, but I'm about ready to run out of conversation. And I'll be signing off right at this point. Don't forget I'll call you on the evening of Thursday, July the 18th, about 6 o'clock your time. And I hope you do get this tape before then. If not, you can always listen to it after I call you on the phone. Sorry there hasn't been too much news to report this time on the tape, but we haven't seen any action. we've been out here all alone by ourselves and there hasn't really been too much going on with the exception of the equator crossing and uh i'll be real anxious to get that film back and uh i might go ahead and send it on home to you and you might have a chance to get a movie projector to take a look at it and if not i might have purchased a projector by the time and uh i might send it on home with you too so you can see some of these movies that i'm taking over here but in any case i'll be seeing you later on the next time i talk to you will be the night that we arrive back in the states so so long for now Thank you. Thank you.

1968-07-13.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-07-13.text:
13 July 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got your tape yesterday and really enjoyed it.

I'm glad to hear you think that this tape recorder will be a good buy. I didn't really want an one for A.C. power only because of the power change over here. And I can always get a hold of batteries for it.

I also got those slides you took, they were really good. You said in your tape that the chopper got their ass's kicked when they went in land. Boy I bet those chopper guys were really shitting their skivvies when the V.C. started giving them hell.

You should be back in the states by the time you get this letter you lucky fucker. Now I've got only 226 more days left over here. And have been here for 167 days.

I asked for 30 more days of mess duty, this mess duty is really skating and the time goes by fast.

We've had 2 "red alerts" last week but nothing has come of them. Rockets were spotted taking off but they weren't coming our way. They hit the air strip and Marble Mt. about 5 miles away.

This morning at 4 AM while we were going to pick up the gooks that work in our mess hall the jeep driver fell asleep and ran off the road down a 50 ft. embankment. The 2 guys in the jeep wasn't hurt, but sure had the shit scared out of them.

Its been fairly quiet around here the past few nites, but we are expecting to be hit soon.

I'll be getting a tape made and sent off to you soon.

Well thats about all from over here in Nam, I keep you informed if anything big comes up. You know like pulling all the U.S. Troops out or something like that. ha ha!

Bye for now and take care.

Little Brother
Bill USMC.

segments.text: I went to South Bend and I was in the camp.
So, I went to the camp and I was in the camp.
I'm getting on a car from doing anything next year because of the pandemic.
Next year is only going to camp, you know, around 4th of July.
Camp is, so if I'm getting on a van next year, so I'll probably get to the next year.
I'll have some fun and get $10 worth of stuff.

They thought for a while yesterday morning that they would probably call off the Cardinals ballgame in St. Louis because they had some awful heavy rain in Chicago yesterday morning and also heavy wind. It's now about 9 o'clock here on Sunday evening, the 30th of June. And I just looked out the window. It's not completely dark yet, but it looks like it's clouding up back over in the west. And so we could get some rain tonight here. Matter of fact, the weatherman did predict possible showers for some time today or tonight. Well, I know a trip home from down there Back to San Diego is not going to be too long, I suppose. Actually, after you leave Subic Bay, you'll probably, oh, you could stop at Guam and then Hawaii. It don't make any difference. The time that you're coming is going to seem like it's pretty slow coming back, but as you mentioned, your time has really flew down there, and Bill says the same thing, that time has really went fast for him, And, of course, time does go when you're not disgusted with everything. I know that everybody gets disgusted somewhat in the service, but it could be a lot worse. And so far, everything's went along real good for both you boys. Bo was out this afternoon. He watched the ballgame. The Cubs and Cardinals was on Bo Springfield in Champaign this afternoon. and we wanted him to go down to Stony Brook, but he didn't want to go. So he stayed here and watched the rest of the ballgame. I guess he stayed and watched the rest of the ballgame. I told him he could just close the front door when he left. So he was gone when we got home. So I guess he probably just watched the ballgame and then went on. He seems like he's kind of lost, But then, anybody that don't have anything to do, it gets real easy to feel like you're lost. I was quite amazed at your statement about the new race, the new race races and the pain Thank you for your voice. Thank you. You're welcome. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. what the government should do, what the government needs to do, whether it's development of you and I and everybody else, whether it's money and materials and everything else, if you and I would have to pay for it one way or the other, whether we like it or not, we still have to pay for it. But if you didn't like it, you didn't like it, you didn't believe it, the people would think that. Right. Of course, it's just one vicious circle. The money goes round and around, and the lover rubs off in your hand or mine. We do get some of the satisfaction of having some of the better things that money will buy. But there again, it's just the way life goes. I was just in the paper. I was raised over the last year or four months. That doesn't sound quite like much, but people are quick to get down. I must say their income has increased by 4.5% over the last year, where they're getting deeper in the hole. And of course, you know, these people out there, it's an increase in the amount of money, especially those on Social Security or retirement or any other kind. That's fixed by three, eight years, or what they put into a retirement fund. Those people really get hurt. I didn't know what the answer is. I just thought it might be or they probably would. Well it looks like about my share of this paper has run out so I think I'll sign off for now. Leave it out for a paper you'll notice any three-year cheats down the tolly. Mine should be on 3-2-3-5 and that should be up to you tomorrow. So good luck to you. Take care of yourself. Be careful and as soon as you get back into the streets but give us a call because we're on the biggest part of the time. So goodbye for now, Mike, and be careful. Hello, Mike. I really goofed on the last tape, and I don't know whether this tape is going to be any better or not. It seems to be a bad one. I'm sure that was already explained. So don't give up. Keep on playing. Your biggest part of the conversation, I'm sure, This is the first day of July. As your dad said, I probably would finish the tape off last night, but I wasn't in the mood for much conversation. I couldn't think of anything to say. and I had my mind on what I was going to do today. And so, to bring you up to date when I'm done, I have a fifth birthday with a lot of furniture except the dad port and the biggest chair. And as you remember, last year, last summer, I hired someone to shampoo this living room rug. But today, I shampooed it myself and for a couple of dollars I had for the shampoo, I didn't make a mistake because I had to rent a shampooer, but I think the way she talks, she isn't going to charge me anything because I won't have it very long. They charge $2 for 24 hours, and I kind of talked her into letting me have it for nothing if I only had it for about three hours. It's all done and I'm waiting for it to begin to dry so I can see if it needs to be spotted any place else before I take this thing back. I also decided that I was tired of that and so I didn't know whether fibroblasts would die or not. but I thought the only one way to find out and that's to do it. So I had a section of drapes in the closet that was doing absolutely no one any good so I thought I'd test it out on that piece first and it took. Your dad didn't think it would and the instructions on the vent said that they didn't recommend it for fiberglass but it took and so I went back down to the store, I could see that it was going to take several more packages than what I had bought. So I went back down to the store, and I got some more, and I ended up not having enough and had to go back again. And it took ten packages of red to dye the five pair of drapes that were in the living room. Well, I just went out to take them off line and that something's gone wrong. The side that was next to the sun, as it dried, it dried out a little faded more so, faded out color more so than the other side hanging away from the sun. So I turned them around and think maybe the sun might finish bleaching out that other side. There is a chance that that fiberglass glass will fade as they hang up the windows, but I don't really care. I'm sick and tired of those things anyway, so I just feel like I want to go buy some new ones, and it may end up, I may have to anyway. But the house is a mess, but the living room is all for us, and I'll probably have it back in shape by evening. And believe it or not, I have a taste of what it's going to be like for me for that bright time. I miss that kid already and that's something that he keeps doing. I guess that he's happy for the past and what I have now. This trip to Scout Camp means that he is growing up and he soon will be out on his own and uh... running around and uh... they won't want to go with us any place but you boys uh... did and uh... whether you mark it or not uh... you don't like to have it happen because uh... that's the time that you're going through but i know he's going to have a good time and and uh... it's going to do him a lot of good and uh... he got initiated just right uh... we had a darn good wind and rainstorm last night. And usually I'll sleep through those things, but I was awake off and on the biggest part of the night, and at 2 o'clock it woke me up. And all I could think of was that kid out there at that scout camp. And I bet he thought, boy, what have I got into? I can just hear him. And I met him. But they're in the Old Forest spot, and I'm sure you know. uh... without that that i think that that the into their and uh... it's a little handy but the other uh... but uh... better whatever the uh... at right and uh... blackburn bill with that they had to look at that drop off what therefore and uh... I kidded him the other night that we talked about the first day of the church. And he said, well, it'll make a difference to me. And so I can't imagine, though, but by Thursday night, he'll be glad to see us and have fun and tell us. He was awake at 5 o'clock yesterday. And I said, well, it's a good day. I said, well, it's not. Because we have those pictures out in the backyard. and I think they'll probably attract other birds due to the fact that they're out there for the pigeons. And naturally early in the morning while they're out there eating their breakfast, and the raisin plant came and it woke him up. Well, due to the fact that it was his big day, why he couldn't go back to sleep. sleep. So he got up here and fooled around and I had baked some salmon rolls and he got up and he ate four or five of those and then he went back to the bedroom and he turned on his radio and about oh quarter seven he woke me up with it playing. So I got up and closed his bedroom door and let him have his music then. And we got up about 7.30 and got ready for church. So we actually got out of church while we went out to the airport and ate breakfast. I had suggested that we go out there here some time ago, and last Sunday we forgot it. It never entered our mind, but after we got to the meeting, I said, I thought we were supposed to go out to the airport again or one of these day seasons. and so your dad said, well, next Sunday we would. So that's where we ended up for breakfast yesterday morning. And it was nice, but I was glad to get home. I had a terrific headache, and I don't believe it was from too much beer on Saturday night. It was definitely a sign of headache, but we did have a good time Saturday night. He didn't enjoy himself too much. David played that tub like he hadn't played it before. And he got a blister on his finger shortly after he got started. He played it so hard. But I think he was wanting to perform for Bull. And he must have been practicing through the week because he really had improved. So maybe the music at school, the lessons there, maybe they're helping him some. I don't know. but he's ready to end up summer school with the math teacher, as he stated on the first of the tapes. And, well, this tape is about over, so I'm going to turn it over and play on some more. I don't know whether I'll fill it up or not, but I'll place the wall on the other side. Thank you.

segments.text: And I hope you don't play back on it because I really believe it's the tape.
I don't believe it's the recorder.
It could be the recorder, but I would advise you not to take back on this
unless you have none.
And, well, if you have no tape, that's why I go ahead and do it.
We'll make the best of it, just like you had to make the best of it listening to it.
If you use your earplug, which I'm sure you have while we're here recording, because we do too,
you will have to keep your finger on the volume control.
Well, of course, it's kind of late to be telling you this now because one side is already done.
But now that I've said this, I'll drop you a note in with the tape to explain instructions to you.
Well, as your dad told you, we went down to Storrington, and Char has been cleaning house, and she's in a throwing away mood.
And so she started holding up my arms with stuff that she thought I might want.
And I really never did turn anything down that anybody wanted to give me.
So the first thing she came out with was a set of Chinese tea dishes.
And I really haven't got into them and looked at to see what there is.
But the teapot was on top and it wasn't wrapped.
So I looked at it and it's a pretty thing.
And it's hand-painted.
And your dad said that he was sure it's been in the family.
It's been in there as long as he can remember.
So, you know, it's been in the family for a long time.
So I'll keep it and then hand it down to one of you kids that shows a desire that you might like to have it, I imagine.
Some of the other things was a Madonna statue that your dad had given Grandma a few years back.
And they felt that he should have it back, too, now.
And then there was a finished quilt that the top, quilt top, belonged to your great-grandmother.
And it is an odd, the prints are kind of odd in it, but it is a pretty quilt.
And it's all finished and ready to use.
The other two quilts, one was just a quilt top, which I'll have to buy the batting that goes on the inside and have it quilted.
The other one was a quilt that Grandma had started.
She had about, oh, I'd say a foot of it quilted, stitched, before she took sick the last time.
so John took it out of the quilt frames and folded it up
so it's always whenever I find someone to finish it for me
I'll get it done
and I have plans to put those two quilts that have to be finished
away for you two boys
and to give you if and when you have a home of your own someday
I'm sure that you would definitely appreciate having a couple of quilts that your grandmother had made, had started at least.
So that's, she went through some other stuff and she is going to get rid of it, but I don't know whether I want any of it.
so the marine dog is always going to have a rummage sale.
And I told her not to throw any of it away,
but I'd take it off her hands and use it for the rummage sale.
And I just went in there and felt that floor.
It feels a little wretched,
and so I think I'll go ahead and get the drapes back up to the wall.
That much will be done.
And I had told Grandma that I would do some painting for her,
and uh but uh i'm kind of in the mood to do it right now i had planned on doing it today while
this floor was drying because i can't do much of anything else but uh um i got kind of a late start
getting this rug shampooed and and i had a few uh interferences so um i'm now in the mood to do
up there starting painting because it may run me kind of late and uh to get done so i think what
I'll do is fiddle around here for a while and do what I can do and then go up there in the morning
for a spin while it's cool and get that done. That way it'll kind of occupy my time and as I
mentioned before with David Goddard it's pretty quiet around here and so it'll be good to have
some little job to do that will take up some of my time. He definitely has been a very good boy Mike
and I hope that it continues.
I hope that he doesn't run into any problems out there at scout camp,
and your dad tells me to quit worrying about him, but he'll be all right.
But the problems that we had before school was out was just a little bit too much,
and I tell you what, since the first of June and school was over, he has been a very good boy,
And although Saturday he was cutting a yard back over on Bates' yard over there on University,
and I had walked over to talk to Bonnie Smith for a minute,
and he was just about to finish up, and some kids were playing around there.
And they had been, I didn't know it, but on Friday night while I was going to a Marine meeting and a picnic,
why they had been tormenting him and calling him names
and trying to run him down with their bikes.
And so he told them that if they didn't stop it, he was going to take care of them.
And so they took off and got away from him.
And so they came over where he was cutting that yard Saturday,
and this one kid in particular kept lipping off to him,
and he told him he better shut up and go on.
And, of course, David was busy and couldn't be bothered.
but when David got through the yard this kid still was mowing off and David started for home I was
kind of looking over that way and I didn't really know what was going on but I uh uh
looked on next thing I knew David had started toward uh home and he got oh just around the
corner there almost to try and move his audience and his kid was still mowing off and David just
rest of the morning, and he turned around, walked back over there, and he popped that
kid twice in the face, and down to the ground he went, and so that took care of that, and
but I can't recommend him for something like that, because I feel like if those kids are
going to provoke that stuff, they got it coming, and maybe I've held him down from
doing, fighting too much, and if he's sure if you're not here, that he is going to take
that crap on him, why maybe they would leave him alone.
But I was kind of glad to see yesterday come,
so things would kind of cool off for a while,
because naturally he gets on that bike and takes off,
and you never know what's going to happen.
And he doesn't know how to control that temper as well as I wished he would.
But anyway, he has really been good, and I can't complain.
So I think I told you his fourth grade teacher, we went out to see her last Monday,
and she said he'd be just as well off if I helped him here at home with his math.
And so this morning I was in one of the best drawers looking for something,
and I ran onto some work that is practice work for his reading.
so I think I'm just
when he comes back
at the end of this week
we'll just put a stop
to the summer school
he had three weeks
and I imagine some of it
did stick but
I don't feel that he's getting out of it
what he should be and so
we'll know better next year than to spend that
kind of money for summer school
I'm certainly
glad that George and I finally got around
to making a tape for you.
I hadn't let Grandma know that we'd got that one tape
telling us that you hadn't heard from,
and I just figured that I just wouldn't say anything to her.
And your dad said, well, bye, girl, just play it anyway,
and maybe we'll get on the ball and send that kid a tape.
And I said, oh, nuts, I'm not going to do it.
They know good and well that those boys want to hear from them
as well as they do from us.
So if they don't have enough sense to get a tape made,
why am I not going to tell them what to do?
So I'm really glad that Georgia May did send you one.
But I did play this last big tape and this short one for the folks,
and they enjoyed it very much.
And so, of course, on that short tape,
you told us that Georgia May had sent you one.
And so Grandpa said, well, I sure wish we had a tape that we could make one for that boy.
But it's really a laugh about Grandma having time to do things anymore.
And when she comes home, she's ready to sit and do practically nothing.
And the work isn't hard, but it's just getting used to it.
And so I did ask her on Friday.
she comes in here on Friday afternoon
at 3.30 and I fix her hair
and she used to
go out to offices every Friday
around noon and get it done
so now she comes in here about 3.30
and I set it for her
and so I asked her Friday
did you ever get a letter of will to those boys
and she said oh yeah I wrote one last Sunday
so I know you got it by now
and
but
of course their weekends
they usually
It isn't too hard for them to find something to do or go someplace.
And so I called up there Saturday morning.
You know, she used to come down here on Saturday, and she had nothing to do.
And I would be trying to get the house straightened up or do this or do that.
And here she come walking in about 10 or 10.30 with nothing to do.
And now, I don't see anything of her.
and hardly ever does she come in after she gets off of work
and very seldom does she get called when she gets home
because she usually lays down right away,
so I don't call her either knowing that she's laying down.
And so Saturday I called up there to see if there were bulls at home
and I'd take those tapes up there to play for her.
And she says, I'm working.
And I said, oh, you've got housework to do?
She said, yes, I have.
And I had a real laugh because it really seems like I never say that.
But she was glad that I called so she could sit down and rest for a little while.
So I went up there later on in the afternoon and played those tapes for them.
And then that evening, where Ram and Wayne Camel and his wife, they went to Champaign for chopped suey up there at some place and food around the evening.
And I don't think they did much of anything yesterday.
but I don't think I wrote to her since it turned off real cool last week
and it was a real rainy, pure week.
And I didn't hardly turn my hand to do anything around here.
I really didn't want to do too much because I knew I'd be doing it this week
and I'd have several days that I could clean and do other things that I wanted to do while David was gone.
And so I just stood around and read and just passed the time away.
The time did go faster than I thought it would,
but I had naturally taken the little electric blankets off the bed and put them away.
And by golly, last Wednesday night, I ended up going to bed two nights with my heavy chair cloth roll bar to keep warm.
And I finally asked the boss, no sense in this.
So I get the heavy electric blanket down and put it on the bed.
And we had that on for two nights.
And that's just the way this weather is here.
And, of course, I've taken it off now because it turned off hot Friday.
and Saturday was even harder.
But that rain we had last night, it was cool things off.
And I've got that window fan on in there, and they're blowing in,
and it's going to help dry that rug much faster, I believe.
And while I was out, while I just shampooed our bedroom rug,
just inside the doorway where it gets all the heavy traffic, it was pretty dirty.
So I've got it shampooed too, and the fan, the small floor fan, drying it.
So Daddy has stamp club tonight, and so I'll be here all evening alone.
But he's been doing pretty good.
He comes home around 10 o'clock from stamp club in the morning.
He used to stop at the union hall and shoot the breeze over there,
But he's been coming on home, especially if he's been to Springfield that day.
And that job over there, it really does tire him out.
It's such a big building.
And by the time he covers all the parts that he has to check in a half a day,
and then goes Lincoln from there and then home from Lincoln, he's had a good full day.
So he sits there and watches Gunsmoke until about 7.30, and they're all repeats.
But he still sits there and watches them anyway and enjoys them just as much as he did the first time.
Then he takes off for his stamp run.
But I imagine he'll leave a little earlier tonight.
He has about between $300 and $400 worth of stamps ready for Haynes and Essex again.
And he's been sitting here the last two or three weeks,
devoting almost all his spare time working on those to get them ready.
And he doesn't want anybody else to get in there and supply them.
So I imagine he's going to take them in there and give them to her tonight.
and as we told you before why that's uh that loss that they had up there which was our game which it
was sad that it had to be that way but uh that will take us on our trip to canada and uh we're
expecting some uh literature from up there just any day about things to not to miss to see so uh
I think we'll enjoy it real well.
And if Boo isn't doing anything at the time that we go,
we're not going to say anything about it until we do leave.
But if he's still around and he's still available,
we're going to have him come out here and stay,
and we'll feel more at ease to have somebody here at night.
And even if he's working, he can still stay here
and at least have the house occupied
because there's so much vandalism going on,
and there's been people that just been away for the day or the evening,
and they've come back and they've had their house broke into,
or kids have got in there and just tore up everything.
So we hate to have our vacation ruined by coming home and finding something like that happening here.
Well, I'm really glad that you're going to get to cross the equator.
I was a little disappointed when we got the word that you weren't going to do it when they had changed their previous plans.
And the evening that we called Delbert and Leon over to see the slides, he sat there and reminisced about when he was in the Navy.
And Bailey just sat here and just laughed so hard at some of his experiences, especially his ordeal when he crossed the equator.
and so I was really glad to hear that you're going to get to do it now.
I hope that you do have plenty of film
and I hope that you're not one of the elected to go through
with no more than has crossed it.
That leaves several that haven't,
so they may end up selecting just certain ones
like they did on Belbert's ship and your dad's too,
the way they talk. We'll be glad to hear from you about how it turned out, and we're pretty
sure that you'll survive it. But as your dad mentioned, and I mentioned it a little bit
today, be sure and call us as soon as they'll let you off the ship to do so. And I know
Georgia May will be glad to hear from you too.
It wouldn't surprise me if she and John, the kids, aren't out there when you pull in.
But as I've thought about it, and I really definitely would have liked to come out,
been there when you got in, why it would have been just our luck that you would have been able to have liberty while we were there.
and if you had it right, it would have only been for maybe two days or three days and two nights,
and it really wouldn't have been worthwhile on our part to be out there
and only get to see you for that short length of time.
So maybe someday we'll get out there,
but then I don't imagine it will be while you kids are in the service
because as far as I know, there just won't be any vacation next summer until the end of August.
And with you kids coming home, I doubt if we make any plans to go anywhere.
And I know very well that the way Bill writes, he won't be extending any of his time over there
because he never fails to write to us about how many more days he has left
until he'll be on his way home.
But he says the time's flying, and I'm glad it is.
I wouldn't want to drag.
Oh, and it's been two weeks ago tonight that Connie called,
and she was supposed to come out to see those slides of his,
and she called and said that she was going to have to babysit.
So I said, well, then you just call in, you can make it,
and no doubt we'll be home and you can come on out.
And so she hasn't called, it's been two weeks.
And so I don't feel like that I should have to call her
and remind her that they're here to be seen because she knows they're here.
I asked Grandma yesterday if she had heard from her
because Connie calls her quite often.
And she said, no, I haven't heard from her for a little over two weeks either.
So then last night Grandma told me that she tried to call her all day, and she didn't answer.
So I don't know anything about her, and I don't care.
But as you predicted, it no doubt has turned out that she's probably giving Bill one of those Dear John letters again.
and I hope that he realizes that it's probably for the best,
although it's hard to accept those things, I know.
Well, I'm lost for words, and I'll sign this off now, Mike,
and get it addressed and get it probably dropped in the box over here at Billy Hughes
instead of running uptown with it.
and I hope you can get it in a short time and either get one back to us or a letter.
So we enjoy hearing naturally.
We look every day just as you naturally look when you get mail call.
I know that I probably don't write as often, but I'm afraid if I did, when I do write,
I try to write as long a letter as I can.
but I'm afraid if I write often
otherwise there wouldn't be enough news to do so
so we'll be waiting to hear from you
and also be waiting patiently for that phone call
from San Diego so bye for now honey and be good
bye bye
Thank you.
