And I told her not to throw any of it away, but I'd take it off her hands and use it for the rummage sale. And I just went in there and felt that floor. It feels a little wretched, and so I think I'll go ahead and get the drapes back up to the wall. That much will be done. And I had told Grandma that I would do some painting for her, and uh but uh i'm kind of in the mood to do it right now i had planned on doing it today while this floor was drying because i can't do much of anything else but uh um i got kind of a late start getting this rug shampooed and and i had a few uh interferences so um i'm now in the mood to do up there starting painting because it may run me kind of late and uh to get done so i think what I'll do is fiddle around here for a while and do what I can do and then go up there in the morning for a spin while it's cool and get that done. That way it'll kind of occupy my time and as I mentioned before with David Goddard it's pretty quiet around here and so it'll be good to have some little job to do that will take up some of my time. He definitely has been a very good boy Mike and I hope that it continues. I hope that he doesn't run into any problems out there at scout camp, and your dad tells me to quit worrying about him, but he'll be all right. But the problems that we had before school was out was just a little bit too much, and I tell you what, since the first of June and school was over, he has been a very good boy, And although Saturday he was cutting a yard back over on Bates' yard over there on University, and I had walked over to talk to Bonnie Smith for a minute, and he was just about to finish up, and some kids were playing around there. And they had been, I didn't know it, but on Friday night while I was going to a Marine meeting and a picnic, why they had been tormenting him and calling him names and trying to run him down with their bikes. And so he told them that if they didn't stop it, he was going to take care of them. And so they took off and got away from him. And so they came over where he was cutting that yard Saturday, and this one kid in particular kept lipping off to him, and he told him he better shut up and go on. And, of course, David was busy and couldn't be bothered. but when David got through the yard this kid still was mowing off and David started for home I was kind of looking over that way and I didn't really know what was going on but I uh uh looked on next thing I knew David had started toward uh home and he got oh just around the corner there almost to try and move his audience and his kid was still mowing off and David just rest of the morning, and he turned around, walked back over there, and he popped that kid twice in the face, and down to the ground he went, and so that took care of that, and but I can't recommend him for something like that, because I feel like if those kids are going to provoke that stuff, they got it coming, and maybe I've held him down from doing, fighting too much, and if he's sure if you're not here, that he is going to take that crap on him, why maybe they would leave him alone. But I was kind of glad to see yesterday come, so things would kind of cool off for a while, because naturally he gets on that bike and takes off, and you never know what's going to happen. And he doesn't know how to control that temper as well as I wished he would. But anyway, he has really been good, and I can't complain. So I think I told you his fourth grade teacher, we went out to see her last Monday, and she said he'd be just as well off if I helped him here at home with his math. And so this morning I was in one of the best drawers looking for something, and I ran onto some work that is practice work for his reading. so I think I'm just when he comes back at the end of this week we'll just put a stop to the summer school he had three weeks and I imagine some of it did stick but I don't feel that he's getting out of it what he should be and so we'll know better next year than to spend that kind of money for summer school I'm certainly glad that George and I finally got around to making a tape for you. I hadn't let Grandma know that we'd got that one tape telling us that you hadn't heard from, and I just figured that I just wouldn't say anything to her. And your dad said, well, bye, girl, just play it anyway, and maybe we'll get on the ball and send that kid a tape. And I said, oh, nuts, I'm not going to do it. They know good and well that those boys want to hear from them as well as they do from us. So if they don't have enough sense to get a tape made, why am I not going to tell them what to do? So I'm really glad that Georgia May did send you one. But I did play this last big tape and this short one for the folks, and they enjoyed it very much. And so, of course, on that short tape, you told us that Georgia May had sent you one. And so Grandpa said, well, I sure wish we had a tape that we could make one for that boy. But it's really a laugh about Grandma having time to do things anymore. And when she comes home, she's ready to sit and do practically nothing. And the work isn't hard, but it's just getting used to it. And so I did ask her on Friday. she comes in here on Friday afternoon at 3.30 and I fix her hair and she used to go out to offices every Friday around noon and get it done so now she comes in here about 3.30 and I set it for her and so I asked her Friday did you ever get a letter of will to those boys and she said oh yeah I wrote one last Sunday so I know you got it by now and but of course their weekends they usually It isn't too hard for them to find something to do or go someplace. And so I called up there Saturday morning. You know, she used to come down here on Saturday, and she had nothing to do. And I would be trying to get the house straightened up or do this or do that. And here she come walking in about 10 or 10.30 with nothing to do. And now, I don't see anything of her. and hardly ever does she come in after she gets off of work and very seldom does she get called when she gets home because she usually lays down right away, so I don't call her either knowing that she's laying down. And so Saturday I called up there to see if there were bulls at home and I'd take those tapes up there to play for her. And she says, I'm working. And I said, oh, you've got housework to do? She said, yes, I have. And I had a real laugh because it really seems like I never say that. But she was glad that I called so she could sit down and rest for a little while. So I went up there later on in the afternoon and played those tapes for them. And then that evening, where Ram and Wayne Camel and his wife, they went to Champaign for chopped suey up there at some place and food around the evening. And I don't think they did much of anything yesterday. but I don't think I wrote to her since it turned off real cool last week and it was a real rainy, pure week. And I didn't hardly turn my hand to do anything around here. I really didn't want to do too much because I knew I'd be doing it this week and I'd have several days that I could clean and do other things that I wanted to do while David was gone. And so I just stood around and read and just passed the time away. The time did go faster than I thought it would, but I had naturally taken the little electric blankets off the bed and put them away. And by golly, last Wednesday night, I ended up going to bed two nights with my heavy chair cloth roll bar to keep warm. And I finally asked the boss, no sense in this. So I get the heavy electric blanket down and put it on the bed. And we had that on for two nights. And that's just the way this weather is here. And, of course, I've taken it off now because it turned off hot Friday. and Saturday was even harder. But that rain we had last night, it was cool things off. And I've got that window fan on in there, and they're blowing in, and it's going to help dry that rug much faster, I believe. And while I was out, while I just shampooed our bedroom rug, just inside the doorway where it gets all the heavy traffic, it was pretty dirty. So I've got it shampooed too, and the fan, the small floor fan, drying it. So Daddy has stamp club tonight, and so I'll be here all evening alone. But he's been doing pretty good. He comes home around 10 o'clock from stamp club in the morning. He used to stop at the union hall and shoot the breeze over there, But he's been coming on home, especially if he's been to Springfield that day. And that job over there, it really does tire him out. It's such a big building. And by the time he covers all the parts that he has to check in a half a day, and then goes Lincoln from there and then home from Lincoln, he's had a good full day. So he sits there and watches Gunsmoke until about 7.30, and they're all repeats. But he still sits there and watches them anyway and enjoys them just as much as he did the first time. Then he takes off for his stamp run. But I imagine he'll leave a little earlier tonight. He has about between $300 and $400 worth of stamps ready for Haynes and Essex again. And he's been sitting here the last two or three weeks, devoting almost all his spare time working on those to get them ready. And he doesn't want anybody else to get in there and supply them. So I imagine he's going to take them in there and give them to her tonight. and as we told you before why that's uh that loss that they had up there which was our game which it was sad that it had to be that way but uh that will take us on our trip to canada and uh we're expecting some uh literature from up there just any day about things to not to miss to see so uh I think we'll enjoy it real well. And if Boo isn't doing anything at the time that we go, we're not going to say anything about it until we do leave. But if he's still around and he's still available, we're going to have him come out here and stay, and we'll feel more at ease to have somebody here at night. And even if he's working, he can still stay here and at least have the house occupied because there's so much vandalism going on, and there's been people that just been away for the day or the evening, and they've come back and they've had their house broke into, or kids have got in there and just tore up everything. So we hate to have our vacation ruined by coming home and finding something like that happening here. Well, I'm really glad that you're going to get to cross the equator. I was a little disappointed when we got the word that you weren't going to do it when they had changed their previous plans. And the evening that we called Delbert and Leon over to see the slides, he sat there and reminisced about when he was in the Navy. And Bailey just sat here and just laughed so hard at some of his experiences, especially his ordeal when he crossed the equator. and so I was really glad to hear that you're going to get to do it now. I hope that you do have plenty of film and I hope that you're not one of the elected to go through with no more than has crossed it. That leaves several that haven't, so they may end up selecting just certain ones like they did on Belbert's ship and your dad's too, the way they talk. We'll be glad to hear from you about how it turned out, and we're pretty sure that you'll survive it. But as your dad mentioned, and I mentioned it a little bit today, be sure and call us as soon as they'll let you off the ship to do so. And I know Georgia May will be glad to hear from you too. It wouldn't surprise me if she and John, the kids, aren't out there when you pull in. But as I've thought about it, and I really definitely would have liked to come out, been there when you got in, why it would have been just our luck that you would have been able to have liberty while we were there. and if you had it right, it would have only been for maybe two days or three days and two nights, and it really wouldn't have been worthwhile on our part to be out there and only get to see you for that short length of time. So maybe someday we'll get out there, but then I don't imagine it will be while you kids are in the service because as far as I know, there just won't be any vacation next summer until the end of August. And with you kids coming home, I doubt if we make any plans to go anywhere. And I know very well that the way Bill writes, he won't be extending any of his time over there because he never fails to write to us about how many more days he has left until he'll be on his way home. But he says the time's flying, and I'm glad it is. I wouldn't want to drag. Oh, and it's been two weeks ago tonight that Connie called, and she was supposed to come out to see those slides of his, and she called and said that she was going to have to babysit. So I said, well, then you just call in, you can make it, and no doubt we'll be home and you can come on out. And so she hasn't called, it's been two weeks. And so I don't feel like that I should have to call her and remind her that they're here to be seen because she knows they're here. I asked Grandma yesterday if she had heard from her because Connie calls her quite often. And she said, no, I haven't heard from her for a little over two weeks either. So then last night Grandma told me that she tried to call her all day, and she didn't answer. So I don't know anything about her, and I don't care. But as you predicted, it no doubt has turned out that she's probably giving Bill one of those Dear John letters again. and I hope that he realizes that it's probably for the best, although it's hard to accept those things, I know. Well, I'm lost for words, and I'll sign this off now, Mike, and get it addressed and get it probably dropped in the box over here at Billy Hughes instead of running uptown with it. and I hope you can get it in a short time and either get one back to us or a letter. So we enjoy hearing naturally. We look every day just as you naturally look when you get mail call. I know that I probably don't write as often, but I'm afraid if I did, when I do write, I try to write as long a letter as I can. but I'm afraid if I write often otherwise there wouldn't be enough news to do so so we'll be waiting to hear from you and also be waiting patiently for that phone call from San Diego so bye for now honey and be good bye bye Thank you.

1968-07-18.text:
The San Diego Union
San Diego, California, Friday Morning, July 19, 1968

Three Warships Return From Vietnam Duty

Pictures — Pages a-1, a-3

By JAMIE RORYSON

Bands played, banners fluttered, and wives and children waved yesterday as three vessels of San Diego-based Destroyer Division One returned home from six months' Vietnam action.

The ships — the guided missile frigates Jouett (DLG-29) and Preble (DLG-15) and the destroyer Hull (DD-945) carried 1,000 officers and men.

In Vietnam, the squadron participated in search and rescue patrols for downed aviators, and bombarded shore targets.

RESCUED 8 FLIERS

The Jouett, with Capt. A. T. Emerson Jr., squadron commander, aboard, wore eight parachutes painted on the superstructure below her bridge, signifying eight aviators were rescued during the deployment. Emerson, of Coronado, served as commander of the Navy's search and rescue units in the Tonkin Gulf Area.

In an interview shortly after the ships docked at the Naval Station, Emerson said vessels of the search and rescue units stood between U.S. carriers and the shore to track incoming and outgoing planes and pick up downed aviators.

SAYS MORALE HIGH

"Morale was high on all the ships of the squadron," he said. "The men had a job to do and they did it tremendously well. I am proud of them."

Capt. Robert S. Hayes of Pacific Beach, captain of the Jouett, said his ship, as flagship of the search and rescue operations, completed 932 helicopter takeoffs and landings from its deck, made 25 night fuel and supply replenishments from other ships, and served 103 days in the combat zone without a serious accident among its crew of 400.

During the deployment, the Hull, commanded by Cmdr. G. A. Church of Coronado, fired 25,000 five-inch shells at enemy targets, believed to be a record number for a single deployment.

GIBBONS IN COMMAND

The Preble is commanded by Cmdr. P. C. Gibbons of San Diego.

                     UNDERWAY DAILY ROUTINE
                     IN PORT HOLIDAY ROUTINE

0345 - Relieve the watch.
0500 - Call the duty ship's cooks.
0545 - Call the duty MAA, food handlers, duty stewards, and reveille PO's.
0600 - Reveille. (All hands except the mid-watch and others authorized to
       sleep late.)
0615 - Reveille PO's make reports to the duty MAA. Mess gear. All hands having
       personal gear in the helo hanger locker lay back to remove same.
0630 - Breakfast for the oncoming watch and PO1s.
0645 - Breakfast for the crew.
0700 - Up all late bunks. Relieve the watch.
0730 - Secure the mess line. Muster on station. Turn in muster reports to
       the ship's office by 0800.
0740 - Test alarms.
0815 - Complete all topside work for entering port. All hands not on watch
       clear topside areas. All hands except engineering watches shift into
       the Uniform for Entering Port (Tropical White).
0845 (About) - Set the Special Sea and Anchor Detail with the exception of
       line handlers. All hands not on Sea Detail assemble on the helo deck.
0930 (About) - All hands to Quarters for entering port. Line handlers man
       Special Sea Detail Stations.
1000 - Moor Pier 4, San Diego, California, U.S.A. Secure from Quarters.
ASAP - Liberty commences for Sections 2, 3, 4, and 5 to expire on board at 0730
       Friday 19 July for Section 2, 0730 Saturday 20 July for Section 3, 0730
       Sunday 21 July for Section 4, and 0700 Monday 22 July for Section 5.
       Commence holiday routine.
1100 - Mess Gear.
1115 - Dinner for the oncoming watch and PO1s.
1145 - Knock off ship's work. Relieve the watch. Dinner for the crew.
1230 - Secure the Mess line.
1545 - Relieve the watch.
1645 - Check setting of material condition YOKE. Make reports to D. C. Central.
1700 - All hands topside shift into the Uniform of the Day or On Station Uniform
1715 - Supper for the oncoming watch and PO1s.
1730 - Supper for the crew.
1915 - Relieve the watch.
1930 - Secure the mess line. Lay before the mast all eight o'clock reports.
2030 - Movie call.
2200 (About) - Unrig movies. Taps. Light out.
2345 - Relieve the watch.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

                            NOTES

1. Morning Schedule. A Press helicopter is expected to take aerial photographs
of the ship at about 0830. Topside areas will be cleared by 0815 and all
personnel topside after that time must be in the Uniform for Entering Port
(Tropical White). Special Sea and Anchor Details with the exception of line
handlers will be set at about 0845 and all personnel not having Special Sea
and Anchor stations will assemble on the flight deck to form a "29" for pictures
being taken from Point Loma. After passing Point Loma, personnel will fall in at
Quarters for Entering Port. After passing through the new bridge construction,
the Commodore's Gig will be lowered and proceed to Pier 4. JOUETT will moor to
Pier 4 at about 1000, and leave and liberty parties may leave the ship from the
after brow as soon as agricultural clearence is obtained.
   To enhance our arrival, JOUETT will stream large balloons from the forecastle
and fantail, and a large sign will be displayed on the port side saying,
"Happiness is Homecoming."

   Refreshments will be served on the helo deck and mess decks, so bring your
dependents and guests aboard for a tour before heading home.

2. Personal Firearms. Personal firearms may be picked up from the Small Arms
Locker (1-133-2A) between 1030 and 1200 today. Base regulations impose stringent
restrictions on the possession of firearms. As a matter of practice, personnel
returning from Westpac are able to remove personal firearms from the base, on the
day of their return, without written permission from Base Security. It is
prudent, however, to keep firearms boxed in their original containers and to avoid
flagrant display (ie..., don't try walking through the gate with a gun under
your arm). If you want to remove your firearms from the ship, do so immediately
and don't bring it back onto the base. Otherwise, leave it in the custody
of the Gunnery Officer.

3. Electrical Power. The ship will be receiving electrical power from the
beach. Only a limited amount of power is available and care must be observed by
all hands in order to prevent loss of electrical power to the ship.
   All persons must notify the duty electrician prior to energizing large
current consuming devices such as motor generator sets, vents, winches, gun
mounts, directors, etc.

4. CIAC Notes. Now is the time to consider the use of San Diego's educational
facilities. Tuition Aid is available from COM 11 thru the I & E Office at the
Naval Station. The government will pay 75% of the cost. You pay the balance.
Check with I & E for available courses and schedules.
   Leave period is upon us. Do you plan to be gone during advancement
examinations? Have you turned in an address to send your exam to? If not,
do so at once to Ruiz PN1.
   Information handouts regarding the medical program for you and your
dependents is available at Career Information Office.
   California has a huge amount of automotive traffic. Do you know the rules
and regulations? Vehicle Code Books are on sale at Career Information Office.
Charge accounts established. Be prepared!

5. Uniforms in San Diego. Uniforms on board while in San Diego will conform
to the uniforms set forth above except, hopefully, after today we will have no
occasion for wearing the uniform for entering port for awhile. Note particularly
the uniforms for Quarterdeck and Topside Watches. Also, the uniform of the day
or on - station uniform must be worn topside after 1700 (1200 on weekends and
holidays). There will be no exceptions to this policy except for urgent dirty
work when specifically authorized by the Command Duty Officer. Dungarees are
permitted below decks only after 1700 weekdays and 1200 weekends and holidays.

6. Liberty. Liberty will expire as shown in the daily routine. Liberty will
commence at 0900 over the weekend. Note that all liberty expires at 0700 on
Monday 22 July when we commence the new hours.

7. Illegal Shooting. Illegal shooting in California State Parks. Governor
Regan states there has been an increase in shooting incidents in California State
Parks, particularly Anza-Borrego Desert State Park. Illegal shooting has resulted
in the death of two park visitors in the last few months. Section 4304.1 of
the California Administrative Code states:

   "Firearms. No person shall possess a firearm with a cartridge in any portion
   of the mechanism; nor shall any person discharge across, in, or into
   any portion of the state park system a firearm, bow and arrow, or air
   or gas weapon or any device capable of injuring or killing any animal
   or damaging or destroying any public or private property."

                                    J. A. WALKER, JR.
                                    LCDR          USN
                                    EXECUTIVE OFFICER

1968-07-23.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-07-23.text:
Tues. July 23, 1968
San Diego

Hi Dad,

Its about 8:45 PM here and I am sitting in my rack writing this so I hope the writing isn't too bad.

I have duty today so that explains why I'm aboard now.

I had Saturday, Sunday and Monday off and of course went up to visit Mother and everyone else. I got back here on the ship about 3:45 this morning so that made it a long night for me.

Again I can't get over how much David has grown in the past 7 months. I set up my stereo equipment while there and he was really crazy about it. He thought that was just the thing.

We packed my things in their car to see if they would not take up too much room. The way it looks now they are going to be able to bring all of my things back with them. Mother and David are also carrying a few small items back too.

We recieved your letter that contained Bill's letter and pictures yesterday afternoon, so that gave us all a chance to read it.

If things go right I plan to leave here tomorrow morning and return Saturday at 7 AM in order to pay another visit up there before mother leaves as she is planning to on Saturday. If this doesn't work out I will go up Friday and tell them goodby.

I got a letter from Bill this afternoon. He sounds envious of me being back here in the states but sure wants another tour of that mess duty. As long as he likes it that's all that counts.

I ordered a turntable from Allied yesterday and it should arrive by express in a week or so if all goes well.

I also bought a movie projector while I was up there for the weekend. It works real good and everyone liked the movies I showed.

I hope things are going smoothly for you back there. Have a good time on the trip to Canada.

I have to close here so will see you later. So long.

Your son,

Mike

segments.text: 28 and we are home safe and sound and needless to say very happy to be home.
We had a very nice ride coming in with the exception of a 30 minute delay in LA due to the fact that there was too many people on the plane.
and they kept asking everyone, making announcements,
are you sure you're on the right plane, and so forth and so on.
And finally, they came through and had us show our tickets
to make sure that we were where we belonged.
At 1.30, they pulled out,
and, of course, the sight from the air at night was something to see.
But it wasn't too long until we were up above the clouds and there wasn't anything to see any longer.
And we had a very full plane and as I remember the reservationist had told me that there shouldn't be too many on a plane
and we would have the middle seat or one of the three seats to ourselves.
But there wasn't an extra seat to be had.
The problem was that they evidently had sold too many tickets for second class,
and the people that came on late had to go up to the first class cabin to sit.
Too bad that David and I didn't get in there a little bit later.
If we could have sat up there, too, we would have been much more comfortable.
But we pulled out, and I was in hopes that we might get about an hour's nap,
but there wasn't any sleeping available.
There was a couple of squalling rats on the plane,
and you just about shut your eyes thinking you might get a little bit of a nap,
and one of them would start hollering and screaming and crying.
And then there was one sitting right in back of me on his mother's lap,
and he kept pushing the back of his seat, which made it very interesting.
So three hours soon passed and we landed in St. Louis.
Almost on schedule, the captain had made up the half hour time.
And we of course walked from the plane in up through the long, long walk that you have to take
and went upstairs to the restaurant and we had a nice breakfast.
We took our time, and of course the time was beginning to get longer and longer as each hour went by, but soon it was time to check our tickets to leave on the Ozark.
The Ozark was 30 minutes late getting into St. Louis.
Or no, it was 15 minutes late getting there, and I didn't think they were ever going to let us get on board.
Well, come to find out that it was having trouble too.
It had radar trouble.
And then a little bit later, they found out it had engine trouble.
Well, before they found out what all was wrong with it,
they let a few people waiting to board it get on.
And we set a little longer.
The hostess came through with the candy and with the pop and with the magazine
trying to occupy everyone.
And I believe we had been on the plane about, oh, 20 minutes.
And they decided to take everyone off, have them go back inside and wait.
And they had made up their minds to change planes.
So about 10 minutes later, they announced that we were ready.
They were ready for us to board the other plane.
Well, we did, and we got into the cave.
Instead of getting in here at 1020 like we were supposed to, we got in at about five minutes to twelve.
Needless to say, I was mighty glad to get my feet on the ground and be in the cave.
And your dad had been waiting for us all that time, so he, of course, he enjoyed just roaming around
and sitting there watching the people and I assumed there had been a plan to come in and take off.
So he just waited around because he knew there wouldn't be any point in coming back home
and I asked him to go back to it.
But he was very glad to see it, I'm sure.
At least he acted like it and he had a lot of questions to ask
and I had a lot of things to tell.
And I kind of feel like my jaw is beginning to ache a little bit from doing so much talking.
But I just couldn't seem to tell it all fast enough.
Well, when he picked us up, he said,
Well, you guys must be hungry and there isn't anything at home to eat,
so we'll stop at the Burger Queen and get a hamburger, which was all right with me,
because I wasn't in any mood to do any Christmas shopping.
All right, Christmas shopping.
You must think I'm drunk.
Grocery shopping.
And so we stopped and I said,
we'd never come on home.
And then began the chore of unpacking and putting away and so forth.
Well, this house looked pretty good before David and I landed,
but it began to look like a cyclone had hit it.
That's when we arrived.
So little by little I've gotten things put away and things straightened up.
About three or four loads of clothes washed.
And your dad had took to bed yesterday morning and he'd washed that load of clothes,
underwear and towels and things.
So they were in the dryer and ready to be put back on the bed when I got home.
So about, oh I think it was around 3.30 we insisted that they was
go to bed and take a nap for a while because we planned on going to Shakey's that evening
for supper because I still hadn't got to the store and really didn't make any plans to
do it.
And so we, he laid down about 3.30, the radio going tell now, and it wasn't very long until
Well he was down to sleep and I laid down about 4 o'clock to really step on the news
and I finally laid the paper down and shut my eyes and told my dad to wake me up at 5
o'clock.
Well 5.20 the phone rang and woke me up.
He said I was sleeping too good to wake me up and he figured I needed some extra sleep.
Well, I stayed up then, but it wasn't but about half an hour later, so here comes the boy on the corner, who I've mentioned to you before, who's dad's in the Navy.
And they had gone out to San Diego to be with him, and they had left all about the second week of June, I believe, and they would be gone until the first of August.
and by golly, they got in yesterday the same as we did,
and they drove out.
She drove a van, a wagon out there,
and of course they got the poor kids,
and her mother went along to help with the kids in the drive.
While they were there, they bought a new car,
also kept the van.
She drove the van back and her mother drove the car back.
It took a little bit longer due to the fact that they were staying together all the way
at home.
She brought that van back loaded with stuff that he had brought over there in the Philippines
and I suppose maybe in Hawaii and also back at San Diego.
They were really having themselves a job unpacking that van yesterday after we got in.
But Dan was real glad to be back and he made, he'd come running in here.
They had just hardly pulled in the driveway so he'd come walking in here.
And he had a lot to talk about and we went back and got David up out of bed.
because I knew he'd want to see Dan.
Well, when Dan's out, we've been out there too, he's nearly flipped.
And then when I walked over to see her and show her the pictures,
she just had a fit because she had naturally read the papers
each day where these ships come in whenever they did,
and they always invite people to come down and welcome the boys in.
And she said if she'd have just known us, she would have certainly been there
to see us and also see you.
But I had no way of knowing where she was at
because Eula Hunt was in the hospital, as I felt, when I got back home.
I went up to see her the day we left, but she wasn't home,
so I didn't get their address.
And so I had no way of locating him.
Or I suppose that if I'd just have taken the time, that certainty,
I could have maybe located where this ship was
and then gone from there.
But that wasn't on my mind that day.
I wasn't about to go look up to somebody while I was waiting there for you.
So I hope that everything's going along all right with you
and you find that you can get adjusted back to Navy life
after having six days off and get back into the routine.
It won't be long until you'll have that long weekend again and be heading for Florence.
So I do want you to know how much we did enjoy you and seeing you and being with you out there.
And it was well worth coming for.
I wouldn't have missed it for anything.
Had I not gone and made up my mind to do this, I would have been sorry, I know, for a long time to come.
But as I said, I'm very happy that I did go down.
And your dad is more than happy that we did go because he has enjoyed hearing what all happened and took place.
And I think that now and then he felt like he was there too.
I want to ask you something about something I couldn't find in the suitcase.
Do you remember the newspaper clipping that you had about the ship coming in?
It was in that shuttle plane holder or whatever.
I thought that you gave that to me to bring home,
and I thought I had put it in a suitcase in the pocket part of the suitcase
the suitcase so it wouldn't get bent or something. I cannot find it. Maybe I got confused. Maybe
you gave that to me or told me to put it in your suitcase. I don't know. But at any rate,
I can't find it. I wish that you would let me know what happened to it. If I was supposed
to bring it home, why, maybe it's still at Georgia Mae. And if it is, why, maybe she
will have found it and bring it with her if she comes. But I happily thought that she
wanted me to bring that aunt home here, but I can't find it anywhere. And if it's lost,
I hate it because I thought I was taking care of those ends pretty well, keeping it in that
room. And I thought I'd put it down inside that picture for Grandma, between the picture
and the cardboard sleeve, with the picture of him. But she didn't find it when I gave
it to her. And David and I went up there after we'd been home for a while. I called and let
him know we was home. And then later on, shortly afterwards, we went up there and took the
and they were really happy to hear all the news and all the doings that went on and so
forth.
And so she just worked her hair so I got there just in time to sew it up for her.
And then there's, then he had all the newspapers paid for me and of course he had no experience
Of course, he hadn't noticed it, but she had, just Connie's wedding pictures in the paper.
So I'm going to be sure to cut that out and send it to you so you can read it and read.
But I only had a little assignment, too, while I was gone.
I was at Macon County Hospital, and I'll send you the clipping of that, and you can explain it more thorough.
But it could have been very serious, and so I went to work out there.
And so, not much else has happened up until last night.
And I know what next door said was kidding me today.
Because I might have known the minute she gets back in town,
we get a lot of noise and excitement going on around here.
But last night, well, we wasn't going to get into bed last night.
I didn't even wait until 10 o'clock noon to get over.
And I was really sleeping hard at about quarter to one, Grandma called.
And she was all excited, and they had just got home.
And they and the winged camel, his wife, and the springfield estate,
used to stop at Subway Inn on the way back, and they were late getting home.
Well, I don't know just how it all got started, but anyway,
it seemed to be a large, very large group of cars down in College Parking Lot.
and they had been driving about 80 to 90 miles an hour up and down these streets around Ellen
and Christian Division. There was four squad cars out here and one sheriff's car. And no
one quite knew what the score was, but anyway it was pretty exciting and so she figured
that we ought to know about it too, so she called me and she got out of bed. Well, I
run our damn neck because I wasn't, I could care less. And if there was anything happening,
why I just as well not know it last night of all nights, as tired as I was. But as it turned out,
why they were two flood cars parked right down here at the division, and one was, and then the
other one was on down back at the University. And they had stopped one of the cars, and then
one car radiated to the other car that he had the information that he needed and for him to meet him down in Colley Park.
So that's where they're headed for. And I guess after Randall called and after the car left,
he was on the block while there was other cars coming back again. They had scattered them all.
And he called the police and told them that the car was clutching again in the back of Colley.
So it was quite an exciting night, especially for them, because they were just getting in.
And the cars woke up too bad.
I didn't even land there awake when the phone rang.
But it's an automatic impulse for me to jump up out of bed when the phone rang.
So as sound asleep as I was while I jumped up.
But he heard the cars woke him up driving too fast, and they also woke up Delbert.
Well, the largest would show up that final night, because they still had a lot of other
testing to do, and up on the farm.
And so they found out what it was.
There wasn't anything on the news this evening, but they found out from one of the police
cars that stopped down at the end of the block to go or be under surveillance of the cars
going through, that a policeman in one of the Sandy's drive-ins had been beat up on.
And when they called for help, why, these bus kids took off in their cars.
And there evidently had been trouble there at Sandy's.
And I don't know which one, but they didn't say.
But anyway, there no doubt had been some fighting going on.
And when the policeman tried to break it up, why, he got the whole ice cube out of him.
And then they evidently took off following in cars.
cars and he's gonna proceed to have more of the fight going on. So nobody wanted to
in the paper about it, so that was all that really happened since we came back home.
And we went to Curtis' farm and they went out and ate breakfast and took the post office,
there wasn't any mail, and we come on home. Daddy started cutting the cut yards late
late the first minute and then I took a little break from him and set the backyard and I've got a lot of weeds pulled.
Boy, it's really really good for this time of year. We had some rain back there while I was gone.
And so I've got a lot of yard weed pulling to do before this next weekend comes up because
I don't really want to get ahead of me while we're going to Canada. I don't know exactly what
they were going to leave. Something said about leaving Friday night and then something said
about not leaving until the following Monday. But as far as I can tell, I mentioned that
I just assumed early Saturday morning and get started and why sit around here for the
weekend when you need to be going anyway. So why not go ahead and get started on Saturday
early and have a couple days ahead of itself.
You know, you can come home and take advantage of the extra days at home to rest and relax
before Thursday May comes around.
Besides that, the 16th and 17th of August, I've got to work at a plumbing sale, and so
I'd kind of like to be back here to finish getting this stuff together, that's the ask,
and get rested up again.
So I'm pretty tired and I expect that by the middle of the week I'll be rested up again and ready to go.
But it's sort of a let down after so much excitement going on and I think that's why I'm tired because of the let down.
And I hope to get that healing worked on because I know it's painful and it bothers you.
And, uh, so we're gonna feed her, boy, it hurts you all over.
And, uh, they're, uh, they do an awful lot of work for you, so you are just gonna get
terribly.
And they respect these old self again, who you never know if there's been any problems
in California, and all that's behind us.
His, uh, color voice has somewhat changed, and, uh, well, in fact, it's conservative
change and he's able to act like a boy and he found a turtle today over in the
stagnant yard and they had found two upon a camping trip they had taken last week
and they had it in their backyard and then they had found this third turtle so they
built a cage over there in their backyard for all three turtles to be kept in captivity for a while
off. And he's been on his bike and just a little while ago we finished supper over there.
I took the end of the stick down the hill and we had a real good supper. And I wrote
down a few lines and let her know that we got home okay. And so he comes up at the window
and announces he and Dan are going to go over there to get the shirt to the drive in. And
I said, well you're not going to go home to eat are you?
He said, no, I'm just going to want to dance.
So he's really happy.
He said on the way home on the plane, he said, boy, I wish that we'd go home right away
so I'd have somebody to play with before we go to Canada.
So he was just thinking about that he wouldn't have anybody to play with
and he hasn't really had anybody to play with out there in California either,
if you know what I mean.
So he got his will and he's real happy.

And Dan got a guitar. His dad bought him one over there in the shopping. I haven't seen it, but David said it's really cool. And so I said, well, you and Dan are going to have to get together now. And he played the drums and you're rockers and Dan played the guitar. And he said, yeah, we are. We've already got a plan that we've figured out. So that ought to be good.
And I don't know if Dan knows how to play or not, but anyway, he was really excited.
He didn't really wait until the van had passed to get to it.
And so I was telling him the other day one night that if you ever go on another cruise,
why, I'm going to make darn sure now that I know that ship's in hold, plenty of stuff,
that I'll just send you about $100 and you can bring back all you can carry and pick up over there.
And when you come back into the safe, I'll meet you out there with the truck and bring it home.
I just couldn't believe until I saw the stuff that she got.
Just what you could have brought back, and I was afraid that she wouldn't have room for it,
along with the stuff you got.
But, of course, there wasn't anything really that I could need or would have to have.
But it's just the idea of wanting to take a role in it.
Mrs. Rogers would come home with, I don't know how many of them,
but they looked like seated chests, only they're hand-carved chests,
and they're still the same purpose they were finished at.
I think we brought home a couple of those.
And they were just soft.
He said they were really nice.
And I don't know what all that he had brought back was him.
So I imagine that it's a thing to know why they got things that weren't nice in the midst of him
because he couldn't get that stuff like that.
And of course you can cut the stuff down inside the test too, if,
uh, anyway, you might have set that.
So I don't, I think people will be out in November, so I imagine that, uh,
they'll be getting ready for that big move, wanting to say, 2 and 2.
Well, I really can't, there's just too much more to say,
and I think I'll sign off here now, and, and, uh,
you can use the other side of this tape to send us a message on, if you'd like.
And as soon as I get these pictures developed, I'll send them out for you to see.
And when Georgia Mae comes back, well, I know nobody about it, but when she goes back to California,
I'll just send the two roles of eight nomads film along, and John's going to show them on his projector
so you can see them when you're up there some weekend.
And when should you send the film back to me?
And that way you'll get to see it.
So I'm going to say so long for now, honey,
and write when you can or send the tape back with the message.
And be good, be careful, and bye-bye for now.
Mike, I'll try and finish this off now.
I watched the Cubs play the Dodgers this afternoon on TV.
They beat them in the first game on TV 8-3.
And then I listened to the second game on the radio.
The Cubs won the second game off.
So that's the biggest crowd that Ruger Field has had for 20 years.
So it must have been close to 37,000, 38,000 people there.
By the way, my mother was out to California, and she had her first copy of that all-hand
come, so she said you were going to write him a hot letter, so you just saved your time.
You won't need to write him.
Apparently, they've started showing all the time now.
Sounds like you had a real nice time when Mother and David was out to California.
It was really lucky you got the six days off that you had.
And, of course, since it don't count on your time,
I prefer, again, furlough or leave time.
I think that comes in pretty handy.
David's sure proud of everything you give him,
and I know that he had a real good time out there with you.
And I think that he was glad to get home,
but he kind of hated to leave out there also.
But, of course, since we're going on this other trip,
boy, he'll be in pretty good shape now for the rest of the summer.
Everything here has been going real good.
It's been a little hot all the last 10 days that your mother was gone.
It's a nice and cooler day and a good, cool breeze,
so all this week is supposed to be cooler than normal,
so it won't be too bad.
I don't know what happened to that radio of yours that you had
in our room, the stamp room and radio room,
it just fades out one day,
so I think a tube has apparently burnt out of it,
but I won't have anything done with it until you get home
because I've got other radios I can play,
but I think that's all wrong with it.
The tube is burnt out probably.
Of course, it has had a lot of playing,
but no particular maintenance of any kind on it.
It was a really nice bunch of pictures of Mother Brown, the ship docking and so forth.
I know that David was quite thrilled with everything about the ship.
His buddy down the street, his dad's in the Navy, that Dan Lodge,
and he just got back from California, also seen his dad.
I'm sure that they were going to do quite a bit of this,
and the Navy talking between themselves about who ships the best.
In case you, what happened in the PX or whatever you call it out there,
run across one of those old radio effects I was telling you about that one,
it was like, the price ain't too rough, go ahead and get it and just send it on home.
I suppose, of course, you'd save more money in Hong Kong or some other place,
but it won't get the rough abuse in shipments from California
as it would from overseas someplace.
So use your own judgment if you see one that you think will do the job,
and it's not too rough on price-wise.
Pick it up and send it on home with the wealth.
Maybe Mother was telling you, but today we got the Cal cartridge cases out this morning,
and he got some silver polished and he really polished him up.
I don't know what he's going to make out of it.
He's got some big idea planned to do with it.
Sounds like Bill kind of likes that mess duty that he's into out there.
Of course, that ain't a bad goal really for him.
He don't have to work too hard and he's got a lot of free time to mess around in.
So that's just, and of course he'll be able to get just what he wants to eat when he wants to eat it.
So that's right down his alley.
Well, it looks like this tape is getting pretty close to running out.
I don't have too much to say.
So I'll sign off for now.
Take care of yourself and let us hear from you whenever you can.
So goodbye for now, Mike.
Be good and be careful.
Thank you.
Boom.

1968-07-28.text: 28 and we are home safe and sound and needless to say very happy to be home. We had a very nice ride coming in with the exception of a 30 minute delay in LA due to the fact that there was too many people on the plane. and they kept asking everyone, making announcements, are you sure you're on the right plane, and so forth and so on. And finally, they came through and had us show our tickets to make sure that we were where we belonged. At 1.30, they pulled out, and, of course, the sight from the air at night was something to see. But it wasn't too long until we were up above the clouds and there wasn't anything to see any longer. And we had a very full plane and as I remember the reservationist had told me that there shouldn't be too many on a plane and we would have the middle seat or one of the three seats to ourselves. But there wasn't an extra seat to be had. The problem was that they evidently had sold too many tickets for second class, and the people that came on late had to go up to the first class cabin to sit. Too bad that David and I didn't get in there a little bit later. If we could have sat up there, too, we would have been much more comfortable. But we pulled out, and I was in hopes that we might get about an hour's nap, but there wasn't any sleeping available. There was a couple of squalling rats on the plane, and you just about shut your eyes thinking you might get a little bit of a nap, and one of them would start hollering and screaming and crying. And then there was one sitting right in back of me on his mother's lap, and he kept pushing the back of his seat, which made it very interesting. So three hours soon passed and we landed in St. Louis. Almost on schedule, the captain had made up the half hour time. And we of course walked from the plane in up through the long, long walk that you have to take and went upstairs to the restaurant and we had a nice breakfast. We took our time, and of course the time was beginning to get longer and longer as each hour went by, but soon it was time to check our tickets to leave on the Ozark. The Ozark was 30 minutes late getting into St. Louis. Or no, it was 15 minutes late getting there, and I didn't think they were ever going to let us get on board. Well, come to find out that it was having trouble too. It had radar trouble. And then a little bit later, they found out it had engine trouble. Well, before they found out what all was wrong with it, they let a few people waiting to board it get on. And we set a little longer. The hostess came through with the candy and with the pop and with the magazine trying to occupy everyone. And I believe we had been on the plane about, oh, 20 minutes. And they decided to take everyone off, have them go back inside and wait. And they had made up their minds to change planes. So about 10 minutes later, they announced that we were ready. They were ready for us to board the other plane. Well, we did, and we got into the cave. Instead of getting in here at 1020 like we were supposed to, we got in at about five minutes to twelve. Needless to say, I was mighty glad to get my feet on the ground and be in the cave. And your dad had been waiting for us all that time, so he, of course, he enjoyed just roaming around and sitting there watching the people and I assumed there had been a plan to come in and take off. So he just waited around because he knew there wouldn't be any point in coming back home and I asked him to go back to it. But he was very glad to see it, I'm sure. At least he acted like it and he had a lot of questions to ask and I had a lot of things to tell. And I kind of feel like my jaw is beginning to ache a little bit from doing so much talking. But I just couldn't seem to tell it all fast enough. Well, when he picked us up, he said, Well, you guys must be hungry and there isn't anything at home to eat, so we'll stop at the Burger Queen and get a hamburger, which was all right with me, because I wasn't in any mood to do any Christmas shopping. All right, Christmas shopping. You must think I'm drunk. Grocery shopping. And so we stopped and I said, we'd never come on home. And then began the chore of unpacking and putting away and so forth. Well, this house looked pretty good before David and I landed, but it began to look like a cyclone had hit it. That's when we arrived. So little by little I've gotten things put away and things straightened up. About three or four loads of clothes washed. And your dad had took to bed yesterday morning and he'd washed that load of clothes, underwear and towels and things. So they were in the dryer and ready to be put back on the bed when I got home. So about, oh I think it was around 3.30 we insisted that they was go to bed and take a nap for a while because we planned on going to Shakey's that evening for supper because I still hadn't got to the store and really didn't make any plans to do it. And so we, he laid down about 3.30, the radio going tell now, and it wasn't very long until Well he was down to sleep and I laid down about 4 o'clock to really step on the news and I finally laid the paper down and shut my eyes and told my dad to wake me up at 5 o'clock. Well 5.20 the phone rang and woke me up. He said I was sleeping too good to wake me up and he figured I needed some extra sleep. Well, I stayed up then, but it wasn't but about half an hour later, so here comes the boy on the corner, who I've mentioned to you before, who's dad's in the Navy. And they had gone out to San Diego to be with him, and they had left all about the second week of June, I believe, and they would be gone until the first of August. and by golly, they got in yesterday the same as we did, and they drove out. She drove a van, a wagon out there, and of course they got the poor kids, and her mother went along to help with the kids in the drive. While they were there, they bought a new car, also kept the van. She drove the van back and her mother drove the car back. It took a little bit longer due to the fact that they were staying together all the way at home. She brought that van back loaded with stuff that he had brought over there in the Philippines and I suppose maybe in Hawaii and also back at San Diego. They were really having themselves a job unpacking that van yesterday after we got in. But Dan was real glad to be back and he made, he'd come running in here. They had just hardly pulled in the driveway so he'd come walking in here. And he had a lot to talk about and we went back and got David up out of bed. because I knew he'd want to see Dan. Well, when Dan's out, we've been out there too, he's nearly flipped. And then when I walked over to see her and show her the pictures, she just had a fit because she had naturally read the papers each day where these ships come in whenever they did, and they always invite people to come down and welcome the boys in. And she said if she'd have just known us, she would have certainly been there to see us and also see you. But I had no way of knowing where she was at because Eula Hunt was in the hospital, as I felt, when I got back home. I went up to see her the day we left, but she wasn't home, so I didn't get their address. And so I had no way of locating him. Or I suppose that if I'd just have taken the time, that certainty, I could have maybe located where this ship was and then gone from there. But that wasn't on my mind that day. I wasn't about to go look up to somebody while I was waiting there for you. So I hope that everything's going along all right with you and you find that you can get adjusted back to Navy life after having six days off and get back into the routine. It won't be long until you'll have that long weekend again and be heading for Florence. So I do want you to know how much we did enjoy you and seeing you and being with you out there. And it was well worth coming for. I wouldn't have missed it for anything. Had I not gone and made up my mind to do this, I would have been sorry, I know, for a long time to come. But as I said, I'm very happy that I did go down. And your dad is more than happy that we did go because he has enjoyed hearing what all happened and took place. And I think that now and then he felt like he was there too. I want to ask you something about something I couldn't find in the suitcase. Do you remember the newspaper clipping that you had about the ship coming in? It was in that shuttle plane holder or whatever. I thought that you gave that to me to bring home, and I thought I had put it in a suitcase in the pocket part of the suitcase the suitcase so it wouldn't get bent or something. I cannot find it. Maybe I got confused. Maybe you gave that to me or told me to put it in your suitcase. I don't know. But at any rate, I can't find it. I wish that you would let me know what happened to it. If I was supposed to bring it home, why, maybe it's still at Georgia Mae. And if it is, why, maybe she will have found it and bring it with her if she comes. But I happily thought that she wanted me to bring that aunt home here, but I can't find it anywhere. And if it's lost, I hate it because I thought I was taking care of those ends pretty well, keeping it in that room. And I thought I'd put it down inside that picture for Grandma, between the picture and the cardboard sleeve, with the picture of him. But she didn't find it when I gave it to her. And David and I went up there after we'd been home for a while. I called and let him know we was home. And then later on, shortly afterwards, we went up there and took the and they were really happy to hear all the news and all the doings that went on and so forth. And so she just worked her hair so I got there just in time to sew it up for her. And then there's, then he had all the newspapers paid for me and of course he had no experience Of course, he hadn't noticed it, but she had, just Connie's wedding pictures in the paper. So I'm going to be sure to cut that out and send it to you so you can read it and read. But I only had a little assignment, too, while I was gone. I was at Macon County Hospital, and I'll send you the clipping of that, and you can explain it more thorough. But it could have been very serious, and so I went to work out there. And so, not much else has happened up until last night. And I know what next door said was kidding me today. Because I might have known the minute she gets back in town, we get a lot of noise and excitement going on around here. But last night, well, we wasn't going to get into bed last night. I didn't even wait until 10 o'clock noon to get over. And I was really sleeping hard at about quarter to one, Grandma called. And she was all excited, and they had just got home. And they and the winged camel, his wife, and the springfield estate, used to stop at Subway Inn on the way back, and they were late getting home. Well, I don't know just how it all got started, but anyway, it seemed to be a large, very large group of cars down in College Parking Lot. and they had been driving about 80 to 90 miles an hour up and down these streets around Ellen and Christian Division. There was four squad cars out here and one sheriff's car. And no one quite knew what the score was, but anyway it was pretty exciting and so she figured that we ought to know about it too, so she called me and she got out of bed. Well, I run our damn neck because I wasn't, I could care less. And if there was anything happening, why I just as well not know it last night of all nights, as tired as I was. But as it turned out, why they were two flood cars parked right down here at the division, and one was, and then the other one was on down back at the University. And they had stopped one of the cars, and then one car radiated to the other car that he had the information that he needed and for him to meet him down in Colley Park. So that's where they're headed for. And I guess after Randall called and after the car left, he was on the block while there was other cars coming back again. They had scattered them all. And he called the police and told them that the car was clutching again in the back of Colley. So it was quite an exciting night, especially for them, because they were just getting in. And the cars woke up too bad. I didn't even land there awake when the phone rang. But it's an automatic impulse for me to jump up out of bed when the phone rang. So as sound asleep as I was while I jumped up. But he heard the cars woke him up driving too fast, and they also woke up Delbert. Well, the largest would show up that final night, because they still had a lot of other testing to do, and up on the farm. And so they found out what it was. There wasn't anything on the news this evening, but they found out from one of the police cars that stopped down at the end of the block to go or be under surveillance of the cars going through, that a policeman in one of the Sandy's drive-ins had been beat up on. And when they called for help, why, these bus kids took off in their cars. And there evidently had been trouble there at Sandy's. And I don't know which one, but they didn't say. But anyway, there no doubt had been some fighting going on. And when the policeman tried to break it up, why, he got the whole ice cube out of him. And then they evidently took off following in cars. cars and he's gonna proceed to have more of the fight going on. So nobody wanted to in the paper about it, so that was all that really happened since we came back home. And we went to Curtis' farm and they went out and ate breakfast and took the post office, there wasn't any mail, and we come on home. Daddy started cutting the cut yards late late the first minute and then I took a little break from him and set the backyard and I've got a lot of weeds pulled. Boy, it's really really good for this time of year. We had some rain back there while I was gone. And so I've got a lot of yard weed pulling to do before this next weekend comes up because I don't really want to get ahead of me while we're going to Canada. I don't know exactly what they were going to leave. Something said about leaving Friday night and then something said about not leaving until the following Monday. But as far as I can tell, I mentioned that I just assumed early Saturday morning and get started and why sit around here for the weekend when you need to be going anyway. So why not go ahead and get started on Saturday early and have a couple days ahead of itself. You know, you can come home and take advantage of the extra days at home to rest and relax before Thursday May comes around. Besides that, the 16th and 17th of August, I've got to work at a plumbing sale, and so I'd kind of like to be back here to finish getting this stuff together, that's the ask, and get rested up again. So I'm pretty tired and I expect that by the middle of the week I'll be rested up again and ready to go. But it's sort of a let down after so much excitement going on and I think that's why I'm tired because of the let down. And I hope to get that healing worked on because I know it's painful and it bothers you. And, uh, so we're gonna feed her, boy, it hurts you all over. And, uh, they're, uh, they do an awful lot of work for you, so you are just gonna get terribly. And they respect these old self again, who you never know if there's been any problems in California, and all that's behind us. His, uh, color voice has somewhat changed, and, uh, well, in fact, it's conservative change and he's able to act like a boy and he found a turtle today over in the stagnant yard and they had found two upon a camping trip they had taken last week and they had it in their backyard and then they had found this third turtle so they built a cage over there in their backyard for all three turtles to be kept in captivity for a while off. And he's been on his bike and just a little while ago we finished supper over there. I took the end of the stick down the hill and we had a real good supper. And I wrote down a few lines and let her know that we got home okay. And so he comes up at the window and announces he and Dan are going to go over there to get the shirt to the drive in. And I said, well you're not going to go home to eat are you? He said, no, I'm just going to want to dance. So he's really happy. He said on the way home on the plane, he said, boy, I wish that we'd go home right away so I'd have somebody to play with before we go to Canada. So he was just thinking about that he wouldn't have anybody to play with and he hasn't really had anybody to play with out there in California either, if you know what I mean. So he got his will and he's real happy. And Dan got a guitar. His dad bought him one over there in the shopping. I haven't seen it, but David said it's really cool. And so I said, well, you and Dan are going to have to get together now. And he played the drums and you're rockers and Dan played the guitar. And he said, yeah, we are. We've already got a plan that we've figured out. So that ought to be good. And I don't know if Dan knows how to play or not, but anyway, he was really excited. He didn't really wait until the van had passed to get to it. And so I was telling him the other day one night that if you ever go on another cruise, why, I'm going to make darn sure now that I know that ship's in hold, plenty of stuff, that I'll just send you about $100 and you can bring back all you can carry and pick up over there. And when you come back into the safe, I'll meet you out there with the truck and bring it home. I just couldn't believe until I saw the stuff that she got. Just what you could have brought back, and I was afraid that she wouldn't have room for it, along with the stuff you got. But, of course, there wasn't anything really that I could need or would have to have. But it's just the idea of wanting to take a role in it. Mrs. Rogers would come home with, I don't know how many of them, but they looked like seated chests, only they're hand-carved chests, and they're still the same purpose they were finished at. I think we brought home a couple of those. And they were just soft. He said they were really nice. And I don't know what all that he had brought back was him. So I imagine that it's a thing to know why they got things that weren't nice in the midst of him because he couldn't get that stuff like that. And of course you can cut the stuff down inside the test too, if, uh, anyway, you might have set that. So I don't, I think people will be out in November, so I imagine that, uh, they'll be getting ready for that big move, wanting to say, 2 and 2. Well, I really can't, there's just too much more to say, and I think I'll sign off here now, and, and, uh, you can use the other side of this tape to send us a message on, if you'd like. And as soon as I get these pictures developed, I'll send them out for you to see. And when Georgia Mae comes back, well, I know nobody about it, but when she goes back to California, I'll just send the two roles of eight nomads film along, and John's going to show them on his projector so you can see them when you're up there some weekend. And when should you send the film back to me? And that way you'll get to see it. So I'm going to say so long for now, honey, and write when you can or send the tape back with the message. And be good, be careful, and bye-bye for now. Mike, I'll try and finish this off now. I watched the Cubs play the Dodgers this afternoon on TV. They beat them in the first game on TV 8-3. And then I listened to the second game on the radio. The Cubs won the second game off. So that's the biggest crowd that Ruger Field has had for 20 years. So it must have been close to 37,000, 38,000 people there. By the way, my mother was out to California, and she had her first copy of that all-hand come, so she said you were going to write him a hot letter, so you just saved your time. You won't need to write him. Apparently, they've started showing all the time now. Sounds like you had a real nice time when Mother and David was out to California. It was really lucky you got the six days off that you had. And, of course, since it don't count on your time, I prefer, again, furlough or leave time. I think that comes in pretty handy. David's sure proud of everything you give him, and I know that he had a real good time out there with you. And I think that he was glad to get home, but he kind of hated to leave out there also. But, of course, since we're going on this other trip, boy, he'll be in pretty good shape now for the rest of the summer. Everything here has been going real good. It's been a little hot all the last 10 days that your mother was gone. It's a nice and cooler day and a good, cool breeze, so all this week is supposed to be cooler than normal, so it won't be too bad. I don't know what happened to that radio of yours that you had in our room, the stamp room and radio room, it just fades out one day, so I think a tube has apparently burnt out of it, but I won't have anything done with it until you get home because I've got other radios I can play, but I think that's all wrong with it. The tube is burnt out probably. Of course, it has had a lot of playing, but no particular maintenance of any kind on it. It was a really nice bunch of pictures of Mother Brown, the ship docking and so forth. I know that David was quite thrilled with everything about the ship. His buddy down the street, his dad's in the Navy, that Dan Lodge, and he just got back from California, also seen his dad. I'm sure that they were going to do quite a bit of this, and the Navy talking between themselves about who ships the best. In case you, what happened in the PX or whatever you call it out there, run across one of those old radio effects I was telling you about that one, it was like, the price ain't too rough, go ahead and get it and just send it on home. I suppose, of course, you'd save more money in Hong Kong or some other place, but it won't get the rough abuse in shipments from California as it would from overseas someplace. So use your own judgment if you see one that you think will do the job, and it's not too rough on price-wise. Pick it up and send it on home with the wealth. Maybe Mother was telling you, but today we got the Cal cartridge cases out this morning, and he got some silver polished and he really polished him up. I don't know what he's going to make out of it. He's got some big idea planned to do with it. Sounds like Bill kind of likes that mess duty that he's into out there. Of course, that ain't a bad goal really for him. He don't have to work too hard and he's got a lot of free time to mess around in. So that's just, and of course he'll be able to get just what he wants to eat when he wants to eat it. So that's right down his alley. Well, it looks like this tape is getting pretty close to running out. I don't have too much to say. So I'll sign off for now. Take care of yourself and let us hear from you whenever you can. So goodbye for now, Mike. Be good and be careful. Thank you. Boom.

segments.text: Hello, Mother, Dad, and David. This is Wednesday afternoon, the 31st of July, and I received a
tape you made on the 28th this afternoon. It's about a quarter after 2 right now, and I've got
duty. Of course, that's the reason why I'm aboard. Otherwise, I'm sure I'd be gone. Most of the
other guys have left the ship by now and things are pretty quiet around here. So I figure
I go ahead and answer your tape now while I've got the time. No, not too much has happened
here on the ship or too much has happened actually since I last saw you when you left
Saturday morning early. I got back in San Diego Saturday morning about quarter after
and arrived back at the ship about 3.30 in the morning.
And I had to stand the first watch from 8 to 12 in the morning.
And I was rather tired, but I took a shower before I went on watch.
And that afternoon I slept quite a bit, and I stood another watch that night.
So it wasn't too bad at all.
Sunday, I went out to SeaWorld with a group from the USO.
and it's a very nice place out there.
You might have heard about it before.
It's similar to Marineland in the Pacific,
which is up by Los Angeles somewhere.
It's got a lot of nice attractions out there.
They've got porpoises and whales and sharks and things like that.
It's a pretty interesting place to go.
I didn't take my camera with me
because it didn't look like a very good day for taking pictures
and I'd never been there before.
I didn't know exactly what they had to take pictures of.
But I'm going to go back out there again some other time just to take pictures.
Tomorrow is Thursday, and it'll be payday here on board the ship,
and I'll be drawing about $119 for two weeks' work, if you want to call it that.
We've been getting off here pretty early in the afternoon, I should say,
actually in the morning for Liberty.
Our division officer is letting us go about 11 o'clock in the morning.
And so that gives us a chance to get away from the ship a lot earlier than most of the rest of the people do.
We have very little work to do.
All we have to do is just clean up any more spaces that have become dirty overnight or anything like that.
And we've got a few troubleshooting jobs that we're just taking our time on here, working on the radar.
But other than that, things have been going along pretty quiet.
and there's not really too much that has to be done.
Tomorrow is Friday, as I mentioned before,
and I plan on going over to the exchange
and buying a few needed items or items I think I need
and do a little bit of shopping around.
I'll also look for that radio that you mentioned on the tape.
I'm sure I can get one out here, the kind that you want,
but I know the price won't be too steep,
So there's a pretty good chance that I'll be keeping an eye open for one when I go over there tomorrow afternoon.
And I'll sure hook one up if I can find one that's suitable.
I received a letter from Allied the other day stating that the turntable that I ordered had been shipped.
and I believe it was shipped last Wednesday from their warehouse.
So you ought to be getting it pretty soon,
and make sure that when it arrives that you open it up and see that it doesn't have anything broken or anything,
and you might go ahead and set it up so it'll be all set up and ready to go with the rest of the stuff when it arrives at home.
one thing I do ask though if you do decide to set up all this stereo equipment that you do remember
everything that I told you and also read the instructions for everything very carefully
because I myself don't even know what the instructions for the turntable are going to be
like uh what you might have to do to operate it or anything but uh of course read the instructions
for that real carefully read over the instructions for everything else and it'll all work out all
right when you get it set up, I'm sure.
Well, Mother, I'll answer your question that you asked me in the tape
about the tipping from the newspaper that we didn't send a plastic sheet.
I don't believe I did send them home with you.
I believe that I still have them out here at George and Mary's house,
and they're in a box that I'm going to have sent home with some other stuff.
And when this box arrives, it's a small box.
Actually, one that you sent something to me in while I was overseas.
so you'll recognize it when it comes and open it up it's got all kinds of newspaper clippings and
souvenirs and things like this you open it up and see if it's in there and if it's not we'll
have to look for it somewhere else but i'm quite sure that's where it's at i put it in there with
some of those things i mentioned to you that i was going to send it home i didn't mention that
i was going to send it home with you or what i'm pretty sure that's where it's at well tomorrow
morning i'll probably leave the ship early in the morning or i don't mean early in the morning
around noon as we've been doing most this week when we've got liberty and I'll go to the exchange
and do some shopping and buy what I want to and go on downtown and slip into my civilian clothes.
I'll probably take in a movie in the afternoon. I've got a free movie pass and there's a new movie
showing in one of the theaters. I just started playing today and I'll probably take it in and
after it's over with I might go down to the library and do a little bit of studying on one

and I had my box that I keep this tape recorder in right now that I'm talking on I had it on the
