And we've still got a couple more that are still up for transfer, and they'll probably be leaving real soon. And we've got one more F.T. that's going to be leaving us. about six days and then about the 15th of next month we've got another FTC that's going to be leaving and no sign of replacements yet either this makes things kind of tight on the rest of us and It certainly doesn't look like we're going to be getting anybody to replace these people I don't know why I believe the ship's trying to do something about this because We've been having a lot of people leave the ship this week, and last week getting transferred to other duty stations or actually getting off of active duty. It's not that we really need the people real bad, but it makes things a little bit easier for the rest of us, and there's going to be some time when we will be going back out to sea again and we're going to need these people. And the best thing to do is to get them down so they can be getting worked into the routine of the ship and be getting trained in what their new duties are going to be. So I know any new people that report to our division will be welcomed very well, and I certainly hope that in due time we do get some more people in here to kind of help things work out a little bit smoother. This is one big reason why the ship has such a tight-leave policy as it did and that their liberty was not going to be so good. Now, I don't know about the other divisions, but our division's been getting pretty good liberty. As I said, we get to leave about 11 o'clock every day. Actually, liberty doesn't go until 3.30 in the afternoon, but if we've got all of our work done and all of our spaces cleaned up and anything that's been assigned to us to do for that day, if we've got it done, we usually get to leave. and some of the other divisions in the ship have been working it this way. So everybody seems to be pretty happy. It turned out a little bit better than what we thought it would. So I guess as long as everybody's happy, it's going to hang a count. Oh, and that letter that I received from Bill there last week while I was up in Georgia Maze, he mentioned that he'd be sending me a tape real soon and that he'd received the tape that I mailed him a few weeks ago. And that he felt that he was pretty sure he was going to buy a tape recorder from Allied. He was going to order one from them because they don't have any over there at the exchange or anything like that. So he sounded like he was going to be sending me a tape pretty soon. I haven't received it yet, of course. And I suppose if he is sending one at all, if it is one on his way, I'll probably receive it in about three or four days. I read the clippings that you sent me from the newspaper there by the hospital. It sounds like a pretty odd incident that happened out there. I know it could be a very serious thing there, a fire in a hospital like that, because things can just get carried away, and there can be an awful lot of innocent people hurt. I also read the clipping there about Connie's wedding, and I tell you, it brought such tears to my eyes, I could barely carry on to read it. But I got over it, and I'm sure that Bill would really like to have a clipping like that for his scrapbook. So I'll hang on to it, and later on maybe I can give it to him. All I can say to him is I wish him a lot of luck because I know that they're going to need it real bad. Mother, do you remember this space here on the ship where we work at? I know I showed you where we stowed away all of our souvenirs and boxes and everything we bought overseas. Well, if you remember correctly where it's at, the other night we had the air conditioner shut off because they shut off the power to do some work somewhere. And when they shut it off, it's caused the water to back flood into this, what we call the shaft alley. And we got about two or three inches of water on the deck. And you can imagine what would have happened if that stuff was still back in there. A lot of it would get wet. and I had my box that I keep this tape recorder in right now that I'm talking on I had it on the deck down in there and uh tape recorder would I had it wrapped up in a plastic bag and I had this in styrofoam inside the box and the box itself got real wet and it was totally destroyed it wasn't good but uh the styrofoam and the plastic bag kept the tape recorder dry and everything else in there and it wasn't damaged at all so i i've taken it out of that area right there and i'm i'm keeping it here in this uh publications locker the little closet like with the combination lock on the door actually that's where i'm sitting at right now while i'm talking on this tape so you'll know just exactly where i'm at and uh so some of the guys got down there yesterday morning and they got that water out of there. We've been getting our electrical power from the pier. Usually when a ship is in port tied up to a pier, they usually leave one of their boilers on to drive a generator to provide the electrical power. Well, we've shut down all the boilers and all the generators here on the ship, and we're pulling our power off the pier. And the other night when I came back from Liberty, most of the lights were off throughout the ship, and they had these emergency battle lanterns on, which I showed you, these little yellow lanterns. And they're battery-operated, of course, and they were on. And they had an emergency generator running on the ship. They were cleaning out one of the switchboards. It's a big electrical panel-like. They were cleaning it out, so they had to shut off all the power to do so. And this is one reason why our air conditioner system back-fluttered on us. And this generator was located right above our living compartment. And, oh, it made such a racket. Boy, it was really noisy. But I believe I did fall asleep. But when they shut it off, I could hear it going down as it was being shut off. And it woke me up. But as soon as it completed winding out when it was shut off, I fell right back to sleep. But I thought it was going to be a pretty rough night of sleep with that thing running all the time. I believe they set off about 1.30 in the morning, so I didn't get too much of my sleep disturbed then. Well, some of the things that I sent home with you, I hope you found places to put them and been able to put them with some of my stuff, some of my souvenirs and little things that I sent home. And when the rest of my stuff comes home, especially the box with the souvenirs in it and things like that, just throw them into a larger box somewhere or put them in a drawer of mine, and when I come home next time, I'll have to go through a lot of my things and throw away and keep and sort things out and relocate them. I suppose that Bill and I are probably getting a few things piled up there that we send home and that we will eventually be bringing home with us. So we've got a little job of house cleaning ahead of us next time we both come home. Well, like I said, tomorrow's payday, and I'm looking forward to it pretty well. that $60 that I put out on that turntable and that $65 that I put out on that movie projector kind of set me back a little bit. But this time I plan on saving at least $50 or so of my pay this week and having it put in the bank. About putting my money in the bank, I've been thinking pretty seriously about opening a checking account out here so I could put my money in the bank, have a place to put it and also if I wanted to draw anything out of it it would be a little bit easier to get to so I'm going to hold on to about $50 out of my pay tomorrow and ask around some of the guys here what would be a good bank to have a checking account with and I believe that I'll start a checking account out here in one of the banks but if I don't I'll go ahead and continue to send money on home to you. But I think it would be a little bit more convenient for me in the respect that I can put the money in the bank and if I have to draw it out for anything, I can get to it. One thing about this, I can be saving up money to come home on leave and when I want to, I can draw about $200 out of the checking account out here and just come on home on leave with that money. Otherwise, I'd have to have you draw money out for me or I'd have to be saving some of my payback every week. And I think it would be a little bit more convenient for me out here. So that would be one of the things I'm going to either do tomorrow afternoon or sometime Friday. I'm thinking pretty seriously about opening a checking account out here. I believe it's the Bank of America that they have out here. It's a pretty good place. They've got branches all over the state, and it's a pretty reputable bank. and I imagine I'll probably end up opening a checking account with one of their branches somewhere. Well, I'm just about run out of news right now. Like I said before in the tape, it's been pretty quiet around here. Not too much has happened. I haven't done very much. And I always look forward to the next day or whatever because there's always something new coming up. There's plenty of activities happening here in San Diego, sporting events, everything like that. so there's plenty to keep busy with on the liberty and uh i hope to be able to buy a ticket for the football game saturday night and i hope to go out there so i'll let you hear from me pretty soon and everybody take care back here david you'll be a good boy too and they have a lot of fun there this summer what's left of it that is and uh everybody have a good time on a vacation up to Canada. So I'll see you later. So long. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you Thank you.

1968-08-01.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-08-01.text:
1 Aug. 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got that tape and really enjoyed it a lot. By the way do you still have your little Sony? If so I'll send G.M. a tape real soon.

I got paid again today, and this makes my 9th month as P.F.C. I wish they'd get their shit together and promote me.

Now man listen to this, a little paper we get over here 2 times a month had a little article in it. It said anyone who has less than 6 mo. left in the Corps when they return from Nam get out early. So if I'm lucky I'll get out in 15 mos instead of 24. Sorry you squids don't get it. (ha ha ha)

Its been fairly quiet the past week over here. But we did have 2 V.C. firing in at us one nite, so every one was in the trenches then the word was passed "FREE FIRE" so me and the cooks I work with opened up on where they was at. I fired 36 rounds in a 15 yd. area where the firing was coming from. So if those V.C. were still there they probly got their ass blown off or the shit scared out of them.

Well I've got only 18 more days left on mess duty. I am trying to get on patrols as a radio man. They said if there was an opening when I got off mess duty I could get on.

And I am going to try and take my R&R either Oct or Nov. I don't know where I want to go for sure yet.

In another 4 days I'll have been in Nam for 6 mos., the time sure has flown for me. I got only 207 more days left over here in this hole.

Oh yea day before yesterday when had a flame tank down here burning the weeds from the barb wire, they caught some of the gooks huts on fire. Which I thought was real funny, I also got some good flicks of it too.

Well as you said all the girls in Cal. look good to you, I just hope they stay that way when I got back to the "big USA."

Its still good and hot over here and it seems to keep getting hotter every day. Also the liberty still sucks, you know I like not at all. Be looking for a tape and some slides heading your way from me soon.

Well I guess I'll be going for now. Write again soon.

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. "SEE THE
BAL LIBERTY SPOTS
JOIN THE CORPS"

1968-08-10.label: Vigilance — Page 17
1968-08-10.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-08-10.text:
HOPE ASSEMBLES STARS

BENEFIT SHOW NETS $180,000 FOR NEW USO

Story by JO3 Barry L. Spigener
Photos by PH2 Michael Fox

Occasions are rare when Bob Hope, Raquel Welch, Andy Williams, Kaye Stevens, 8,000 Navy and
Marine recruits and 50,000 other people get together for the same purpose, but that's what
happened recently when the Bob Hope USO Show was presented in San Diego.

The show was presented to raise money for a new USO building to be built in San Diego. The San
Diego Stadium was packed one warm Saturday night in May by people who paid from $2.50 to $500 to
see the show. The audience was the largest assembled west of the Mississippi River for a show since
World War II.

The show began at 8:45 p.m. with the massing of the colors by six high school ROTC color guard
units. As the crowd settled down, the Bob Hope USO Girls, 20 San Diego area girls clad in blue
mini skirts and knee-high boots, paraded onto the stage. They had a rather unsettling effect on
the 8,000 recruits seated around the stage area. As they departed, the Les Brown Band struck up
"Thanks For The Memories" and Bob Hope came up the runway onto the stage.

He opened with a bombardment of jokes that was to continue periodically for nearly four hours.
Quipped Hope, "I've been entertaining our fighting men at different universities around the
country. It's nice to sit here and see the real McCoy."

The audience surrounded the stage which was situated near the football field's goal line, and he
had to keep moving around to cover the entire audience. "I feel like Twiggy on a topless bar,"
joked Hope.

Motioning to the recruits seated on the playing field near the stage, Hope remarked, "That's not
a bad spot. It's on the goal line, but the Chargers never get there anyway."

Blonde Marilyn Maxwell, who has been appearing in USO shows since World War II, slithered onstage
in a tight-fitting black dress and said, "Hi fellows." She was warmly received.

After singing "That's Why The Lady Is A Tramp" and "A Good Man Is Hard To Find", she joined Hope
in a duet of "It's Delightful" with Hope putting in an occasional "It's".

The next singer was Bruce Cloud, who sang "Impossible Dream". Hope noted it might well have been
dedicated to Harold Stassen.

Singer Elaine Dunn was the next entertainer. She received cheers from the men in the audience when
she whipped off her long skirt, revealing spangled tights, and did a rousing song and dance routine.

While the other entertainers were performing, Hope sat by the runway near the recruits,
occasionally chatting with some of them, and signing autographs.

Following a quick appearance by Archie Moore, the Honey, Ltd. group performed. The four girls had
no trouble keeping the males in the audience entertained.

[Photo: Bob Hope studies the stage area at the San Diego Stadium before beginning rehearsal for
the USO Benefit.]

1968-08-10.label: Vigilance — Page 18
1968-08-10.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-08-10.text:
[Photo: IT MUST BE FUNNY-Hope breaks up as he runs through part of his act during afternoon
rehearsal.]

[Photo (Top Right): ---AND OVER HERE WE HAVE-"Ole Ski-Nose" consults with an aide about the proper
placement of the entertainers for the Benefit.]

[Photo (Lower Right): CONCENTRATION-Raquel Welch studies her music before rehearsing for the
evening performance.]

1968-08-10.label: Vigilance — Page 19
1968-08-10.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-08-10.text:
SHOW ACCLAIMED WEST'S LARGEST

Kaye Stevens, a singer who knows how to hold an audience, did just that with her songs and jokes.

The Youth of America, a group of teenagers from the San Francisco area, appeared next and put on
an impressive display of talent. A volunteer non-profit group that includes a band, chorus and
dance group, they greatly impressed the audience.

The show, scheduled to begin at 8 p.m., and run for three hours, had been running nearly that long
when it broke for intermission at 11:30 p.m.

The show got underway again after a 15-minute intermission. The Harper's Bizarre, a folk-rock
group, opened the second half of the show and had the audience join them in a lengthy audience-
participation number. Although the show was running longer than expected, the audience's enthusiasm
indicated they didn't mind at all.

[Photo: DETAILS-Hope and staff go over last minute details to ensure a smooth-running show.]

[Photo: "I'M NEXT?"-Andy Williams stands around the sidelines waiting for his chance to rehearse.]

1968-08-10.label: Vigilance — Page 20
1968-08-10.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-08-10.text:
Next to be introduced was Raquel Welch. She appeared in a long, white gown and slinked around the
stage, bringing cheers from the recruits on the field as she sang and traded remarks with Hope.

When the show was almost over, a Marine who had recently returned from Vietnam and was recovering
from wounds at Balboa Hospital presented Bob Hope with the first "GI Joe" award, for service
"above and beyond the call as an American".

As Hope clutched the 40-inch trophy in one hand, the 58,750 people attending the show gave him a
standing ovation. The comedian was visibly touched by both the award and the crowd's reaction.
Momentarily speechless, he finally managed to speak, as the cheers and applause continued, "I'm so
damn proud of you guys." Speaking of the trophy he said, "This is the best thing I have ever
received in my life."

Concluding the show was Andy Williams. He sang several songs, including "Born Free", "Honey" and
"Moon River", his theme song.

Hope, along with Raquel Welch, Kaye Stevens and Les Brown, had arrived earlier in the day by plane
from Los Angeles. They were met at the San Diego airport by the Bob Hope USO Girls, a Navy band and
various city officials, including Mayor Frank Curran.

Also on hand was the Commandant of the 11th Naval District, Rear Admiral Marshall F. Dornin.
Speaking to the Admiral, Hope said, "I appreciate your getting up this early — I thought admirals
never got up before noon." He continued, "I had an uncle in the Navy, Admiral Tuna, chicken of
the sea."

Mayor Curran gave Hope a special Award of Merit. He hung it around Hope's neck and bussed him on
both cheeks. Seldom at a loss for words, Hope remarked, "You better watch that. With the way de
Gaulle is going, you may be next."

Hope and the others left the airport and went to the stadium where they spent the afternoon
rehearsing under a blazing sun.

Approximately $180,000 was raised for the building fund by the show, combined with the $100,000
previously collected, assures a new USO building for San Diego.

The new building will be constructed at Pacific Highway and Market Street and will have recreational
rooms for games, a room for dancing, movies or parties, a reading room and an area where men may
shower and store clothing. The building is expected to be finished by Christmas, 1968.

[Photo: SOCK IT TO 'EM-Keeping the men intrigued was easy for Raquel Welch (left) as she sings
to the crowded arena.]

[Photo: ENTHUSIASM-Kaye Stevens breaks up the crowd with her animated styling of a song.]

1968-08-10.label: Vigilance — Page 21
1968-08-10.attribution: Vigilance, Cruiser-Destroyer Group publication, August 1968 — Ducy Family Archives
1968-08-10.text:
Although a lot was said about the show, probably the comment that sums up most people's feelings
came from a young sailor. He said the show "left me a little misty-eyed. Those are great people.
Imagine Andy Williams standing out there among all those bugs and insects to help us out. Fantastic!"

And as Bob Hope himself said, "It was a hell of a show."

[Photo (Above Left): "MR. HOPE, PLEASE"-While other performers are on stage, Hope sits with the
recruits signing autographs.]

[Photo (Above Right): VETERANS-Wounded Vietnam veterans brought from Balboa Naval Hospital wait
near the stage for the beginning of the show.]

[Photo (Bottom): "IT'S DELIGHTFUL"-Marilyn Maxwell and Bob Hope opening the show with a duet of
"It's Delightful".]

1968-08-20.label: Tape 11, Side 1 — Mike Ducy
1968-08-20.attribution: Audio cassette recording, Tape 11, Side 1 — Mike Ducy. Transcribed by OpenAI Whisper. Ducy Family Archives

segments.text: Hello, Mother, Dad, and David. This is Mike speaking. This is the 20th of August, Tuesday, about 9 o'clock in the evening.
We just got back in from being out on operations last night and all day today.
The ship got back in about 6 o'clock this evening.
I've got duty today. That's the reason why I'm aboard now.
I had to stand part of a four hour watch actually I only had to stand about 45 minutes of it because
our getting into port at the time that we did I didn't have to stand the whole watch
so I'm pretty lucky in that respect
it's uh seemed rather strange going out to sea after being in port for just one month
how many days we had in port here it's about 32 days I think since we got back from overseas
and it seemed just like the same routine that we had over there so it wasn't
anything new. We'll be going back out again tomorrow night about 7 o'clock and
returning Thursday night about 5 o'clock in the afternoon and of course we'll be
in port for over the weekend and we're due to go out again next week Monday and
Tuesday for the same type of operation and I understand after we return to port
Tuesday night we are to have 45 straight days in port before we go out again so
it sounds like things are looking pretty good for the future well after I talked
to you on the phone of a Georgia maze the last weekend I finished my weekend
up there at their house in a usual manner played cards there Sunday night
and I caught a midnight bus back to San Diego and arrived here about 2 30 in the morning
and I had duty Monday morning of course but I had to watch in the afternoon
but it wasn't a very bad day after all Monday last week I didn't do too much I usually stayed
aboard the ship in the evening I'm getting kind of tired of going into town every night it's getting
to be the same old thing.
This weekend, I...
Pardon me, I mean last weekend,
which is the weekend of the
16th, 17th, and 18th,
I had duty
Friday night on the 16th.
The 17th,
which was Saturday,
I went to San Diego
and watched the Chargers play the Steelers
that night
at the stadium. The Chargers lost it
by a score of
33 to
It was a pretty good game.
The Steelers played pretty good football and it was a good game all the way.
The Chargers are supposed to play the Rams this Saturday night and unfortunately I can't
see that game because I have duty.
It disappoints me somewhat because I know it's going to be a pretty good game and there
will be a pretty big crowd out there.
I stayed overnight in San Diego.
I got myself a room for $4 for one night.
I got some pretty good sleep that weekend and Sunday I ran into a buddy of mine who
went through A school with me.
He's on a ship out here and we took in a couple of shows and we just messed around for the
rest of the day and we went out for supper.
So I came on back to the ship rather early.
I did do my laundry in town, my civilian clothes have to be washed occasionally, you know.
So I worked them out the laundrette there in town.
And after I got them done, I came on back to the ship.
And we went out to sea yesterday afternoon.
Here we are back again on Tuesday.
So that's what I've been up to since I last talked to you.
Not too much of anything.
I received a tape and some slides from Bill.
And I suppose you've got them by now.
I parsed around and I meant to mail them over the weekend.
I had them in an envelope and all ready to go.
but I didn't get around to buying any stamps to put on them,
and I horsed around.
I didn't mail them until yesterday afternoon.
So you should have got them sooner than what you did,
but due to the fact that I didn't mail them any sooner than what I did,
that's why the short delay in your getting them after I received them.
I'm pretty glad to hear from him, and from what he says on the tape,
he's got a tape recorder, so I suppose we'll be hearing from him by tape more often.
I hope so. It's rather hard to tell, though.
I received my box of checks and my checking book, checking account book that is, from
the Bank of America out here last week.
And would you believe they spelled my first name wrong.
They spelled it M-I-C-H-A-L-E instead of the proper way.
So Saturday when I went into town I took my checkbook with me and my checks and I was
going to the bank and was going to return them to them and have them give me a new set
of checks. Well, the bank was closed on Saturday morning, so I was unfortunate due to the fact
that I could not return the checks, and I can't do it this week because of being out
at sea and having to stand duty also. So I'm going to have to try to get in there Friday
sometime. We'll be in Fort Friday, so I suppose I'll at least go in there Friday morning or
Friday afternoon, whenever I can, and return these checks to them so I can wait for another
two weeks for them to send me a new set of checks. This makes me rather mad about this
situation, but there's not too much I can do about it. I'll just have to keep using
the checks that they gave me when I opened the account. I also wanted to put some money
in the bank and I couldn't do that because the bank was closed. So it's kind of a bad situation.
I did receive one check in the mail, which is very welcome. Last week, I received my $100
Vietnam Veterans Bonus from the Illinois Veterans Commission, which I applied for over two and a
half months ago. And it finally came and I imagine Bill will probably be getting his real soon also.
So he applied for his about the same time I did.
And I'm sure that he'll be welcome to get this money as well as I was.
I plan on putting it in the bank.
I earn to keep my taking account at a good level.
I want to keep the balance over $100.
And this would be a good way to get the balance up.
And I'm going to try to keep it above $100.
Speaking about football, the Bears and the Packers were televised out here
on national television.
And I didn't have an opportunity to see the game
because I was on the radar as we were leaving port for CD sale,
but one of the other guys told me about the game.
And, of course, the Bears won it 10-7,

and I don't know what the next year's got in store for it,

So Sunday, I'm not too sure about that.

That's the big thing.

rather hot at this time of the year.
Out here it's really nice.

and now it gets down pretty chilly out here in Harvard.

So the temperature dips down pretty low, down to 60, somewhere around there,

We've been operating southeast.
Not southeast.

i might mention about the last tape i received from you which was around the 13th of last month
uh i believe you sent it just before you came out here

So you might be hearing something from him about that,

1968-08-20.text: Hello, Mother, Dad, and David. This is Mike speaking. This is the 20th of August, Tuesday, about 9 o'clock in the evening. We just got back in from being out on operations last night and all day today. The ship got back in about 6 o'clock this evening. I've got duty today. That's the reason why I'm aboard now. I had to stand part of a four hour watch actually I only had to stand about 45 minutes of it because our getting into port at the time that we did I didn't have to stand the whole watch so I'm pretty lucky in that respect it's uh seemed rather strange going out to sea after being in port for just one month how many days we had in port here it's about 32 days I think since we got back from overseas and it seemed just like the same routine that we had over there so it wasn't anything new. We'll be going back out again tomorrow night about 7 o'clock and returning Thursday night about 5 o'clock in the afternoon and of course we'll be in port for over the weekend and we're due to go out again next week Monday and Tuesday for the same type of operation and I understand after we return to port Tuesday night we are to have 45 straight days in port before we go out again so it sounds like things are looking pretty good for the future well after I talked to you on the phone of a Georgia maze the last weekend I finished my weekend up there at their house in a usual manner played cards there Sunday night and I caught a midnight bus back to San Diego and arrived here about 2 30 in the morning and I had duty Monday morning of course but I had to watch in the afternoon but it wasn't a very bad day after all Monday last week I didn't do too much I usually stayed aboard the ship in the evening I'm getting kind of tired of going into town every night it's getting to be the same old thing. This weekend, I... Pardon me, I mean last weekend, which is the weekend of the 16th, 17th, and 18th, I had duty Friday night on the 16th. The 17th, which was Saturday, I went to San Diego and watched the Chargers play the Steelers that night at the stadium. The Chargers lost it by a score of 33 to It was a pretty good game. The Steelers played pretty good football and it was a good game all the way. The Chargers are supposed to play the Rams this Saturday night and unfortunately I can't see that game because I have duty. It disappoints me somewhat because I know it's going to be a pretty good game and there will be a pretty big crowd out there. I stayed overnight in San Diego. I got myself a room for $4 for one night. I got some pretty good sleep that weekend and Sunday I ran into a buddy of mine who went through A school with me. He's on a ship out here and we took in a couple of shows and we just messed around for the rest of the day and we went out for supper. So I came on back to the ship rather early. I did do my laundry in town, my civilian clothes have to be washed occasionally, you know. So I worked them out the laundrette there in town. And after I got them done, I came on back to the ship. And we went out to sea yesterday afternoon. Here we are back again on Tuesday. So that's what I've been up to since I last talked to you. Not too much of anything. I received a tape and some slides from Bill. And I suppose you've got them by now. I parsed around and I meant to mail them over the weekend. I had them in an envelope and all ready to go. but I didn't get around to buying any stamps to put on them, and I horsed around. I didn't mail them until yesterday afternoon. So you should have got them sooner than what you did, but due to the fact that I didn't mail them any sooner than what I did, that's why the short delay in your getting them after I received them. I'm pretty glad to hear from him, and from what he says on the tape, he's got a tape recorder, so I suppose we'll be hearing from him by tape more often. I hope so. It's rather hard to tell, though. I received my box of checks and my checking book, checking account book that is, from the Bank of America out here last week. And would you believe they spelled my first name wrong. They spelled it M-I-C-H-A-L-E instead of the proper way. So Saturday when I went into town I took my checkbook with me and my checks and I was going to the bank and was going to return them to them and have them give me a new set of checks. Well, the bank was closed on Saturday morning, so I was unfortunate due to the fact that I could not return the checks, and I can't do it this week because of being out at sea and having to stand duty also. So I'm going to have to try to get in there Friday sometime. We'll be in Fort Friday, so I suppose I'll at least go in there Friday morning or Friday afternoon, whenever I can, and return these checks to them so I can wait for another two weeks for them to send me a new set of checks. This makes me rather mad about this situation, but there's not too much I can do about it. I'll just have to keep using the checks that they gave me when I opened the account. I also wanted to put some money in the bank and I couldn't do that because the bank was closed. So it's kind of a bad situation. I did receive one check in the mail, which is very welcome. Last week, I received my $100 Vietnam Veterans Bonus from the Illinois Veterans Commission, which I applied for over two and a half months ago. And it finally came and I imagine Bill will probably be getting his real soon also. So he applied for his about the same time I did. And I'm sure that he'll be welcome to get this money as well as I was. I plan on putting it in the bank. I earn to keep my taking account at a good level. I want to keep the balance over $100. And this would be a good way to get the balance up. And I'm going to try to keep it above $100. Speaking about football, the Bears and the Packers were televised out here on national television. And I didn't have an opportunity to see the game because I was on the radar as we were leaving port for CD sale, but one of the other guys told me about the game. And, of course, the Bears won it 10-7, and I hear the Bears had a real good touchdown run, about a 77-yard run on the second place in scrimmage at the beginning of the game. And I wish I could have seen it, but I suppose when the football season gets into full swing, I'll have the opportunity to watch a few games on television, and I hope the Bears have a pretty good season. I've been watching the baseball standings pretty closely, and the Cubs are sure to have dropped back into fourth place or somewhere around there. I hear they won a game this afternoon in ten innings, six to five, I believe. So I suppose they'll probably be back up in second place again if they can get a couple more wins. of course it looks like the Cardinals are right on top and I suppose they'll stay there until World Series time they probably got the pennant all sewed up I did read an article in the sports column in the newspaper out here the sports writer was commenting on how the Cubs were building the hopes up of their fans and their followers by winning games like they were and giving the fans World Series hope. It seemed that he felt that even if the Cubs did win 23 of their next 26 games or whatever they have, they could still not win the World Series. I'm sorry, they could not win the National League pennant. And if the Cardinals lost 26 of their next 28 games, the Cubs would only finish two games out of first place and they could never do it. So he was kind of belittling the Cubs team for filling up the hopes of their fans and followers by having such a hot winning streak like they have. Of course, San Diego has got their answer to all baseball teams out here. They've got the San Diego Padres who will become a National League team next year. and they're not so hot themselves. They've got a few Cubs players who used to play for the Cubs. They've got a guy by the name of Billy Cowan and one other guy who played shortstop or second base. I can't remember the name right now. I might think of it later. But I haven't went out to see them play or anything, but I usually follow them in the newspaper and see how they've been doing. And they're not a very hot team. I just finished typing up a letter to the Reserve Center letting them know of my activities for the last couple of months or so. Since I last wrote to them, I received a typewritten letter from an officer down there about a week ago telling me that he received my last letter. And he posted it on the bulletin board down there. And they found it rather interesting. And he'd like to hear from me again if I had anything new to say. So I wrote to them and told them about the equator crossing and about returning back to the state. And so I'll be mailing that off with this tape and they'll have something else to post down here on the bulletin board for the new recruits to read. Last week I believe it was on Wednesday I took a little guided excursion cruise out here in the harbor which I've passed through many times on the ship but only cost me 75 cents and that lasted for an hour and it's a little tour they take you around the harbor and they explain various points of interest and everything to you and I shot up two and a half rolls of movie film I supposed to go back out and pick them up next week I took them out to the MCRD to the base out there where Bill went to boot camp at as a matter of fact to have a film of process because I took them out there I took them Saturday to be developed and uh I didn't want to come back out here to the base to the exchange because it was too far it's a lot closer when you're in town in San Diego to go to the MCRD if you're going to go to the exchange and and buy anything or take film in to be processed, it's much more closer, more convenient. So the film's out there, and I'll go back out Friday and pick it up. I'll take it up to Georgia Maze with me some weekend and show it and slice it all together with the rest of my film. Well, after I talked to you on the phone there Sunday at Georgia Maze while I was there, you said you'd wrote a letter to me and asked me if I got it well I said I had and we discussed that it would probably be waiting for me on a ship when I got back that night and it was it was postmark August 7th from Messina New York and it was wrote on Princess Hotel stationery so this was probably the one you wrote in Canada and I've also got one other letter here that you wrote on August 1st right after you got back home from your visit out here and I didn't answer that because I believe we talked on the phone shortly after that also so I got two letters here that I haven't answered because we've had the opportunity to talk on the phone so I guess we're all getting kind of lazy on letter writing and that's one reason why I'm making this tape because I've got an extra cartridge here and just feel it's a little bit easier to talk and say what I had to do and say what I had to say rather than to try to write it down. Well in case you're still wondering about my foot I went up there last Monday after I talked to you on the phone I said I was going up there and We were going to give them an ultimatum. Well, I went up there, and they discussed it among the three corpsmen and the medical officer, and they came up with the conclusion that what they would do, I would come in there twice a week on Monday and Friday, and they would put this acid on there. They would not cut any dead skin off of it because that's what was irritating or making it hurt. So they would just put acid on there and let it kill as much as possible. In the meantime, I like to try to keep it dry by keeping a bandage pad on it that they put on there, and they gave me a couple of extra ones. And then when I take a shower, if at all possible, to wrap my foot in a plastic bag to keep it dry. And then when I get out of the shower, if I want to wash my foot, I can wash it separately. So it's shown quite a bit of improvement. I imagine all that growth in there is dying away now. I was just in there yesterday, Monday, and it looked pretty good. And they put some more acid on it, and I'll be going in again Friday. It doesn't hurt to walk on it quite as much as it used to, and it's not quite as sore, so I think it's showing some improvement. And someday, after they've probably got enough of this acid on there and they've killed enough of it, they can cut it out and it won't irritate it or it won't hurt me. and the other night I was laying in my rack on my stomach and I moved into a middle rack. I used to sleep on a top rack but now I've moved into a middle one which is a lot nicer so there's the rack right above me now. I was laying on my stomach and I raised my feet up to pull a blanket underneath them and I hit my heel on the top rack and oh man that hurt. I'm not kidding. Navy Exchange Mobile Canteen is on the pair. I'm not kidding. It really hurt. And I just thought I was going to shout out in pain. But the pain went away within a few minutes, and it didn't hurt anymore. I guess it was pretty tender. And the funny thing about it, after that happened, it seems like it hasn't hurt quite as much for some reason. I don't know. But I'm pretty well satisfied with it. It's not bothering me like it used to. It still irritates me to stand on it for a while or to put too much weight on it. But as far as I'm concerned, it's showing signs of improvement, and I'm pretty well satisfied with what they're doing up there for us. So I don't think we've got too much more to worry about. It'll probably all grow out, and they'll be able to take care of it within a pretty short time. Well, they just passed the word that the Mobile Canteen is out on the pier, so I'm going to go out and get a coke or something else and I'll be back in in a minute to finish up the rest of this tape. Oh, here I am back again. I went out and got a hamburger and a can of fop and I ate the hamburger and I got the can of fop sitting right here on the table. We're still tied up here at pier four, the pier that we came in on when you saw the ship come back from overseas. When we come back in Thursday evening, we're supposed to tie up at Pier 2, which is a lot better pier. It's a lot closer to the Exchange and the movie theater and everything else. Everyone likes to go to Pier 2 because the piers on down towards here, they're a little bit farther away from the main activities on the base. David, I saw a jellyfish in the water off the side of the ship this evening after we got back in. It was really a big one. It's one of the biggest ones I've ever seen. It was about 20 inches long and about a foot round. It looked like, you know, you see them, they look like just a big mass of membrane and tissue and everything. They're kind of a whitish color. And you don't ever want to go swimming where there's any of those either. because they can attack a person and I don't know what they do. I guess they've got stingers or something in them. I don't know what they are, but they're pretty dangerous for swimmers who are in the water. But I don't think we'll see any of them back there in Illinois in any of the pools or any of the lakes back there because they sure as hell may be a saltwater animal of some type. Well, if you were watching our calendars fairly close last Friday night, you noticed that last Friday was the 16th of August, and that was my one-year happy anniversary here in the United States Navy on active duty, which is really a great thrill. I've got 361 days left, and I'm going to start counting the days right now. It's a little bit easier to keep track of them now that I've got less than a year. and I don't know what the next year's got in store for it, but I'm pretty sure it's full of surprises just like this last year is that Bill will be celebrating his one year sometime this week. I imagine it's probably the 23rd, and I suppose you'll be hearing about that in one of his letters as he's halfway through and he's on the downhill ride. Well, I don't know whether Georgia Mae is back here now once you receive this tape and when you play it, but in case she is and she has a chance to listen to it, I hope they had a nice trip back, and I hope they have an even nicer and safer trip on the way back home to California. I don't know when I'll be able to make it up there again. They haven't said anything about changing our duty sections, So as I told them before I left, I'll probably be back for either the first weekend or the second weekend of September. There's nothing definite yet, so it'll probably be sometime around there. It appears to me right now that they aren't going to change the duty sections back to where you'll have two weekends off, one weekend duty where you stay aboard the ship, and one weekend where you only have two days off. So it doesn't look like it's going to improve any. It'll probably stay to the point where we only have one weekend off and split weekends for the rest of the month. So it doesn't look like they're going to change it yet for a while, but they'll probably let us know in advance of any changes that they are going to make. While I was having duty this Saturday, I don't have any definite plans for over the weekend. And I suppose I'll probably go in Friday afternoon or evening into town and try to get my checks taken care of. I plan on buying a couple more pairs of pants over here at the base of the exchange. And I'll probably take them out and have them washed with the laundrette so I'll be able to be worn whenever I want to. I might buy a pair of shoes Friday night also. So Sunday, I'm not too sure about that. Probably go to church in town somewhere Sunday morning like I did last Sunday. Probably taking a show Sunday afternoon. They've got a couple in town that I'd like to see but I haven't seen yet. So it doesn't look like any great thing for the weekend is planned, but I usually find something to do, something to occupy my time, and actually it's just something to spend my money on. That's the big thing. Well, I suppose the weather back there is probably rather warm and humid, rather hot at this time of the year. Out here it's really nice. It gets up in the upper 70s during the daytime, and now it gets down pretty chilly out here in Harvard. As a matter of fact, last Friday when I stood the 12 o'clock to 4 o'clock in the morning watch, I stood to watch with my pea coat on. You'll probably laugh when you hear this, but of course I was wearing white with a pea coat on in order to keep warm. So the temperature dips down pretty low, down to 60, somewhere around there, and it gets rather chilly out here. But in town during the daytime, it's really nice. The weather, as a matter of fact, out at sea, it was real nice and sunny. It was a little bit windy because the ship was going at a pretty good clip of speed. But otherwise, it was real nice and sunny and clear out there. We've been operating southeast. Not southeast. That would put us inland somewhere in Mexico. We've been operating southwest of here about 160 miles. And, oh, the sea was real smooth out there. It wasn't rough or anything like that. I hear some of the beaches they've been having pretty rough surf because of some weather which is coming down from Antarctica or something like that, but on down southwest of here where we were operating at and where we will continue to operate at for the next operations that we go out on, the sea was fairly calm and smooth and the weather was real nice. I've got an idea here. I'm going to go ahead and ask you and see what your opinion on it is. this money that I have in the bank back home, being the rather large sum that it is, would it be possible for me to put it in a bank, credit union of some type, for one year in order to draw 5% interest on it or whatever it is? If it would be 5% of the amount that I have, I would figure I would earn $50 in one year. Would it be possible I could put this in a bank for one year and take it out at the end of the year? say perhaps I put it in here sometime late in August and when I get out next August I would take it out and I would have a little bit of money that has been added on to it to the interest that it built up over the year you might check on the Carpenters Credit Union and see what the story is on that that'd be one of the best places to find out and let me know what you find out if I could just put it in for a year or whatever the case is because uh i don't plan on spending it yet and uh why not make a few dollars off of it if i can so let me know what you find out about this i might mention about the last tape i received from you which was around the 13th of last month uh i believe you sent it just before you came out here I received it and I played it and it sounded all right it wasn't scratchy or anything like the other tape was the one that was all bad and distorted and everything and I believe you probably had a bad tape there this oxide coating on it probably wasn't very good and it was just a poor tape so I don't think there's anything really wrong with your tape recorder and uh you're going to send a tape on back to me just make a little bit of a test recording on it and play it back yourself and see what it sounds like to give an indication of whether you've got a good tape or not. But otherwise, their last tape sounded real good and it didn't have any distortion that the other previous tapes did have. I received one letter from Bill just before I received the tape on the slide, and he mentioned that his message would be over in 12 days or something and he was going to put in for a radio operator's duty whereas he would go out on these patrols with the rest of the troops and he would probably be a pack type radio operator and he said that they would give this to him if they had an opening for it so So you might be hearing something from him about that, and he'll probably be letting you know just what kind of a job he's going to be doing next. But this is what he told me in the letter. In case if you haven't heard anything about this yet, I thought I'd pass this information on to you. We haven't been very busy here on the ship for the past few days. Yesterday we found that we had a bad break solenoid in our gun director. which is an electrical component and it had become overheated and was shorted out and it kept blowing fuses so we took it out and we tried to get a part number off of it so we could order a new one well we were not very successful in doing this because the information that was stamped on it was not adequate so we could find a part number so we took what information was I took it in hand myself and they sent me downtown to the Naval Supply Center, which is down at the end of Broadway Street, down by the Broadway Fairs. I'm sure Dad probably knows where this is at. And I got a pretty big deal down there, pretty big operation, pretty big complex. So I borrowed one of the trucks from the ship and I drove down there and tried to get some information on it so we could order a new one and they couldn't help us out too much so tomorrow we're going to go over here on the base and look around and see if we can find a replacement for it or whatever or see how we can order one and that's about all we've got scheduled for tomorrow besides going out tomorrow evening about seven o'clock back out to sea but i suppose our early liberty like we have been getting since we got back in the states i suppose this isn't going to be in existence any longer because I'm sure they're going to get us back down to where we're conforming to a rigid schedule of doing this and that and everything like this so they you could say the holiday is over with and it's time to go back to work actually so they going to start planning all kinds of little things for us like material inspections on the ships to make sure the spaces are all clean once a week and little things like this. So they're getting back down to the way they were before we left the state. And the fun is over with, and it's time to get back to business now. So we've had all of our good delivery that we're going to get. And we're all eagerly looking forward to going back overseas again. You can be very assured of that. Ha ha. So we've got a pretty tight schedule from here on out and one good thing about it though, we'll be in port for quite a while to come. You have these little operations you go out on for three or four days. They seem rather worthless and useless and a waste of time, but somebody's got to go out there and do it. So everyone has to take their turn and we're no exception. Well, my tape isn't starting to run out yet, but I'm starting to run out of information and things to say, and my eyes are getting a little heavy. Oh, I've got, speaking about my eyes, I've got one thing to tell you. I, as I was out at the laundrette the other night, that Sunday night doing my laundry, I took off my glasses and I was wiping them off with a paper towel. And as I was doing that, they broke right in the middle in the nose piece that goes over your eyes, my civilian glasses, and my black ones with a black frame. So I couldn't wear them anymore, so when I got on the bus to go back downtown, while I was finishing my laundry, I had to play blind man, practically, and go without any glasses. And I didn't, I had to ride the bus back to town without any glasses and go back to the locker club and i put my i was ready to go back to the ship anyway and i went came back to the ship without any glasses on i've got a pair of glasses that i wear here on the ship to my ones the navy issued to me and i'm wearing them now so i plan on excuse me i plan on going over on the base either sometime this week or next week and getting a new set of frames for my lenses that i have now so that they're rather inexpensive i believe here from the navy exchange here on the base their optical department which they have so it'll probably run me about seven dollars for a new set of frames for my glasses i don't know why they broke i didn't realize i was putting that much pressure on them or anything and i imagine that they were old and they probably might have a slight crack in them anyway but uh that's just one of those things so i'll have to take care of that next week. Seems like there's always something coming up. Thank you.

1968-08-23.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-08-23.text:
August 23, 1968
Friday 9:00 PM

Dear Mother & Dad,
     Here are a few lines to let you know I got your August 18 letter Wednesday and the letter of the 21st today. No doubt you have got my tape by now.
     I stood duty for a guy yesterday and charged him $7.50 for it. I am standing duty today for another guy but this one is free. And tomorrow I have duty myself. So I am spending three days in a row aboard without liberty. Sunday I plan on going into town and go to Mass then out to eat. In the afternoon I am going to a show then wash out some new pants at the laundromat.
     We have a two-day operating schedule next week that will conclude Thursday then its 7 straight weeks in port 'till our next exercise in the second or third week of October.
     Did you have any trouble operating the slide projector? How does the radio pick up Chicago stations?
     I didn't buy groceries at the exchange the last time I was at G.M.'s. She said she had enough food but sent me and John out a couple of times for groceries. I am willing to help them out but since she has advertized the fact around the neighborhood I am not going to offer to do it again. She should know better. When I saw the top of the sales slip on the page of the letter I didn't know what you put it there for but I see now. That saying makes a lot of sense. Anyway I think they are too lazy to drive over there to get groceries.
     I have an appointment at the clinic on the base for next Wednesday to have my foot looked at and worked on. I guess you don't have to raise hell with them just keep coming to sick call until they wise up and realize they can't do much for you. I must admit though that it feels a lot better and doesn't hurt to walk on so much. But it has to come off before it has a chance to cause too much trouble (if it already hasn't).
     Well its time to get a shower and hit the rack. I have the 4-8 watch in the morning. I'll write again next week. Bye for now.

                    Your son,
                         Mike

segments.text: Hello Mike, I'm like you, I think it's about as easy to make a tape as it is to sit down
and write a letter anymore.
We received your tape last Thursday and we all enjoyed it very much.
I've heard it about three times now
and I finally realized
the best way for anyone to hear it
was to come down here
and from up the street
and listen to it if they so desired
there was quite a bit of commotion going on up there
as you no doubt realize
and so I told Grandma last
we had a tape
that if she wanted to come down and listen to it
why she was welcome to
and she did come down
and that did give her a few minutes break away from the hubbub.
And then Sunday, yesterday, John and Jeremy Mabel came down for a little while
and so then they listened to it and Bull was here and he heard it.
This is Monday and about 3 o'clock in the afternoon
and the Pritchetts got away this morning about 4.30.
they planned on stopping down in Missouri at one of the caves and I imagine that they got down there
about the right time and to have breakfast and then go on the tour of the caves which would mean
that they got away from St. Louis maybe or away from Missouri uh oh probably about 10 o'clock
They plan on being home by noon our time on Wednesday.
But if they don't make it until Thursday, they aren't going to worry about it.
They would like to take it a little easier going home than the way they came out here.
David and I just got back from out to Dave and Gene's,
a place where they balance wheels and such as that.
And our Chevy is needing some work done on it,
and I'm trying to get it all done before this week's over,
so I won't have to worry about it once my school starts.
I took David out to the Lincoln Homestead site Friday evening,
and his patrol went on a weekend overnight camp out.
And I unloaded them at the bridge
because they planned on walking in
as part of their different ones requirements.
And I turned around and I started back home
and the car wanted to die on me.
It wasn't getting any gas.
That's the way it acted.
Well, to make a long story short,
I barely made it into
Winkle's Corner
a filling station there
and he tinkered around with it
and thought maybe it was vapor locked
and so forth and so on
and I finally
I should have been home by
no later than 5.30
or no later than
quarter to 6 at least
and I got home about 6.15
and I managed to get it
in the drive
so the Saturday morning I took it over to
a binkson and they put a new gas filter on it and then it still wasn't acting right between
there and home so I turned around yesterday and I took it back over there and it died on me in
Talley's parking lot and it had to be pushed then up into the filling station so today they put a
new pump on the carburetor and there was a hole in it they said and a new water hose which was rotten
and I had this appointment made for the balance the wheels and see how why the car was shimmying
and so forth so I should have it in pretty pretty good shape the only thing left that I know of is
the clutch is slipping so I'll get that done there's no big rush about it though and besides
that Friday afternoon I had John put on an oil cleaner, so I now have a France oil cleaner
in the Chevy. So I hope that it does the job, and we was all laughing and kidding him that
ever since I've had that oil cleaner put in, why I've been having trouble with the car.
But it seems he really had good luck on this oil cleaner business back here, and I can't
really remember how many he did sell but i know he put on six cleaners and one of those six was
was one that he had given grandpa for his birthday so he actually sold five of them uh plus don
took three which are uh without any doubt sold and he left six uh at grandpa's so that uh
If anyone comes along that wants them, they'll be here in town.
And I imagine that those will be gone before too long.
He signed up three salesmen back here, which is very, very good as far as he's concerned.
That gives him an extra percentage, too, from the way I understand it.
So they took only one box of cleaners home with them.
And they had come out here with, I think, 22.
so they were real happy about that I believe all that brought any on his side
of the family was one brother and he finailed a little deal about that he
said he ought to get his wholesale so he got his for instead of paying the 29
something while he got his for 19 something which made George Bailey a little unhappy
but I know that they are glad to be on their way home and uh I know that that uh it isn't
it isn't uh all the same when you would when you've been away and they're the kids were
old they were real good really but uh mother and daddy uh just aren't like they used to be
and they're older and and um Georgia Mae's been away just too many years and uh there was a lot
of difficulties that went back and forth and I hear Georgia Mae's side and then I hear mother's
side and I was getting the beginning to get a little bit fed up with both of them and because
As I told you, they're both of them so near alive.
But they managed to get through the week without any big blowups,
so that's all that's necessary.
But Grandpa said, Believe you me, I don't intend to go out there.
I want to go out there when Bill comes home,
but I don't give a damn whether I ever get out there or not.
And he just couldn't understand her at all.
Well, nobody could understand him either.
we were up at uh up there taking pictures yesterday morning after they got back from church
and i had my instamatic on the picnic table and she better had hers on the picnic table
which we were through taking pictures and they had already taken one of the uh one picture
with a polaroid and it hadn't turned out good and they took they took another one and it turned out
good. It was just perfect. Well, then he turned the Polaroid over to John to take pictures of us
four together, the mother and daddy, George and me, and it didn't turn out any good. Well,
we figured it was John that didn't know how to work it right, so he tried it again,
and still no good. Well, out of a clear blue sky, Grandpa took that camera mic, that Polaroid,
and he started banging it on the picnic table.
And he banged it against that picnic table about two or three times,
and I'm not kidding you, we all of us nearly dropped our teeth.
The first thing I could think of was he was going to hit those Instamatic cameras,
and that was making me mad because he had lost his mind.
Well, Becky was sitting on the seat at the picnic table,
and it scared the daylights out of her.
and John had gone into the garage to throw the Polaroid papers away that you have
and the pictures that weren't any good and he didn't know what had happened
and I'm not kidding you, we were all fit to be tied.
And he soon got over it.
I mean, he had to resolve it with why he threw the Polaroid in the garbage can
and I went over there and got it out and I said, I'm taking that home.
I'm going to save that for evidence.
Well, I mainly brought home to show it to Dan and to David, or to your dad and David.
And so later on in the afternoon, why,
Avis and Donna and her bunch came over and they made ice cream.
I think they made three gallons of homemade ice cream.
And he was all right.
He was bragging about what he'd done.
He said he wasn't going to be worried about that damn thing anymore.
And he'd worried with it all these years,
and he wasn't going to be worried with it anymore.
and so mother said well she was glad it was gone she'd heard all she wanted to hear about it so
i guess everybody's happy but boy that's one heck of a way to do when you got a item that
cost that much and there had been some darn good pictures taken with that thing but it's just him
and if it wasn't him then there's uh no reason why it couldn't have been checked out to see what
was wrong with it but you know how he is and i guess one other incident he went into the garage
to do to find something and he couldn't find it and there was a couple of broom breaks in there
i suppose grandma had been using them and she hadn't put them where she where they belong
and he picked them up and he threw them clear cross back into the garage well that was something
george may hadn't seen before either and so i imagine all this that i'm telling you you'll
all about it and there'll be probably little elaborations go along with it.
But she's darn glad she lives out there and I'm glad I live where I live but
there's times when I wish I lived a little bit farther.
Well I just played this tape back and in different spots to see how it was doing
and it seems to be doing all right. I think you are partly right that
it isn't working, or that the tape was bad, and I don't think it's the recorder itself,
other than the fact that the thing doesn't want to rewind at different times like it
should, but there again, I think it's the tapes.
These tapes were made in Mexico, and I think that they're cheaper, and I think that the
quality just isn't what they ought to be.
and there again you get what you pay for.
We had such hot weather last week that it was just almost unbearable.
And I didn't, well I was busy, but what I did was sit in front of the fan at the sewing machine practically the whole week
and I felt that at least I was accomplishing something
but this house looks like that's all I did was sit.
So I had really planned on, I had made up my mind that it was going to be cool this week
and in fact I was hoping it would be
and I would get some much needed cleaning done
but uh oh a day or two ago grandma mentioned that she wanted uh to clean out her jungle in the
backyard all that shrubbery and stuff and uh so i said okay if it's it's gonna if it's cool
monday why we'll get it and get it done and so that it's over with for the rest of the week
but she doesn't plan on working all this week either they don't really need her over there
and so she's going to take advantage of having this week off to get things cleaned up
and some stuff done that she wants to do.
And maybe Friday, if Grandpa isn't working,
I think they and the camels are going to take a short trip.
Where to, I don't know, but they're talking about taking off for a long weekend,
which will be nice for them, and I hope they do get to go.
So, would you know it, Saturday it began to cool off a little bit.
It wasn't quite so bad.
And Sunday, yesterday, was a beautiful day.
In fact, it was cool enough early in the morning that you could use a sweater.
And last night, we walked up to about 8.30.
I kept thinking maybe
I had a feeling you wouldn't get my
quick short note that I mailed
Thursday afternoon
about calling us
but we waited until about 8.30
and didn't get any phone calls from you
so Daddy had said we would walk up
up there and tell
the Georgia man John goodbye
and I had already told the kids goodbye
late that afternoon
because I knew they would be in bed by the time
we went up there in the evening
and when we walked up there yesterday evening I had to wear a sweater and it was just a week
ago yesterday we were just mothering and it was rather hard on the bridges because they're just
not used to this humidity and of course I think the air conditioner that was installed a week
ago today was harder on them in many ways than the heat but anyway today it was really nice this
morning and and it was cool enough i wore a sweater up there to grandma's and we got started
oh about quarter till eight on the the shrug and the snow barb ocean the mock orange and that
and my gosh we've got i know tom jones's truck probably wouldn't hold it all that we cut out of
there. And I would say about 10, 30, or 11, we were through, and she had rented a bed
from one of the rental places, so she wanted to take that back. And I wanted to go to the
post office, of course, and since I didn't have any car, why? She said, well, we'd just
do both. And David had to go over to a scout patrol meeting, which only lasted for about
30-40 minutes and he went over there when he come back why he went with us and we got all that done
so then I come home and I had started to move four peonies from the driveway to the backyard
along the fence and they're the ones I believe I wrote and told you that the drunk next door
backed into and I had planned on moving some of them anyway this fall and I moved some last fall
out of it from under the tree there along the driveway because the shade doesn't help them any
to do what they should do so I had moved them last fall and they didn't do any good this this year to
blew them but they will next so now I decided to move the four that Joan backed into and
because I was going to move them anyway and so I dug started to get ready to dig them up yesterday
and that ground was so hard that spade wouldn't even budge the ground so I turned the hose on
that part and let it soak up real good but the backyard was soft enough to dig so I got the four
holes dug that I was going to need and yesterday and so I can do all that work up there at
Gravel's while I still had my work clothes on while I went ahead and saw if I couldn't
get those peonies transplanted so I did and they're all transplanted now and I trimmed
them back and they look pretty nice so that part of my fire work is done and in the meantime
why about one o'clock the Chevy was done from over at Bingston's and I went over and got in
and come back by and picked up David and we went out there to Gene's then on North Water and we
sat there for about an hour while he worked on the wheels and it wasn't too bad it wasn't as bad as
I thought it was going to be, and he didn't, I really can trust him, so it only cost me
nine dollars to get the wheels lined and the shoes cleaned, and there was an awful lot
of play in the steering wheel, so he took care of that too, and so I feel like that
everything will be okay now.
So tomorrow morning I hope to get up
and get started on this house.
I've got some ironing to do.
And then I've got to get uptown
one day this week
and get my new white shoes
and white hose
and a pair of bandage scissors
and go to the bank
and get some money out of the bank
for the school tuition.
and get that taken care of.
But I'll have Friday that David has to go to school all day that day.
And so I really could do all I had to do that one day as far as that's concerned.
Even if I went uptown that morning after he left and the stores were open,
why, I can get it done by the time he would go home for lunch.
and uh thursday i've been called to help register the kids for thursday so that makes me happy i
can go up there and help do something otherwise uh you're limited when when you work and and
so they called me the other day want to know if i'd help and and i said yes i could well they
was only going to ask me to help for the two hours, either in the morning or the afternoon,
and I told her I could help both times if that would help them, which it would.
So I go up there Thursday morning and work from 10 until 12 and then back from 1 until 3
and get the kids all registered to start the school full day Friday.
Then they're out Saturday, Sunday, and Monday for Labor Day,
and they go back then the 3rd and start their full-time schedule.
And, of course, as I told you, that's the day I start, too, on the 3rd.
And that same day, same night, the 3rd, I have the Marine meeting here,
and I imagine there's going to be a few unkind words said that night
because I've got a few of them planned myself.
We had our rummage sale, and it was a flop, and it was plenty hot that day.
and evening, the evening that we started and the next day.
And as it turned out, which is nothing too unusual, there wasn't enough help.
And it was very, very disgusting.
And there's many things to be said.
And so I'm not the only one that's going to have plenty to say at this meeting.
And as I told them, since it's going to be in my own house, I guess I can say what I damn well please,
which I fully intend to.
I no doubt will pay my dues for the following year
which are due in September
but as far as participating to the full extent
as I have for the past year
I am not going to worry about it at all.
And I've already been advised by Tinky Fryfogle
not to get involved in anything
because of this coming school year
and I told her I didn't intend to.
She's got herself a good job.
She's been asked and chosen, and she's accepted,
to teach the student nurses, the RN student nurses in the clinical end.
And Ed were here the other night after I got home from the family potluck out to Avisus.
And as usual, your dad and David had come on home early, and I stayed on.
When I got home, they'd been here about 20 minutes, and we'd sit here and talk for a while.
She's really excited about her new job, too.
She will have real good hours from 8 to 4, I think it is, and no Saturdays and Sundays.
Then she'll have holidays off and everything.
So this working mostly all weekends and two or three nights through the week from 3 to 11 or 11 to 7,
whichever they happen to ask her to work, why those hours are over with.
But she has enjoyed it all, and this is going to be quite a challenge for her, and she's real happy about it.
So she's given me a lot of confidence, and a good friend of hers is going to be one of my instructors.
I think there's about four instructors up there at the LPN class.
And the notice that I got about what to do the first day,
it said that it's going to be the largest class that they've ever had.
So maybe there will be a few of them that feel the same as I do,

Well, we went out to Shakey's last Wednesday night. It was so blasted hot, as I have mentioned, and on the night before, your dad had said, don't fix any supper tonight, don't get the kitchen hot, and just have a cold lunch.
Well, I managed to put something on the table, and none of us was really too hungry, so we got by.
Well, then I had asked George May if we couldn't make plans to go out to Shakey's one night,
and I'd have him down here for lasagna one other night, and it seems as though we couldn't get together.
Of course, the week was short, and John did have his family to go see and so forth,
but we never did get together, but we managed to have some good visits together.
But anyway, we had decided that if John and Georgia could go, why would we go on Wednesday night?
So on Wednesday night, we decided to go anyway to Shaggy's,
whether George and me and John could go or not,
because it was so hot again that I didn't want to cook.
And it didn't make your dad unhappy because it was cool out there with the air conditioning.
So we went out there, and we really had a good time.
And that place was packed.
I guess everybody else had the same idea that it would be cool out there.
And I never did see that.
And, well, I had made the remark that I'd like to do that parking lot full just one time.
Well, it wasn't full, but Friday night, David was gone to this overnight camp out,
and your dad had to go to an apprentice meeting.
And so he told me that when he got through the meeting,
he knew why we'd go out for just a little while,
and we'd have a small pizza and listen to the music.
so when he he picked me up about 10 15 and we went out there and my gosh that parking lot was just
low pack and the inside was too so they really had a good crowd and
oh well we was out there Wednesday night while we took the tape recorder along
and uh and the crowd pinned out a little bit why uh where it wasn't quite so noisy

but it doesn't to us, but it sure does on a tape.
and the idea was that we'd re-tape it and send you a few lines or a few verses

But we had to tape some of it onto a tape of Bill's type of tape
and then re-tape it on one for you.
But I'm not going to worry about that too much.
And we had some of that tape also slipped or something.
It didn't sound just right.
And so I think, there again, it's the tape.
But I hate to send this thing in to get it worked on
because I hate to be without it.
But I'm beginning to see almost the end of this tape come up, so if I happen to run out of tape, I naturally turn it over.
And there's a slight possibility that your dad and David might have a few words to say, too.
But, in fact, well, I think I'll try to say some more.
since you didn't call about that slide projector whether you wanted it brought back or not why it
