1968-08-28.text: Hello Mike, I'm like you, I think it's about as easy to make a tape as it is to sit down and write a letter anymore. We received your tape last Thursday and we all enjoyed it very much. I've heard it about three times now and I finally realized the best way for anyone to hear it was to come down here and from up the street and listen to it if they so desired there was quite a bit of commotion going on up there as you no doubt realize and so I told Grandma last we had a tape that if she wanted to come down and listen to it why she was welcome to and she did come down and that did give her a few minutes break away from the hubbub. And then Sunday, yesterday, John and Jeremy Mabel came down for a little while and so then they listened to it and Bull was here and he heard it. This is Monday and about 3 o'clock in the afternoon and the Pritchetts got away this morning about 4.30. they planned on stopping down in Missouri at one of the caves and I imagine that they got down there about the right time and to have breakfast and then go on the tour of the caves which would mean that they got away from St. Louis maybe or away from Missouri uh oh probably about 10 o'clock They plan on being home by noon our time on Wednesday. But if they don't make it until Thursday, they aren't going to worry about it. They would like to take it a little easier going home than the way they came out here. David and I just got back from out to Dave and Gene's, a place where they balance wheels and such as that. And our Chevy is needing some work done on it, and I'm trying to get it all done before this week's over, so I won't have to worry about it once my school starts. I took David out to the Lincoln Homestead site Friday evening, and his patrol went on a weekend overnight camp out. And I unloaded them at the bridge because they planned on walking in as part of their different ones requirements. And I turned around and I started back home and the car wanted to die on me. It wasn't getting any gas. That's the way it acted. Well, to make a long story short, I barely made it into Winkle's Corner a filling station there and he tinkered around with it and thought maybe it was vapor locked and so forth and so on and I finally I should have been home by no later than 5.30 or no later than quarter to 6 at least and I got home about 6.15 and I managed to get it in the drive so the Saturday morning I took it over to a binkson and they put a new gas filter on it and then it still wasn't acting right between there and home so I turned around yesterday and I took it back over there and it died on me in Talley's parking lot and it had to be pushed then up into the filling station so today they put a new pump on the carburetor and there was a hole in it they said and a new water hose which was rotten and I had this appointment made for the balance the wheels and see how why the car was shimmying and so forth so I should have it in pretty pretty good shape the only thing left that I know of is the clutch is slipping so I'll get that done there's no big rush about it though and besides that Friday afternoon I had John put on an oil cleaner, so I now have a France oil cleaner in the Chevy. So I hope that it does the job, and we was all laughing and kidding him that ever since I've had that oil cleaner put in, why I've been having trouble with the car. But it seems he really had good luck on this oil cleaner business back here, and I can't really remember how many he did sell but i know he put on six cleaners and one of those six was was one that he had given grandpa for his birthday so he actually sold five of them uh plus don took three which are uh without any doubt sold and he left six uh at grandpa's so that uh If anyone comes along that wants them, they'll be here in town. And I imagine that those will be gone before too long. He signed up three salesmen back here, which is very, very good as far as he's concerned. That gives him an extra percentage, too, from the way I understand it. So they took only one box of cleaners home with them. And they had come out here with, I think, 22. so they were real happy about that I believe all that brought any on his side of the family was one brother and he finailed a little deal about that he said he ought to get his wholesale so he got his for instead of paying the 29 something while he got his for 19 something which made George Bailey a little unhappy but I know that they are glad to be on their way home and uh I know that that uh it isn't it isn't uh all the same when you would when you've been away and they're the kids were old they were real good really but uh mother and daddy uh just aren't like they used to be and they're older and and um Georgia Mae's been away just too many years and uh there was a lot of difficulties that went back and forth and I hear Georgia Mae's side and then I hear mother's side and I was getting the beginning to get a little bit fed up with both of them and because As I told you, they're both of them so near alive. But they managed to get through the week without any big blowups, so that's all that's necessary. But Grandpa said, Believe you me, I don't intend to go out there. I want to go out there when Bill comes home, but I don't give a damn whether I ever get out there or not. And he just couldn't understand her at all. Well, nobody could understand him either. we were up at uh up there taking pictures yesterday morning after they got back from church and i had my instamatic on the picnic table and she better had hers on the picnic table which we were through taking pictures and they had already taken one of the uh one picture with a polaroid and it hadn't turned out good and they took they took another one and it turned out good. It was just perfect. Well, then he turned the Polaroid over to John to take pictures of us four together, the mother and daddy, George and me, and it didn't turn out any good. Well, we figured it was John that didn't know how to work it right, so he tried it again, and still no good. Well, out of a clear blue sky, Grandpa took that camera mic, that Polaroid, and he started banging it on the picnic table. And he banged it against that picnic table about two or three times, and I'm not kidding you, we all of us nearly dropped our teeth. The first thing I could think of was he was going to hit those Instamatic cameras, and that was making me mad because he had lost his mind. Well, Becky was sitting on the seat at the picnic table, and it scared the daylights out of her. and John had gone into the garage to throw the Polaroid papers away that you have and the pictures that weren't any good and he didn't know what had happened and I'm not kidding you, we were all fit to be tied. And he soon got over it. I mean, he had to resolve it with why he threw the Polaroid in the garbage can and I went over there and got it out and I said, I'm taking that home. I'm going to save that for evidence. Well, I mainly brought home to show it to Dan and to David, or to your dad and David. And so later on in the afternoon, why, Avis and Donna and her bunch came over and they made ice cream. I think they made three gallons of homemade ice cream. And he was all right. He was bragging about what he'd done. He said he wasn't going to be worried about that damn thing anymore. And he'd worried with it all these years, and he wasn't going to be worried with it anymore. and so mother said well she was glad it was gone she'd heard all she wanted to hear about it so i guess everybody's happy but boy that's one heck of a way to do when you got a item that cost that much and there had been some darn good pictures taken with that thing but it's just him and if it wasn't him then there's uh no reason why it couldn't have been checked out to see what was wrong with it but you know how he is and i guess one other incident he went into the garage to do to find something and he couldn't find it and there was a couple of broom breaks in there i suppose grandma had been using them and she hadn't put them where she where they belong and he picked them up and he threw them clear cross back into the garage well that was something george may hadn't seen before either and so i imagine all this that i'm telling you you'll all about it and there'll be probably little elaborations go along with it. But she's darn glad she lives out there and I'm glad I live where I live but there's times when I wish I lived a little bit farther. Well I just played this tape back and in different spots to see how it was doing and it seems to be doing all right. I think you are partly right that it isn't working, or that the tape was bad, and I don't think it's the recorder itself, other than the fact that the thing doesn't want to rewind at different times like it should, but there again, I think it's the tapes. These tapes were made in Mexico, and I think that they're cheaper, and I think that the quality just isn't what they ought to be. and there again you get what you pay for. We had such hot weather last week that it was just almost unbearable. And I didn't, well I was busy, but what I did was sit in front of the fan at the sewing machine practically the whole week and I felt that at least I was accomplishing something but this house looks like that's all I did was sit. So I had really planned on, I had made up my mind that it was going to be cool this week and in fact I was hoping it would be and I would get some much needed cleaning done but uh oh a day or two ago grandma mentioned that she wanted uh to clean out her jungle in the backyard all that shrubbery and stuff and uh so i said okay if it's it's gonna if it's cool monday why we'll get it and get it done and so that it's over with for the rest of the week but she doesn't plan on working all this week either they don't really need her over there and so she's going to take advantage of having this week off to get things cleaned up and some stuff done that she wants to do. And maybe Friday, if Grandpa isn't working, I think they and the camels are going to take a short trip. Where to, I don't know, but they're talking about taking off for a long weekend, which will be nice for them, and I hope they do get to go. So, would you know it, Saturday it began to cool off a little bit. It wasn't quite so bad. And Sunday, yesterday, was a beautiful day. In fact, it was cool enough early in the morning that you could use a sweater. And last night, we walked up to about 8.30. I kept thinking maybe I had a feeling you wouldn't get my quick short note that I mailed Thursday afternoon about calling us but we waited until about 8.30 and didn't get any phone calls from you so Daddy had said we would walk up up there and tell the Georgia man John goodbye and I had already told the kids goodbye late that afternoon because I knew they would be in bed by the time we went up there in the evening and when we walked up there yesterday evening I had to wear a sweater and it was just a week ago yesterday we were just mothering and it was rather hard on the bridges because they're just not used to this humidity and of course I think the air conditioner that was installed a week ago today was harder on them in many ways than the heat but anyway today it was really nice this morning and and it was cool enough i wore a sweater up there to grandma's and we got started oh about quarter till eight on the the shrug and the snow barb ocean the mock orange and that and my gosh we've got i know tom jones's truck probably wouldn't hold it all that we cut out of there. And I would say about 10, 30, or 11, we were through, and she had rented a bed from one of the rental places, so she wanted to take that back. And I wanted to go to the post office, of course, and since I didn't have any car, why? She said, well, we'd just do both. And David had to go over to a scout patrol meeting, which only lasted for about 30-40 minutes and he went over there when he come back why he went with us and we got all that done so then I come home and I had started to move four peonies from the driveway to the backyard along the fence and they're the ones I believe I wrote and told you that the drunk next door backed into and I had planned on moving some of them anyway this fall and I moved some last fall out of it from under the tree there along the driveway because the shade doesn't help them any to do what they should do so I had moved them last fall and they didn't do any good this this year to blew them but they will next so now I decided to move the four that Joan backed into and because I was going to move them anyway and so I dug started to get ready to dig them up yesterday and that ground was so hard that spade wouldn't even budge the ground so I turned the hose on that part and let it soak up real good but the backyard was soft enough to dig so I got the four holes dug that I was going to need and yesterday and so I can do all that work up there at Gravel's while I still had my work clothes on while I went ahead and saw if I couldn't get those peonies transplanted so I did and they're all transplanted now and I trimmed them back and they look pretty nice so that part of my fire work is done and in the meantime why about one o'clock the Chevy was done from over at Bingston's and I went over and got in and come back by and picked up David and we went out there to Gene's then on North Water and we sat there for about an hour while he worked on the wheels and it wasn't too bad it wasn't as bad as I thought it was going to be, and he didn't, I really can trust him, so it only cost me nine dollars to get the wheels lined and the shoes cleaned, and there was an awful lot of play in the steering wheel, so he took care of that too, and so I feel like that everything will be okay now. So tomorrow morning I hope to get up and get started on this house. I've got some ironing to do. And then I've got to get uptown one day this week and get my new white shoes and white hose and a pair of bandage scissors and go to the bank and get some money out of the bank for the school tuition. and get that taken care of. But I'll have Friday that David has to go to school all day that day. And so I really could do all I had to do that one day as far as that's concerned. Even if I went uptown that morning after he left and the stores were open, why, I can get it done by the time he would go home for lunch. and uh thursday i've been called to help register the kids for thursday so that makes me happy i can go up there and help do something otherwise uh you're limited when when you work and and so they called me the other day want to know if i'd help and and i said yes i could well they was only going to ask me to help for the two hours, either in the morning or the afternoon, and I told her I could help both times if that would help them, which it would. So I go up there Thursday morning and work from 10 until 12 and then back from 1 until 3 and get the kids all registered to start the school full day Friday. Then they're out Saturday, Sunday, and Monday for Labor Day, and they go back then the 3rd and start their full-time schedule. And, of course, as I told you, that's the day I start, too, on the 3rd. And that same day, same night, the 3rd, I have the Marine meeting here, and I imagine there's going to be a few unkind words said that night because I've got a few of them planned myself. We had our rummage sale, and it was a flop, and it was plenty hot that day. and evening, the evening that we started and the next day. And as it turned out, which is nothing too unusual, there wasn't enough help. And it was very, very disgusting. And there's many things to be said. And it didn't make your dad unhappy because it was cool out there with the air conditioning. So we went out there, and we really had a good time. And that place was packed. segments.text: Well, as I was saying, there's no point in that slide projector being out there.
and if Bill, if and when he sends you any slides,
you can play the tape and look at the slides
the way you have done in the past
and if you want to fool with taking them up to Georgia Maze
and they have got a projector like Bill has,
so one little small individual one,
then, well, two people could look at it
at the same time and listen to the tape
and if you've already seen them
And then those kids are not interested in looking at those slides and listening to that tape.
And the next day that those kids go to bed, those slides can be looked at by George, May, and John.
And then that's all that's necessary.
So I made up my mind without hearing from you that the projector would stay here.
Well, when I got up there last night, my Georgia Maybann informed me that she didn't see any
point in taking it back either, that they would do something about getting one themselves
and they would see the slide some way.
But it's nice that they'll send them to you first so that you can see them because going
back and forth across the water isn't like it used to be when you were stationed over
there. And he had mentioned in a letter that I had got last week, the reason why he hadn't
sent those pictures was that he didn't have, with his sleeping during the day, he doesn't
get up until 4 o'clock most of the time, and by that time, the post office was closed.
So he hadn't been able to get any stamps to send them. But he was going to try to make
point of doing so the next day. So he may in the meantime have forgotten that he was
supposed to send them on to you. So if he does send them back home, why I will turn
around and send them to you along with our pictures from our trip to Canada which I forgot
to give George May to bring out to show you. I'm not going to worry about any slides or
of tapes that you may have, that you may have received from Bill, because I know that as
soon as they've been seen, I know that you'll get them sent on home.
But if he's going to make tapes with messages on them, we naturally will be wondering what
the tape would have to say on it.
And luckily, or thank goodness, he did say enough on this tape that he sent to explain what had been going on during the weeks that we had her frame.
He didn't say, but I kind of had a feeling that he felt that we weren't home and there wasn't any point in writing.
He didn't say so, but that's the feeling that I got.
But at least the tape did fill in for the three weeks that we didn't hear from you.
And after we did start hearing why, we got two letters in the same week and then we got
the slides and the tapes from you.
And after you had seen them.
And I can understand about that deal that you mentioned that you horsed around and didn't
get any stamps to send them.
Because the same thing happens on this end.
I fully intend to make a tape or write a letter to either one of you boys.
And the next day, I realize I haven't done it yet.
But my intentions are good always.
You should have in the mail in a very short time a short letter from the bank
and a card to fill out in regards to changing your checking account over to a savings account.
She explained it to me how it would work,
and I asked her if she would like to send a short letter to you explaining it,
and that way you would get it directly from the bank.
And maybe if I relayed the information on to you, I may not make it clear.
So she said she would.
So you would have to sign a card anyway.
I couldn't do it for you, and you can do it through the mail.
And I had talked to Marilyn Hatch on Thursday night about how their bank worked on that,
and you would have to, if you wanted to add any money to the savings account,
you would have to put in an even number of $100 or $200.
You couldn't put in $105 or $110.
You'd have to put in $100 savings each time you wanted to make a deposit.
But out there at the Pershing National Bank, it doesn't work that way.
But the only stipulation which this letter will state
is that you have to notify them within 90 days before you want to take any money out.
So you can do whatever you think.
I think it's 4% interest the other way.
And that is more than you would get from the credit union.
As far as I'm concerned, the credit union is fine for borrowing money,
but it doesn't pay the interest that the banks do.
and there's a good reason for that because they're not the business that the banks are.
So if you would like to, when you come home,
if you want to borrow the money from the credit union to buy a car or something,
you have got money in the, a small amount in the credit union,
which is already established and if you have a job or you have any backing,
well then you can borrow the money from the credit union and pay it back and leave that money there
as far as that's concerned and keep drawing interest for you until such a time that you really did need it.
But you can do some thinking on that at a later time or we can talk about it when you come home later along in the year.

He did say he was going to put in for his R&R and go down to Sydney, Australia for seven days. Well, of course, that'll be quite an experience for him. And Sydney, Australia, although I'd never been there, but I knew some fellas in the service that had been there. They say it's about like going to, oh, Chicago or New York or some other big town. They have everything there that our big cities in the United States have. And Sydney, I believe their population is probably considerable, over 2 million now. So it is a pretty big town. I don't know just how they, where them fellas sleep or how they take care of that when they're down there. They've had that, they've used Sydney for a rest area for a long time. They even used it during World War II. So no doubt they got pretty decent facilities for them to stay in while they're there. And I know that you can see a lot of sites. I told David that maybe Bill would send him home a baby kangaroo from down there. So, of course, David got all hopped up about Bill sending him a kangaroo. Of course, we know that's impossible, but David keeps hoping for the impossible, you know, like all kids his age would do. Well, I see David just pulling the yard on his bicycle. It looks like he's going to play out in a face pond since Mother didn't have any fish in there the biggest part of the summer. he's really used that fish pond to play in quite a bit. He's got boats and everything else in it. He made some boats, he calls them boats. They're nothing but pieces of wood with pop cans on the bottom for floats. I see his buddy also not just walking in the yard. It looks like he's got a gasoline engine of some kind. So Lord only knows what they're up to. I suppose some big deal where they're going to pump a lot of water. I don't know just what they're going to do, but I suppose I'll have to cut this off pretty soon and go out and get the situation stopped before it gets going too far because that's about all they need to do is start running a gasoline engine out there and neighbors on the north will start having a minor stroke or maybe a major stroke. You can't ever tell about that. I'm sorry to hear about you breaking your glasses, of course, but every time I get mine and wash them, I think the same thing can happen. That nose piece, of course, what I try to do is hold them on the nose piece there when I dry them, and instead of holding the other lens, and that might have been what happened. You had to hold it one side and was drying it, and that nose piece, of course, that the bridge there is not too heavy. I'm always afraid of breaking mine, but of course I don't have the extra pair. Of course, I've got the sunglasses that I could use. They'd be a little rough at night. So you ought to keep that in mind that if you possibly can, keep yourself an extra pair of glasses at all times. So if you break one pair, you've got another pair to fall back on. Of course you also probably didn't realize how important they were to you until you didn't have them and then you knew just how bad you didn't need glasses. I haven't done anything with this hi-fi stuff you sent home yet. I don't think I'm going to get in any hurry to do anything with it because I suppose the first time it gets hooked up or gets running Dave will have to be playing the records and everything else so I'm really not in any hurry to get it set up. I'm sure it will have two or three weeks but like I say I'm not getting overly ambitious about it because it'll be just as good when it does get hooked up and it's sure good looking outfit. I was quite surprised at the size of it and especially the receiver. It's way bigger than I anticipated seeing, but it does look awful nice. Well, I left this for a little bit. I went in to watch some of the proceedings on the convention. I suppose you've been following a little bit in the paper and will probably see it on some TV out there. They seem to think they're going to have a lot of trouble up in Chicago with riots and so forth. So they've got, I don't know, somebody said around 8,000 troops in Chicago. And tonight on the TV, they said for every three people that you've seen in the convention hall, I think they had two people to protect those three people. So it looks like they've got plenty of protection. I don't know whether it's all necessary or not, but then by the same token, some of these people think you never know what they're going to do next. So it probably is best that they take all these precautions to keep somebody from getting hurt or killed. However, I wouldn't be much surprised if they don't have a full-scale riot in the city of Chicago before this is over with. But then, of course, they would have probably had a riot of some kind anyway, whether they had the convention there or not. I was glad to hear you got to go out and watch Chargers play football. I think the American League, I see in the paper tonight, the American Football League has won 10 games against the National League this year, that is, in preseason games and lost only five. so it looks like they're doing pretty good for themselves. However, I do believe that the American Football League plays a little more right-open football than the NFL does. I just watched part of that game with the Bears and Green Bay on. That was a week ago tonight, last Monday night after I come home. I come home and stamp a little early and watched the last half of the second quarter and then the biggest part of the third quarter. and then I went to bed because I had to get up and go to Champaign the next day. So I turned in about 11 o'clock. I suppose the game actually lasted until almost midnight. So it looked like a real good game. That Sayers looked pretty good. I didn't see the run he made. I did see him carry two or three times, and that Livingston, he made some pretty fair runs also. And, of course, over this weekend, the Bears played Washington Redskins and beat them pretty bad. I think 43-10 or some such figure is that enough. They didn't have any problem. As a matter of fact, I think they had some third-string quarterback in the game the last quarter. I don't even remember his name. I think probably this week we're going to send this tape recorder in. and we still have trouble with the thing on the rewind. One of these caps in our hubs that drive it seems to slip or don't take a hold, so there's something wrong down inside of it. So I think we'll send it in and see if we can't get it fixed up. And then in case we do get it taped for me while it's gone, or Jake's got one that they'll pay on, we'll borrow Jake's and use it. Well, it looks like this tape is just about to run out. I can't hardly tell how much is left on here, so I'll say goodbye for now and take care of yourself and let us hear from you when you get time. That radio that we talked about, if you get a chance to get one, we're okay. If you don't and you make another cruise out in the Pacific, that'll be good enough too. but I can wait until any time is convenient for you to get it. So goodbye for now, Mike, and we'll all see you later. Thank you. Thank you.

1968-09-03.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-03.text:
Sept 3, 1968
Tuesday 4 PM

Dear Mother, Dad and David,
     I got your tape last Thursday and your letter Saturday. I was going to write over the weekend but kept putting it off. Now I am at the library here in San Diego and have been doing some studying on my course.
     Yesterday was of course a holiday for us too. I slept till about 1:00 PM then went over on the base and saw a movie. While there I ran into one of the guys who was in my class at Great Lakes. We talked for a while then he took me around his ship and showed me what it
was like. The ship is a troop transport and they carry around 1200 marines at one time when they are operating overseas.
     I plan on going up to G.M.'s this weekend for the usual visit. I am going to call her tomorrow night and see if it is alright and let them know I'll be there.
     I was glad that you decided to keep the projector with you. Anyway I don't believe we are going to be receiving that many slides from Bill and I can still see them with my slide viewer. How
they see them is their concern. I would hate to have had them bring it back out here then we wouldn't be getting any slides to see; which may be the case. So again I say "Good thinking."
     I listened to what you had to say about the savings account and in some ways I'm not too sure about it. As of yet I haven't got any information about it from the bank. I feel that I will need that money a year from now and maybe it would be useless to put it in a savings account. I just
feel that it could be earning me a few dollars in the meantime instead of just sitting there. One thing for sure is it won't rot away, at least for sometime.
     I thought that last Wednesday I was to have my foot taken care of. Well, I got the days mixed up and am due to go over on the base tomorrow morning to have them look at it. But, it doesn't hurt at all now so I don't know what they will do.
     I too was a little startled at the ordeal you told of about grandpa
and the camera. I thinks the whole trouble was that he may have had some old film and that was why the pictures wouldn't come out.
     I got a new set of frames last week. I had to get them here in town because they don't have any optical shops at any of the base exchanges around here. They are similar to my old ones and are guaranteed for one year against breakage. I paid $18 for them which I thought was a little high but I doubt if I could have saved much more
anywhere else the way the prices are on things out here.
     Our weather out here has been so nice I can hardly believe that it has been so hot at times back there. Right now its about 75° outside and real sunny.
     I can see dad's reasoning on buying the groceries at the exchange commissary. It does make sense to me but I am going to ask about it before I go up there this week. But like I said before, I don't think they are too eager to go over there and
take the time to get the stuff. Perhaps she feels she is taking advantage of my coming up there and may feel this isn't fair to me. She didn't seem too energetic about it last time I was there but if she mentions it again, I'll get the stuff providing its okay. Actually I think we are worrying about something that isn't really as bad as it seems.
     I am glad to hear that David conformed to the punishment that he had no doubt deserved. I do hope he can have a better year in school and finds it a little
easier to do the work. I guess I can say the same for you too, mother!
     We still have been getting early liberty on the ship every day. But the duty days we usually have two watches and it gets a little boring but its only one out of every four days so I guess its not too bad.
     They are installing some new electronic equipment in the gun plotting room where I work. It is an addition to our radar that should improve its performance somewhat. It should take about 5 more weeks before we can
use it and test it out.
     Be sure to let me know if you have any difficulties using the stereo equipment or in hooking it up. Again I'll ask, how does it recieve the Chicago radio stations? I just wonder about how sensitive it is with the antenna it has built in.
     I suppose I'll head back to the base early tonight. There is a good movie there tonight and I'd like to see it. I have seen most of the ones playing here in town and occasionally they have some good movies out there.
     Well I guess this letter is running rather long. I had better sign off before you get a postage due on it.
     I'll write again or make a tape in a week or so. See you later.

                    Your son,
                         Mike
1968-09-03.attribution: Letter, Mike Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-09-18.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-18.text:
Wednesday 18 Sept. '68
7:00 PM

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     Even though I just called last night I thought I'd write to answer your letter I received Monday. I could have talked on and on about all that I was going to do when I got out and how thrilled and surprized I was but you know how I feel about it. It seems like I get the good breaks without any trouble. So you see God must be watching over me. I certainly hope and pray that this holds up and that come November I can get this Navy off my back with the exception of the weekly drills.
     I was very pleased to hear that things are going smoother for Mother at the school. How is David doing so far?
     I called Georgia Mae night
after I talked with you. She was really surprized over it. I told her I might take a few of my 17 days leave and spend some time with them. But of course I explained this may not be possible due to our personell shortage here. I told her I would see them on the 4th, 5th, and 6th of October. She brought Johnny home from the hospital the Tuesday after he went in. He had acid in his stomach was the diagnosis she gave me.
     Of course I am now faced with the pleasant task of getting all of my belongings together and shipping them home. I have two small tape recorders, my movie projector and camera, and a lot of civilian clothes to get back there. I will wait until the first week of October
to get things ready.
     Due to this coming up here are a few things I no longer have to worry about;
     1. extending my active duty if I make second-class
     2. when to take leave
     3. getting transferred to another ship so I can make another cruise again.
Some of the shock of this matter is starting to wear off but I won't believe it until I step off that plane in Decatur during the month of November.
     I mentioned a little about my past weekend on the phone. I had duty Friday and that was a real ------. I got called on the carpet because some GM left some magazines open. But I had a good defense and a first-class FT who stood be-hind me. The words were
really flying and I don't think I have ever been so mad at anyone since I have been in here. Along this same line the GM's left a magazine open Monday night with the key still in the lock and it really hit the fan then. But the FT's have been cleared for all of this and the GM's don't get liberty until 1800 instead of the usual 1530.
     Saturday this FTG3 who works with me and is married picked me up when I got off duty and we went over to his place to put in a rear-seat speaker in his car and some gauges in the dash. We got all of our tools from the ship. The speaker went pretty smooth, but the gauges were a little rough. I took my movies and projector over and we watched them
Saturday night. I stayed overnight at their invitation. They are also Catholics so we went to church Sunday morning. That was a real experiance because the Mass was a folk mass. Do they have these back home? We finished up the gauges later in the day and it looks like a factory installed job now. They are both my age and seem to be pretty happy and pleasant people for being married, but I guess its because they have no kids running around the house to cause confusion and trouble.
     I am going to buy a lot of clothes here at the exchange and send home before November. I can save a few dollars this way. I would also like to get a 12 gauge shotgun out here. They have some nice
ones like Bills for $88.
     Well I had better go for now if I intend on going to the base movie. See you later. Bye.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

P.S.
     I will send the pictures back later.
1968-09-18.attribution: Letter, Mike Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-09-24.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-24.text:
Sept. 24, 1968
Tuesday

Dear Mother and Dad,
     Today I received the letter you wrote Saturday. I also have the one you wrote last Tuesday here to answer.
     So far nothing new has came up in the past week since I talked with you on the phone. As of yet I still don't know the magic day in November but have heard two different stories. One is that they will keep us 'till the last day of the month and the other is that you get separated on your usual discharge date which makes it on the 15th of the month.
     I am glad you were concerned about mentioning the car situation in the last letter. You are right it is not the kind of car I was looking for. So you can see that my answer is one of "not interested." I gave the situation a
lot of thought before and especially this past week. Of course to have a new car would be my wish but I realize that this is a little out of the question because it would be necessary to have a steady job and be well established before undertaking such a venture. How soon, after I get home, I will need the transportation of a car or will be able to afford it of course depends on the fact of getting a job. But I do think I will settle on a late model used Chevrolet or Pontiac.
     Sunday I ran into a guy who was in my class at Great Lakes. We went to Tijuana that afternoon and got back about 11 PM. That place is really something. It reminded me a lot of some of the overseas ports but most of the places are cleaner.
There were a lot of tourists and sightseers there. It is easy to get yourself in trouble down there but we managed to come back alive and healthy. I suppose I will go down one more time before I get out and buy some souviniers.
     The past two days have been somewhat of a heat-wave out here. It has been very warm and sunny the whole day instead of late morning and part of the afternoon as usual. We are due to shift into blues the middle of next month so I hope the weather is accomodating.
     Friday night I went out to the stadium and saw the U.S.D. Aztecs play Northern Illinois University in a football game there. The Aztecs won 40-13 and about 35,000 were there. Northern looked pretty bad but the Aztecs are
the number one team in their college bracket. This guy on the Aztecs made a 67 yard touchdown run and that really brought the crowd to its feet and was worth my admission price of $1.00 (military ½ price discount).
     Well I had better close here and get cleaned up so I can go to the base movie at 8:30. I'll be looking forward to hearing from you again and counting the days too. So long.

                    Your son,

                         Mike
1968-09-24.attribution: Letter, Mike Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-09-25.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-09-25.text:
Sept. 25, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got your letter you wrote the 19th today.

Well things with the Corps is same as before, "they suck."

Boy I guess you are really short, but there isn't much I can say about it but 151 days left over here. and hopping the same for the Corps.

I checked on my R&R and that ass hole SSgt. forgot to put my name down for it. So now I've got to wait till Nov. instead of Oct.

We just had a red alert, 2 rounds come busten balls over our heads. They didn't hit anywhere around that we could tell. Now all the "boots" that think their "salty" are telling sea storys. What a laugh!

I put in for my L/cpl. test today, and should be takin it soon.

I am also signed the pay roster, for $73.00 and sending $100.00 to the bank.

Sounds as if your liberty is starting to be fucked up. To bad squid, we don't get any over here.

I am going to be sending some books on Scott amps. see what you think about them. and which one will be the best cheapest ones. Then send me back your ideas, and then I'll order them.

Well I guess I'd best be goin for now. Write when ever you can, and I'll do the same.

Bye for now, and take care

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. I got my $100.00 from the State today. Have you got yours yet?
1968-09-25.attribution: Letter, Bill Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-09-27.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-27.text:
27 Sept. '68
San Diego

Dear Mother, Dad and David,
     Today I received a note letter from Bill on the 16th. Here are the pictures he finally sent. One funny thing is that he only used one 10¢ stamp and it wasn't cancelled. Also here are the pictures you sent me.
     Well, yesterday I celebrated my first year aboard the Jouett. Needless to say a lot has happened since a year ago and
much of it has been unanticipated.
     I am standing duty Saturday for this buddy of mine and Sunday is my day of duty. So I'll be spending my weekend on the ship.
     I am hoping to go to G.M.'s next weekend but may not make it because there is word out about having to
be aboard Saturday for an inspection of weapons handling proceldure. So I am not sure yet what my plans are.
     Well I had better close here.
     Bill said he is still on mess duty and is expecting R+R in October. His hut was blown over by a typhone (his spelling) and now he is living in a better one.
     Bye for now.

                    your son, Mike

EXTENSIVE TRAINING AND PREPARATION ACCOMPLISHED BY THE SHIP'S PERSONNEL IN THE
FACE OF AN EXTREMELY HOSTILE ENEMY ENVIRONMENT. AFTER ARRIVAL IN THE GULF OF
TONKIN, JOUETT-CONTROLLED CAP WAS CREDITED WITH POSITIVE DESTRUCTION OF ONE MIG
AIRCRAFT AND ONE "PROBABLE" WHILE IN TONKIN GULF, THE SHIP PROVIDED AIR ADVISORY
CONTROL FOR APPROXIMATELY 18,000 STRIKE AIRCRAFT. THROUGHOUT THE SIX MONTH
DEPLOYMENT JOUETT ENJOYED EXCEPTIONAL EQUIPMENT RELIABILITY, FLAWLESS CONDUCT
ASHORE, AND THE ABSENCE OF A SINGLE SERIOUS PERSONNEL CONTRIBUTED IN LARGE
MEASURE TO THE SECURITY OF NAVAL SHIPS IN THE SOUTH CHINA SEA. THE COURAGE,
STAMINA, PROFESSIONALISM, AND DEDICATION DISPLAYED BY THE OFFICERS AND MEN OF
USS JOUETT EARNED THE ADMIRATION AND GRATITUDE OF THE PILOTS AND AIR CREWMEN OF
TASK FORCE SEVENTY-SEVEN AND WERE IN KEEPING WITH THE HIGHEST TRADITIONS OF THE
UNITED STATES NAVAL SERVICE. AS A RESULT OF THIS PERFORMANCE IN SEVENTH FLEET,
JOUETT RECEIVED 35 COMMENDATORY MESSAGES FROM HIGHER AUTHORITY.

FORTY SAR OPERATIONS AND RESCUED EIGHT AVIATORS, THREE FROM ENEMY TERRITORY.
JOUETT-CONTROLLED CAP WAS CREDITED WITH POSITIVE DESTRUCTION OF ONE MIG AND
ONE "PROBABLE" WHILE IN TONKIN GULF. THE SHIP PROVIDED AIR ADVISORY CONTROL
FOR APPROXIMATELY 18,000 STRIKE AIRCRAFT. OVER 900 HELICOPTER EVOLUTIONS,
LANDINGS OR TAKEOFFS, WERE CONDUCTED WITHOUT A SINGLE MISHAP. JOUETT ALSO
PIONEERED IN THE TACTICAL DEVELOPMENT OF THE NTDS CONFIGURED DLG IN A LIMITED
WAR SITUATION. AS A RESULT OF THIS PERFORMANCE IN SEVENTH FLEET, JOUETT
RECEIVED 35 COMMENDATORY MESSAGES FROM HIGHER AUTHORITY.


========================================================================================
NOTES
========================================================================================

Key statistics from the deployment summary:
- 93 days stationed along carrier route over North Vietnam
- 40 SAR operations, 8 aviators rescued (3 from enemy territory)
- 1 confirmed MIG kill + 1 probable (Jouett-controlled CAP)
- ~18,000 strike aircraft provided air advisory control
- 900+ helicopter evolutions without mishap
- 35 commendatory messages from higher authority
- NTDS (Naval Tactical Data System) pioneer in limited war

Awards presented by RADM Sheldon H. Kinney, USN
Remarks by CAPT Arthur T. Emerson, Jr., USN (COMDESRON ONE)
Invocation by LT Albert R. Treibel, CHC, USN

Notable: PC1 Clayton O. Childs received Seventh Fleet Letter of Commendation —
same Childs featured in Vigilance magazine "Father, Son Request Duty Together"
article. FTCS Evan D. Cox and FTMC Robert L. Gaskill (Fire Control Technician
senior rates, Mike's department) received Navy Achievement Medals. FTGC Glenn H.
Underwood received Seventh Fleet Letter of Commendation.

1968-10-20.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-20.text:
Sunday, Oct. 20, 1968
7:00 PM

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     I just got done eating supper and am at the USO now to relax for a few moments and write a few lines. I've been up since 3:20 this morning and am begining to feel the effect. I stood the 4-8 watch aboard the ship and came into town about 9:00 this morning.
     I got out to the stadium about 11:45 AM today for the Chargers game. It started at 1 PM out here and may have been televised back home because I
saw the NBC cameras there. The Chargers beat the Denver Broncos and I believe the score was 55-17. It was a good game and their only home game this month. They had about 40,000 there and the weather was great for it. A Navy band and a drum and bugle corps from the boot camp provided the halftime entertainment. The reason for this was because today starts Navy Week with the Navy birthday next Sunday.
     After the game I came back downtown and went to 5:15 mass. There were quite a few people there too.
     When I finish this I plan on going out to do my laundry then head back to the ship.
     We get underway tomorrow at 0800 for 5 more days of operations then are back in port for a few more weeks. Last weeks exercises were the usual with a lot of confusion and too many mistakes. But that is why we are going out, so we can train
the new people and make the ship ready for another cruise. Sorry to say, but I don't plan on making that trip again.
     Monday morning the captain announced the results of the advancement exams. My name was among the others and I get second-class on December 16th. As a matter of fact I was the only person in gunnery division to pass the test. I was a little surprized that I made it and am glad I did.
     I hope you got the
three boxes I sent home. Last Saturday the express office was closed that day and I had to send them by Greyhound because I wouldn't be able to do it during the week.
     The same day I spent around $120 on things I got at the exchange at the MCRD. I got two sport coats and a new electric razor among them.
     You can expect me to send almost all the rest of my things home around the 9th of November.
     I am sure I'll be up to Georgia Mae's on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of next month. From what information (rumors) I have been able to pick up I may get discharged around the 16th, but I'm sure it won't be much earlier especially not during the first three days of the month. I am sending the pictures on to her tonight with instructions to return them to you.
     I guess I had better close about here. I hope mother and David are doing fine in their
studying and homework and that all else is going good back home. Keep counting the days with me, bye for now.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

P.S.
     If you wrote since we last talked on the phone I'll probably get it in the morning before we leave and will answer when we get back in.
1968-10-20.attribution: Letter, Mike Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-10-27.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-27.text:
Sunday 27 Oct.

Dear Mother, Dad + David,

     Friday evening I received your letter after I got back to the ship. I've got another week behind me and a three day weekend to look forward to this week. Last week was pretty hectic and much the same routine we have at sea.
     We were suppose to be back in about 2 PM Friday but didn't moor until 7:30 that night. The fog was so heavy they had trouble navigating in the harbor so sat it out for a while and when we did start in it was a long affair.
This other FT and myself operate our radar for navigation when we come in to port. We got a "well done" from one of the officers because of the job we did on tracking contacts in the fog on our way in.
     I have duty today and its about 9 AM here. I suppose I'll watch the football game around 10.
     Last night I went to the arena and saw a hockey game. San Diego won and it was a good one. I am going again Tuesday night when they play Seattle.
     Yesterday I spent some more money as I have been doing on Saturdays for the past couple of weeks. I have got about all of the clothes I want and about all I need to get now are a few uniform accessories like rating badges and a neckerchief.
     I have enough things to send another box home now and may send it sometime this week or next.
     I am almost certain I'll be home anywhere from the 15th to 18th. Of course I don't know for sure but this
seems to be the procedure they are following. So I have less than three weeks left and only two weeks to get ready because that last week I want to have it done.
     We are not due to get underway again until Nov. 19th but there is rumor out that the captain has voluntered us to run plane guard for one of the carriers the week of the 4th. We should find out for sure about that this week. Believe me the things that happen here on this ship really do
make a lot of people mad. There were really a lot of angry wifes and families Friday night after being 5½ hours late. And the week before that, we were going to moor at pier 6. All the people were there waiting for the ship and as the ship neared the pier we backed down and went all the way down to pier 2. Again there were some angry people. The reason for this stunt they say is that the water wasn't deep enough at pier 6 so we had to moor at pier 2. All I can say is, in three weeks it will be over
with (I hope).
     I'm glad to hear about the job promotion for Dad, hope he likes it. No doubt this may be a little incentive to trade for a new car. I was reading in those clippings about the carpenters picketing at the hospital because of a dispute over some doors. I bet there is a good story behind that one. Also I noticed the write-up about the Chicago Bears possibly coming to town. All I can say is it will never happen. What do they plan on doing, build a 30,000 seat stadium then
charge $10 a head to see it. Maybe they could arrange to play on MacArthur's football field and give the proceeds to the school board as an act of charity. The whole idea sounds ridiculous.
     Of course, if all goes well, I'll spend this coming weekend at Georgia Mae's. This should be the last weekend I have up there and I will be sending some things home from there.
     Well its about time for the football game to start so I had better go here. David, be good and study hard in
school. See you soon.

                    your son,

                         Mike
1968-10-27.attribution: Letter, Mike Ducy — Ducy Family Archives

1968-10-30.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-30.text:
Oct. 30, 1968
Wednesday, 1620

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     Only one more day is left in this month then it is November. This has been a slow month for me but I am sure those first two weeks of next month will go by fast.
     This morning I received your letter of the 26th. The pictures were good and the newspaper clipping was informative as usual.
     I also got a letter from Bill today that he wrote the 18th. He typed it and made very few errors with the exception of his spell-
ing which seems to be a trademark of his. But it was very neat and I was glad to see that he has the incentive to type.
     I'll be calling Georgia Mae around 7:30 PM tonight and see if I can visit them this weekend. I am ready for a few days away from here and really do look forward to going up there.
     Last night one of the other FT's and I went out to the arena and saw the Gulls play hockey. It was a pretty rough and wild game but ended in a 2-2 tie.
     Although I don't have duty tonight I plan on staying aboard instead of going into town. I seem to have been caught a little short on finances this week after my shopping spree of Saturday. I will probably go over on the base to the movie about 8:30 to occupy the rest of the evening.
     I was sorry to hear about David hurting his leg. I hope it hasn't became too serious and isn't bothering him now. No doubt he is anxious for tomorrow night to get here so he can go
trick-or-treating.
     I hope you can sign me up for that test and that I'll be able to take it when I get home. It sounds like a good job and I'd like the opportunity to give it a try.
     We had a little rain late last night while I was returning to the ship. This is no doubt a sign that winter isn't too far away. But I doubt if there will be the rain like we had last winter. Of course now that we are back on standard time it really does seem like winter is near.
     Monday I went
through a physical exam to see if I am healthy enough to get out of here and be turned loose as a civilian. This is one of the many steps you have to go through to get your freedom but is usually where they start. As I think of it thats one of the first things they do when they bring you in this outfit. So I guess it works both ways. In case you are wondering about my foot I am glad to say that it has healed completely and isn't causing me a bit of trouble. The corpsman didn't ask to look at it
but did ask me how it was so I told him and he seemed convinced.
     Well I guess I'll close here and write to Bill. Bye for now. Hope to see you soon.

                    Your son,

                         Mike
